title: Accessibility conformance (WCAG 2.2 AA)
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` has been binding since Sprint 01: every screen ticket carries an `a11y` label, every design ticket carries a CVD sign-off gate, and axe-core has been advisory in CI since R0. What has *not* happened is a single, end-to-end, evidenced conformance pass over the built product. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.1 goal 2 makes that an R5 objective — "Reach and evidence **WCAG 2.2 AA** conformance across every screen, including the chart surfaces and the node editor" — and §9.3 exit criterion 2 states the evidence standard: "WCAG 2.2 AA conformance evidenced per screen: axe-core clean, manual screen-reader pass signed off, conformance report published. Any non-conformance is a documented, Owner-accepted exception with a remediation ticket."

§9.2 scopes **E47** (42 pts, S23–S25) as: full WCAG 2.2 AA audit of every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md`; remediation of every finding; high-contrast and colour-blind-safe themes verified against all order-flow encodings; screen-reader scripts for the chart data cursor, footprint inspection, DOM ladder and both rule editors; reduced-motion coverage; focus-order and focus-visibility audit; a published accessibility conformance report (VPAT-shaped).

This Epic is therefore **not** "add accessibility" — it is "prove it, and fix what the proof exposes". The hard parts are pre-identified by `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6: the WebGL surfaces (chart, footprint grid, DOM/heatmap, profiles) are opaque to assistive technology and depend on the three-layer strategy (offscreen DOM mirror, throttled live regions, data-table alternative **SCR-045**) shipped incrementally across E11/E18/E21. R5 is where those three layers get tested together, at real tick rates, by a real screen reader, against a pinned SR matrix (§8.1).

The descoping ladder (`30-release-roadmap.md` §12) marks **"A11y Level A conformance"** as *never cut* — a Level A regression blocks the GA gate outright. AA findings may become Owner-accepted, expiring exceptions; Level A findings may not.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories covering the SET-domain accessibility surface: **US-SET-007** (accessibility preferences, Must), **US-SET-004** (themes/density contrast under every theme, Must), **US-SET-005** (CVD-safe palettes and the no-hue-alone rule, Must), **US-SET-001** (settings keyboard operability and persistent labels, Must), **US-SET-002** (single global hotkey layer, conflict and reserved-key rules, Must), **US-SET-003** (keyboard-operable destructive-confirm policy incl. hold-to-confirm fallback, Must), plus **US-CHART-014** (data-table alternative) as the canvas escape hatch this Epic verifies.
- Screens audited and remediated: all of `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001 … SCR-159, with deep passes on **SCR-030** (chart panel), **SCR-045** (data-table alternative), **SCR-032** (footprint settings/inspection), **SCR-050** (heatmap + DOM ladder), **SCR-052/053** (CVD, tape), **SCR-081**/**SCR-082** (rule form and node-graph editors), **SCR-060/061/076** (order ticket and confirms), **SCR-113** (hotkey editor), **SCR-116** (appearance & density), **SCR-117** (accessibility settings), **SCR-135** (audit log), **SCR-143** (system health).
- Components: the design-system a11y contract in `15-component-catalogue.md` §11 re-verified for CMP-001…CMP-238, with concrete remediation of the trading-specific set (CMP-113 HeatmapCell, CMP-136 DomLadderRow, CMP-158 OrderConfirmSummary, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-211/212 confirm/toast surfaces, CMP-228 PreviewTile, chart primitives CMP-180…CMP-199, rule nodes CMP-140…CMP-159).
- API: `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings` and `GET /api/v1/me/preferences` carry the accessibility preference block; `GET /api/v1/me/hotkeys` supplies the resolved bindings the cheatsheet and remap conflict rules read.
- Tables: `settings` (`21-database-schema.md` §, JSONB preference document) — accessibility preferences are a scoped key set, no new table.
- CI: axe-core, Lighthouse ≥95, contrast-token linter, keyboard-only E2E, motion/flash audit, and accessibility-tree snapshot promoted from advisory to **required checks** per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §9.
- Evidence: per-screen conformance matrix, executed SR scripts against the pinned matrix (§8.1), and a published VPAT-shaped conformance report plus an in-app accessibility statement linked from **SCR-117** and **SCR-119**.

## Out of scope
- Mobile/Android screen readers and Safari-direct testing — excluded by locked decision and `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1.
- Rewriting any feature's information architecture to "simplify for accessibility"; density is solved by alternatives (SCR-045) and IA, not by removing trading functionality (§1).
- Performance optimisation as such — **E46 Performance hardening**; this Epic only asserts that a11y machinery (DOM mirror, live regions) stays inside its own frame budget and files E46 tickets otherwise.
- General design-QA/token/copy sweep and bug burn-down — **E49**, which this Epic feeds and which depends on it (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1: `E47 --> E49`).
- Localisation/RTL — not in the v1 product scope.
- AAA conformance beyond the two named stretch targets (§5.3 critical-state contrast, no timing limits).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every screen has evidence, not an assertion
  Given the conformance matrix covers SCR-001 through SCR-159
  When the R5 GA gate is evaluated
  Then each screen row carries an axe-core result, a keyboard-path result, a screen-reader pass or
    deferral reason, and a named sign-off from the Accessibility role
  And no row is blank or marked "assumed compliant"

Scenario: Canvas surfaces are usable without sight
  Given NVDA on the pinned Windows/Electron combination
  When the tester follows the §8.2 task script on chart, footprint, DOM ladder and both rule editors
  Then every task completes using keyboard and screen reader alone
  And no task requires a mouse, hover or drag

Scenario: A Level A regression blocks GA
  Given a PR introduces a keyboard trap on any in-scope screen
  When CI runs
  Then the keyboard-only E2E gate fails and the merge queue rejects the PR
  And the failure names the screen and the trapped control

Scenario: An AA finding may be accepted, but never silently
  Given a finding cannot be remediated within R5
  When it is closed
  Then it exists in the exception register with a WCAG SC reference, a compensating control,
    a named Owner acceptance, an expiry date, and a linked remediation ticket
  And it is reproduced verbatim in the published conformance report

Scenario: Accessibility does not regress after GA
  Given the axe, Lighthouse, contrast-linter, keyboard-E2E, motion-audit and a11y-tree-snapshot gates are required checks
  When any of them fails on main
  Then the branch protection blocks merge and an alert is raised to the frontend on-call
```

## Technical notes / design
Three work streams run in parallel and converge on one register. (1) **Instrumented sweep** — automated audit across every route/panel state, producing a machine-readable findings file that becomes the backlog for the remediation stories. (2) **Human sweep** — SR scripts and keyboard-only task runs on the surfaces automation cannot judge (announcement quality, focus intent, mirror/canvas correspondence). (3) **Gate hardening** — turning the advisory checks into required checks so R5's result cannot silently erode. Remediation is deliberately grouped by *pattern* (canvas surrogate, roving-tabindex grid, dialog/focus-return, motion token, colour-encoding) rather than by screen, because the same defect repeats across many screens and a per-screen ticket structure would produce hundreds of duplicates.

## Test plan
Automated: axe-core per screen state, Lighthouse a11y, contrast-token matrix, keyboard-only Playwright suite, motion/flash luminance analysis, accessibility-tree snapshot diffs. Manual: pinned SR matrix (NVDA P0, JAWS P1, VoiceOver P1 before GA) executing the §8.2 task script; 200% zoom and 400% reflow checks; CVD simulation of every order-flow encoding. Regression: the whole suite runs on the release candidate, and results are attached to the GA PRR.

## Security notes
The DOM mirror and live regions expose account, position and order data as text; they are rendered inside the same authenticated surface and must obey the same RBAC filtering as the visual surface, never a broader dataset (an offscreen mirror that renders all accounts while the canvas renders one would be an authorisation leak). Accessibility preferences are per-user settings and must not be writable cross-user. The published conformance report and the in-app statement must contain no hostnames, account identifiers or screenshots with live data.

## Accessibility notes
This Epic *is* the accessibility note. Conformance target: WCAG 2.2 Level AA across `12-sitemap.md`, with the §5.3 AAA stretch targets for buy/sell and LIVE/DEMO chrome. WCAG 2.2-specific criteria explicitly audited: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size, 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication.

## Performance notes
The DOM mirror is windowed and must not materialise more than the visible unit set; live-region updates are throttled per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2 (default 1 update / 2 s per ambient field). Enabling every accessibility preference simultaneously must not cost more than 1 ms per frame on the reference machine, measured with the E46 harness; any excess is an E46 ticket, not an accepted regression.

## Observability
`a11y.preference_changed{key,value}` analytics (already specified on SCR-117); CI dashboards for axe violation count, Lighthouse a11y score and keyboard-E2E pass rate per screen; a build-over-build trend so erosion is visible before it becomes a release blocker.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Conformance matrix complete for SCR-001…SCR-159 with named sign-offs.
- [ ] Manual SR passes executed on the pinned matrix; NVDA and VoiceOver full passes signed off before GA.
- [ ] All six CI gates are required checks on `main`.
- [ ] Zero open Level A findings; every open AA finding is a registered, expiring, Owner-accepted exception with a remediation ticket.
- [ ] Conformance report published and the in-app accessibility statement linked from SCR-117 and SCR-119.
- [ ] `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md` and `15-component-catalogue.md` reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] Demoed to Owner (keyboard-only + screen-reader walkthrough) with acceptance recorded.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E44** (live-enablement gating and environment separation — the LIVE/DEMO chrome and its non-colour-only badge are part of the audited surface, per `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 `E44 --> E47`). Blocks **E49** (`E47 --> E49`): the design-QA sweep consumes this Epic's findings register. Consumes the a11y machinery built in E05 (design system), E10 (app shell), E11/E18/E21 (canvas surrogates), E36/E37 (rule editors).

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-conformance`

## References
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (whole document, normative); `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.1–§9.4, §11.1, §12; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §27 SET; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §11; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`.

```mermaid
graph TD
  K01[E47-K01 Spike: audit method & SR harness] --> T01[E47-T01 Full WCAG 2.2 AA sweep & findings register]
  K01 --> T04[E47-T04 SR scripts & pinned-matrix harness]
  T01 --> S01[E47-S01 Chart canvas surrogate & data cursor]
  T01 --> S02[E47-S02 Footprint, DOM ladder & heatmap]
  T01 --> S03[E47-S03 Rule form & node-graph editors]
  T01 --> S05[E47-S05 Focus order, target size, drag alternatives]
  T02[E47-T02 CI gate hardening] --> T01
  T03[E47-T03 Contrast & CVD token matrix] --> S06[E47-S06 High-contrast & CVD-safe themes]
  T03 --> T02
  S07[E47-S07 Accessibility settings SCR-117] --> S04[E47-S04 Reduced motion & flash coverage]
  S01 --> T04
  S02 --> T04
  S03 --> T04
  S04 --> T05[E47-T05 Conformance report & exception register]
  S05 --> T05
  S06 --> T05
  T04 --> T05
```

## Agent guidance

Multiple agents will work E47's children in parallel. To pick the next ticket:

1. Respect `blocked_by` on each child ticket — do not start a ticket whose blockers are not yet Done.
2. Prefer the epic's own dependency graph (see `## Child dependency graph` / `## Children — dependency graph` section above) over guessing from titles.
3. Design (`-D0x`) and Spike (`-K0x`) tickets generally gate their dependent Story/Task tickets — pick those first if unblocked.
4. QA (`-Q0x`) and Security (`-X0x`) tickets are epic-closing; they depend on most Task/Story work and should be picked last.
5. Two agents must not take tickets that both modify the same non-generated file; check open PRs/branches for path overlap before starting.
6. Shared interfaces to agree before parallel work starts: any WS/REST contract change, any shared machine.json under `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/machines/`, and any shared design-system token — post in the ticket comments before changing.

title: UX research: keyboard-only and screen-reader trading baseline study
body:
## Context
E47 is the epic that turns the promises in `05-accessibility-standard.md` into a verified WCAG 2.2 AA conformance claim across every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md`. Everything else in this epic — theme work, focus-order work, canvas surrogates, announcement scripts — is remediation of an *existing* product surface. Remediating blind is the single biggest waste risk on the epic: a designer can satisfy the letter of a success criterion (`aria-label` present, contrast ≥4.5:1) and still ship a surface a keyboard-only trader cannot actually trade on within a realistic time budget.

`05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 states the bar explicitly: AA is adopted not for legal reasons but because (a) the Owner may develop RSI/motor or vision conditions over the tool's lifetime and (b) keyboard-first operation is a *speed* requirement — mouse-only trading is a latency risk. That framing makes this a usability study, not a compliance checkbox exercise. We need timed, observed evidence of where keyboard-only and screen-reader operation currently breaks down before we spend design capacity on fixes.

This ticket runs ≥5 sprints ahead of the consuming FE remediation stories (Sprint 23–26) so its findings can shape D02's audit priorities and D03–D09's specs rather than arrive as post-hoc justification.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Participants**: the Owner, up to 2 account managers, plus 2 external assistive-technology-expert participants (one NVDA daily driver, one keyboard-only/low-vision participant) recruited through the accessibility role's network. 60-minute moderated remote sessions.
- **Surfaces studied** (highest-density, highest-stakes first): SCR-030 chart panel + SCR-045 chart data-table alternative, SCR-060-band DOM ladder, the order ticket, SCR-116 appearance settings, SCR-117 accessibility settings, SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet, SCR-012 command palette, and both rule editors (form editor and node-graph editor).
- **Task script** derived from `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2 item 3, run keyboard-only against the R4 build: switch symbol via watchlist search; read the last 5 bars' OHLCV + delta via the DOM mirror and independently via `Alt+T` (SCR-045) and compare data parity; inspect one footprint bar's price levels; place and cancel a limit order; read the top 10 DOM levels; open and change one accessibility preference (US-SET-007); find the binding for "flatten" via the cheatsheet.
- **Measures per task**: completion (yes/no/with-help), time-to-complete vs a mouse-using control run, number of "lost focus" events, number of times the participant asked "where am I?", verbatim quotes on announcement flooding.
- **Deliverables**: (1) a findings report at `docs/research/a11y/47-keyboard-sr-baseline.md` with a severity-ranked defect list mapped to WCAG 2.2 SC numbers and screen IDs; (2) a one-page "top 10 things that must change" summary consumed by E47-D02; (3) session recordings and transcripts stored per the research retention policy; (4) a proposed **announcement-verbosity default** recommendation (feeds US-SET-007 and E47-D07) backed by the observed flooding data.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design, wireframe or token work — that is E47-D02/D03 onward.
- Mobile/Android screen readers (locked out of scope).
- Safari or non-Electron browser targets (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1 excludes them; Chromium headless is a CI-only surface).
- Remediating anything found — findings become tickets, not fixes, inside this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Study executed against the real build
  Given the R4 Electron production build is installed on the test rig with NVDA 2024.x pinned
  When all 5 participant sessions have been run against the fixed task script
  Then each task has a recorded completion verdict, elapsed time and focus-loss count
  And no session substituted a prototype or Figma flow for the real build

Scenario: Findings are actionable and traceable
  When the findings report is published
  Then every finding names the screen ID (SCR-nnn), the component ID (CMP-nnn) where applicable, and the WCAG 2.2 success criterion it violates
  And every finding carries a severity of blocker / major / minor using the §8.2 item 5 bar (a task that cannot be completed keyboard+SR-only is a blocker)

Scenario: Announcement flooding is quantified, not guessed
  Given a participant observes the chart with live ticks on a fast-moving symbol
  When ambient announcements are measured over a 2-minute window at default verbosity
  Then the report states announcements-per-minute and the participant's subjective usability rating
  And a recommended default throttle cadence is stated with the evidence that supports it

Scenario: Participant cannot complete a task (failure path)
  Given a participant becomes stuck or trapped on a surface
  When the moderator ends the task after the 5-minute ceiling
  Then the task is recorded as a blocker finding with the exact keystroke sequence that produced the trap
  And the moderator does not coach the participant to a workaround before recording the failure

Scenario: No trading risk introduced by the study
  Given the study involves placing and cancelling orders
  When any order task is run
  Then it is run exclusively against the Bybit demo environment with the Live gate off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Run against the Electron production build (the only shipped surface per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1), NVDA 2024.x pinned, Windows 11 23H2, default hotkey map, default dark theme, default verbosity — a deliberately un-tuned baseline so findings represent what a new user meets.
- Use a second machine for screen+audio capture so the SR audio is on the recording; NVDA speech-viewer logs are captured to text for the flooding count (avoids hand-counting from audio).
- Control run: the same task script performed by a mouse-using participant, to produce the time ratio. A ratio >3× on a core trading task is itself reported as a finding even where the task technically completes.
- The external participants must be briefed that this is a private internal tool; NDA per the standard research consent pack.

## Test plan
- Pilot session with an internal frontend a11y champion before participant 1 to validate the script length and the capture rig; pilot data is excluded from findings.
- Peer review of the findings report by the Accessibility role and one QA/SDET before publication; QA checks that each blocker finding is reproducible from the written keystroke sequence.
- Spot-reproduce 3 randomly chosen findings independently; any that do not reproduce are demoted or removed with a note.

## Security notes
- Sessions run on demo accounts only; no live API keys present on the test rig. Recordings may show account identifiers and balances — store in the restricted research bucket, not the general docs tree, and redact account IDs from the published report.
- External participants see product screens under NDA; do not expose the admin/users screen with real manager identities — use seeded fixture users.

## Accessibility notes
- The research artefacts themselves meet the standard: the report is structured markdown with real headings and tables (no screenshot-only findings), every screenshot carries a text description, and the summary is readable without colour.
- Participant accommodations: participants choose their own AT, verbosity and speech rate; sessions offer breaks every 20 minutes; no timed pressure beyond the documented 5-minute per-task ceiling, which is a moderator-side measurement bound, not a participant-facing timer.

## Performance notes
- Announcement cadence and focus-change latency are recorded as perceived-performance data: if a focus move into the DOM mirror takes >200 ms to be announced, that is logged as a finding and forwarded to E46 performance hardening, because a mirror that lags the canvas is an a11y defect, not only a perf one.

## Observability
- Emit nothing new from the product for this ticket. The study's own telemetry is the NVDA speech log plus moderator notes.
- Findings counts by severity are recorded on the E47 epic as the baseline the epic burns down against, so progress is measurable at the epic level.

## Definition of Done
- Findings report merged at `docs/research/a11y/47-keyboard-sr-baseline.md`, peer-reviewed by the Accessibility role.
- Top-10 summary attached to this ticket and linked from E47-D02.
- Every blocker finding has a corresponding follow-up ticket or is explicitly folded into a named E47 design ticket's scope.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment on this ticket; Status moves to Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs.
- Recordings stored and access-restricted; consent forms filed.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E44` — the study must run against a build with the Live-enablement gating in place so the Demo/Live switch task is realistic.
- Feeds E47-D02 (audit), E47-D03 (themes), E47-D07 (announcement scripts).

## Branch
`design/e47-a11y-baseline-research`

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §1, §3, §6, §8.2
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-007, US-SET-004, US-CHART-014
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-012, SCR-013, SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-116, SCR-117
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3 (design-ready gates)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11 (E44 → E47)

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e47-a11y-baseline-research`
- PR title: "E47-D01: UX research: keyboard-only and screen-reader trading baseline study"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-D01>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/design, area/design-system, priority/p1, design, ux-research, a11y

**Done means**
- See ## Definition of Done above.

**Do NOT**
- Any visual design, wireframe or token work — that is E47-D02/D03 onward.
- Mobile/Android screen readers (locked out of scope).
- Safari or non-Electron browser targets (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1 excludes them; Chromium headless is a CI-only surface).
- Remediating anything found — findings become tickets, not fixes, inside this ticket.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-D01` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Accessibility design audit of all screens: annotated findings catalogue
body:
## Context
E47's remediation stories (Sprint 23–26) need a single, exhaustive, prioritised list of what is wrong, per screen, before any of them can be estimated or scheduled. Without it the epic degenerates into whack-a-mole against axe-core output — which catches roughly a third of real WCAG failures and none of the ones that matter most here (canvas opacity, focus order in a 6-panel workspace, announcement flooding, colour-only encoding of side).

This ticket produces the **audit of record**: every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md` walked against `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3–§7 and WCAG 2.2 AA, with each finding annotated directly on the design source (Figma frame comment + catalogue entry) and mirrored into a machine-readable register the engineering chunk turns into stories. It absorbs E47-D01's observed findings so research evidence and expert review land in one list.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Coverage**: all screen bands — SCR-001..019 (auth, shell, chrome, onboarding), SCR-020..029 (workspace/layout), SCR-030..049 (charting incl. SCR-045 table alternative, SCR-047 empty, SCR-048 error), SCR-050..099 (order-flow, DOM, trading, positions, rules, journal), SCR-100..119 (watchlist, settings incl. SCR-116/117/118/119), SCR-120..139 (admin). Every screen gets a verdict, including "no findings".
- **Per-screen audit record**: screen ID, its design sign-off checklist state, findings list, each finding with `{id, wcag_sc, level, severity, surface (canvas|chrome|both), evidence, proposed remedy, owning design ticket}`.
- **Check dimensions per screen** (from the standard): keyboard reachability and no-trap (§3.1), focus order and landmark model (§3.4), colour-independence of side/state (§4), dark + light + high-contrast contrast ratios (§5), canvas surrogate/live-region/table-alternative presence (§6), reduced-motion behaviour and flash rate (§7), target size ≥24 px, visible-label-not-placeholder, error identification in plain language.
- **Machine-readable register** at `docs/plan/a11y/47-audit-register.json` (array of the finding objects above) so E47's engineering and QA chunks can generate stories and test cases from it without re-reading prose.
- **Heat map view**: a one-page summary ranking screens by blocker count, used to order the Sprint 23–26 remediation sequence.
- **Routing**: every finding assigned to exactly one of E47-D03 (themes/contrast), D04 (focus), D05 (SCR-117), D06 (canvas surrogate + tables), D07 (announcements), D08 (motion), D09 (hotkeys/cheatsheet/palette), D10 (design-system primitives) — or flagged `engineering-only` where no design change is needed.

## Out of scope
- Producing the fixes themselves (that is D03–D10 and the engineering chunk).
- Auditing backend-only surfaces, API payloads, or CLI/ops tooling.
- Re-auditing after fixes — that is E47-D12 design QA.
- Level AAA criteria beyond the two the standard adopts explicitly (non-text contrast 7:1 for buy/sell where feasible, reduced motion).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued screen has a verdict
  Given 14-screens-catalogue.md enumerates the SCR-001..139 bands
  When the audit register is published
  Then every screen ID in the catalogue appears exactly once in the register
  And screens with no findings carry an explicit "no findings" record with the auditor and date, not an absent entry

Scenario: Findings are routed, not orphaned
  When a finding is recorded
  Then it names exactly one owning design ticket key or is marked engineering-only with a one-line reason
  And no finding is left with an empty owner

Scenario: Research findings are absorbed
  Given E47-D01 produced blocker findings from observed sessions
  When the register is published
  Then every D01 blocker appears in the register with its research evidence linked
  And any D01 blocker the auditors judge non-reproducible is recorded as such with the reason, never silently dropped

Scenario: Canvas surfaces are not waived (edge case)
  Given a screen renders its primary data to a WebGL canvas
  When it is audited
  Then it is checked against all four layers of the canvas strategy (DOM mirror, live regions, table alternative, canvas role/label)
  And a missing layer is a blocker finding, not an accepted exclusion

Scenario: Contrast is measured, not eyeballed
  When a colour pair is recorded as passing
  Then the register stores the computed ratio and the token pair names
  And any pair below the applicable threshold is a finding regardless of visual impression
```

## Technical notes / design
- Two-pass method: (1) **static pass** against the design source (Figma frames + catalogue entries + `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens) using the contrast linter from `05-accessibility-standard.md` §9.3; (2) **live pass** against the running R4 build with axe-core DevTools, keyboard-only traversal and a 60-second NVDA spot-read per screen.

- Severity bar matches `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2 item 5: task-blocking keyboard+SR-only = blocker (P0); awkward-but-completable = major/minor.
- The register schema is versioned in the file (`"schema": 1`) so the QA chunk's generator can fail loudly on shape drift.

- Validate the register JSON parses and every `owning_ticket` value resolves to a real E47 ticket key.
- Cross-check a random 10% of "no findings" verdicts by a third reviewer.

## Security notes

title: High-contrast and colour-vision-safe theme design (SCR-116)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer encodes an enormous amount of meaning in hue: bid green / ask red (owner decision OD#10), delta sign, imbalance flags, heatmap intensity, CVD direction, bubble side, environment (Demo/Live), P&L sign, order side on the ticket and on chart overlays. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §4 forbids colour-only encoding outright and §5 sets contrast minimums that the dark theme in particular has to be measured against, including for *data ink* on canvas — not just text.

US-SET-004 and US-SET-005 already promise light, dark, high-contrast and CVD-safe palettes (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) with a live preview (SCR-116), and an automated check asserting that no view depends on hue alone. This ticket designs the palettes and the non-colour encodings that make that claim true across *every* order-flow surface, and hands the design-system team a tested token set.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Palettes**: `theme.dark` (baseline, re-validated), `theme.light`, `theme.high-contrast`, `theme.cvd.deuteranopia`, `theme.cvd.protanopia`, `theme.cvd.tritanopia` — each a complete token set covering UI chrome, text, borders, focus ring, and the **chart data-ink ramp** (candle up/down, bid/ask, delta positive/negative, heatmap intensity ramp, profile POC/VA/HVN/LVN, CVD line, bubble fill, liquidation flash).
- **Non-colour encodings** designed once and applied everywhere: `B`/`A` glyph prefixes for bid/ask cells, explicit `+`/`−` signs for every delta and P&L value, pattern/hatch for imbalance-flagged cells, shape differentiation for buy vs sell markers on chart and DOM, icon+text for the Demo/Live environment badge (CMP-074 EnvBanner), text labels in every legend (CMP-037 SwatchLegendItem).
- **Contrast evidence sheet**: computed ratios for every token pair per theme against the applicable threshold (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text/UI, and the 7:1 target the standard adopts for critical buy/sell state where feasible), produced by the §9.3 token linter, not by hand.
- **SCR-116 hi-fi**: theme + accent + chart palette + density + font-scale (100/112/125/150 %) + grid-line intensity + the live preview tile (CMP-228 PreviewTile) showing a real footprint cell, a ladder row and a positions row under the current choice; plus the sub-4.5:1 custom-palette warning state named in the catalogue entry.
- **Simulation proofs**: every order-flow surface (footprint, heatmap, profile, CVD, bubbles, DOM) rendered under each CVD simulation and under greyscale, attached as the evidence pack.
- **Token contribution**: a PR-ready token diff for the design-system package (`16-design-system-brief.md` naming), with the light/dark/high-contrast/CVD variants expressed as one schema, not four forks.

## Out of scope
- Implementation of theme switching (engineering chunk; the CSS-custom-property swap contract is already stated in the SCR-116 catalogue entry).
- Per-user custom palette authoring UI beyond the accent/chart-palette controls already catalogued.
- Motion and reduced-motion tokens (E47-D08).
- Focus-ring geometry (E47-D04 owns it; this ticket only supplies its colour per theme).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every theme passes its contrast thresholds
  Given the six palettes are complete
  When the token contrast linter runs over every text, UI-component and data-ink pair
  Then no pair falls below its applicable WCAG 2.2 AA threshold
  And the evidence sheet records the computed ratio for every pair, including canvas data-ink against the canvas background

Scenario: No surface relies on hue alone
  Given an order-flow surface encodes side, sign or state
  When it is rendered in greyscale
  Then side, sign and flagged state remain distinguishable through glyph, sign, shape or pattern
  And the legend for that surface states the encoding in text

Scenario: CVD-safe palettes preserve meaning
  Given the deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia palettes
  When each order-flow surface is rendered under the matching simulation
  Then bid versus ask and positive versus negative delta remain distinguishable at a normal viewing distance
  And the design records which pairs required an additional non-colour cue to achieve that

Scenario: Custom palette below threshold (failure path)
  Given a user selects a custom accent that yields a text contrast of 3.9:1
  When the selection is made in SCR-116
  Then a warning is shown stating the combination fails contrast and text may be hard to read
  And the warning is announced via a polite live region, not shown as a colour change alone

Scenario: Live accent is never the only environment signal (edge case)
  Given the Live environment accent is applied
  When the high-contrast theme is active and the accent hue collapses toward the foreground
  Then the environment remains identifiable through the badge icon and the word "LIVE"
  And the design states this explicitly on CMP-074
```

## Technical notes / design
- Themes are one schema with variant values (`--cv-color-*`), so a new theme cannot silently omit a token; the linter fails on a missing key rather than falling back to dark.
- Data-ink contrast is measured against the actual canvas background per theme, including the grid-line layer, because the effective background behind a candle wick is not the page background.
- The high-contrast theme increases border weight and focus-ring thickness as well as contrast — contrast alone does not solve dense-grid legibility; grid separation is structural.
- CVD palettes are built from a colour-blind-safe base (blue/orange family) rather than by desaturating green/red, which merely makes both unreadable.
- Heatmap intensity ramps are checked for perceptual uniformity so that "twice as bright" reads as "more size" monotonically in every theme; ramps that invert perceived order under simulation are rejected.

## Test plan
- Automated: token contrast linter over all six palettes in the design-system package CI (§9.3) — merge-blocking.
- Visual: greyscale and three CVD simulations applied to a fixed screenshot set (footprint, heatmap, profile, CVD pane, DOM, positions grid, order ticket) and reviewed by two designers plus the Accessibility role.
- Usability spot-check: the Owner and one manager confirm the CVD-safe palettes remain *tradeable*, not merely compliant — a palette that passes but slows recognition is rejected and reworked.
- Hand-off check: the token diff builds in the design-system package without unresolved references.

## Security notes
- No secrets or PII involved. One indirect concern: the Demo/Live distinction is a safety control, and a theme that weakens its salience is a safety regression — any theme variant is reviewed against the environment-badge legibility case before sign-off, with the Security engineer notified if a variant reduces it.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket *is* an accessibility deliverable; the acceptance bar is the evidence sheet, not a designer's judgement.
- 200% zoom and 125/150% font scale are checked on SCR-116 itself, per its catalogue sign-off checklist.
- Colour is never the sole differentiator in the palette *pickers* either: each swatch carries a name and the chip shows a check glyph when selected, not only a coloured ring.

## Performance notes
- Theme changes must remain a CSS custom-property swap applied within one frame with no panel remount and no GL-context loss (SCR-116 catalogue statement); the token structure is designed so the canvas layer reads palette values from a single uniform block that can be re-uploaded in one call rather than per-primitive.

## Observability
- `appearance.theme_changed`, `appearance.chart_palette_changed`, `appearance.font_size_changed` analytics events already exist in the catalogue; the design confirms the CVD palette identifier is included in the payload so adoption of accommodations is measurable (aggregated, per SCR-117's stated analytics intent).

## Definition of Done
- Six complete palettes plus non-colour encoding spec published in Figma and mirrored into `16-design-system-brief.md`.
- Contrast evidence sheet attached; linter green over all palettes.
- Simulation proof pack attached for every order-flow surface.
- SCR-116 hi-fi complete against its catalogue sign-off checklist, including the failing-contrast warning state.
- Token diff accepted by the design-system team (E47-D10 consumes it).
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs the evidence sheet.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E47-D02` (audit routes the colour findings here).
- Feeds E47-D10 (design-system contribution) and the Sprint 23–26 FE theme remediation stories.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-004, US-SET-005
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-116, SCR-117

title: Focus order, focus visibility and landmark model spec
body:
## Context
A CandleViewer workspace is six or more simultaneously-live panels (chart, DOM, order ticket, positions, watchlist, journal) inside an Electron window, any of which can be re-arranged by the user. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.4 says dense layouts are solved by information architecture, not by exempting screens — which means the focus model has to be *designed*, once, and then obeyed by every panel, rather than emerging from DOM order.

E47-D02's audit will produce a large cluster of findings in exactly this area: focus that escapes into hidden panels, focus lost when a panel re-renders on a data update, focus rings invisible against the dark canvas, modal dialogs that do not restore focus, and no reliable way to move between regions without tabbing through hundreds of ladder rows. This ticket designs the answer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Landmark/region model**: the named region set for the app shell (banner, nav rail, workspace, each panel as a labelled region, status bar), the heading hierarchy rule (one `h1` per screen, nested panel headings, no skipped levels), and the region-cycling contract behind `Ctrl+\` (§3.2) including wrap-around and the announcement made on each move.
- **Focus-order spec per screen archetype**: workspace (SCR-020 band), full-page form (settings SCR-110..119, admin SCR-120..129), modal dialog (CMP-043/CMP-044), overlay/palette (SCR-012, SCR-013), dense grid (DOM ladder, positions grid, SCR-045 table).
- **Escape-hatch rule for dense grids**: a grid is a single tab stop; arrow keys move within it (roving tabindex), `Esc` leaves it, and the grid announces its extent on entry ("DOM ladder, 200 levels, focused best bid"). This is what prevents the ladder from swallowing keyboard navigation.
- **Focus-visibility spec**: ring geometry, minimum 3:1 contrast against *every* adjacent surface including the WebGL canvas and the heatmap's brightest cell, the high-visibility variant promised by US-SET-007, and the shared utility contract for canvas-adjacent surrogate elements (CMP-039 FocusRing).
- **Focus-retention rules under live data**: focus must never be stolen or dropped when a panel re-renders, a position closes, a rule fires, or a WS reconnect re-seeds a panel; the spec states, per event class, where focus goes and what is announced.
- **Dialog/overlay contract**: focus trap while open, initial focus target per dialog type, focus restoration to the invoking control on close, and the `Esc` universal-cancel behaviour from §3.2.
- **Annotated redlines** applied to the affected catalogue entries and Figma frames.

## Out of scope
- Hotkey assignments and the cheatsheet (E47-D09).
- Announcement content and verbosity (E47-D07); this ticket specifies only *that* a focus move is announced and with what label, not the ambient narration policy.
- The DOM mirror's data model (E47-D06).
- Implementation (engineering chunk).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every archetype has a defined focus order
  Given the five screen archetypes
  When the spec is published
  Then each archetype states its tab sequence, its roving-tabindex zones, its entry and exit keys, and its initial focus target
  And every screen in 14-screens-catalogue.md is mapped to exactly one archetype

Scenario: Focus ring is visible on the hardest background
  Given the focus ring is placed over the brightest heatmap cell and over the darkest canvas region in each of the six themes
  When contrast is measured
  Then the ring meets at least 3:1 against the adjacent surface in every case
  And the design states the technique used to guarantee it (for example a two-tone ring) rather than relying on a single colour

Scenario: Dense grid does not trap the keyboard
  Given focus is inside the 200-level DOM ladder
  When the user presses Tab
  Then focus leaves the ladder to the next region rather than advancing one row
  And pressing Escape also exits the grid and returns focus to the panel header

Scenario: Live update does not steal focus (failure path)
  Given focus is on a specific ladder row and a WS reconnect re-seeds the book
  When the panel re-renders
  Then focus remains on the same logical price level if it still exists, or moves to the nearest surviving level with an announcement saying so
  And focus never jumps silently to the document body

Scenario: Dialog restores focus
  Given the flatten-all confirm dialog is opened from the toolbar
  When it is dismissed by Escape or by completing the action
  Then focus returns to the invoking control
  And focus was trapped inside the dialog for its whole lifetime
```

## Technical notes / design
- Roving tabindex, not `tabindex="0"` per row, is the normative pattern for grids — stated explicitly so implementers do not produce 200 tab stops.
- Focus identity in live grids is *logical* (price level, bar timestamp, order id), never index-based; this is the rule that makes the re-render scenario satisfiable and it constrains the engineering data model, so it is called out here rather than discovered later.
- Region cycling is bidirectional (`Ctrl+\` and `Ctrl+Shift+\`) and follows the user's visual panel arrangement, not DOM order, because panels are user-rearrangeable — the layout system must expose an ordered region list.
- The ring utility is a shared export (CMP-039) precisely so canvas surrogate nodes and normal DOM controls look identical; per-component ad hoc rings are prohibited.

## Test plan
- Prototype the region-cycling and grid-escape behaviour in a clickable Figma/coded spike and test it keyboard-only with the Accessibility role and one QA/SDET before sign-off.
- Contrast-measure the ring against a fixture set of 12 worst-case backgrounds × 6 themes; results attached.
- Walk every archetype's tab order on paper against the redlines with two reviewers; discrepancies resolved before sign-off.
- Hand the spec to QA to draft the keyboard-only Playwright smoke script (§9.4) — if QA cannot write a deterministic assertion from the spec, the spec is not specific enough and is reworked.

## Security notes
- Focus order on destructive controls matters: the spec must not place "Flatten all" or "Cancel all" as the initial focus target of any dialog or region, and confirm dialogs must not focus their confirm button by default. Initial focus on destructive confirms is the cancel/secondary action.
- Admin screens must not expose disabled-by-RBAC controls as focusable; the spec states that RBAC-hidden actions are absent from the accessibility tree, not merely visually dimmed, to avoid leaking capability existence.

## Accessibility notes
- Covers WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (focus order), 2.4.7 (focus visible), 2.4.11 (focus not obscured, minimum) — the last is specifically relevant because floating panels and the order ticket can overlay a focused ladder row; the spec requires scroll-into-view-with-offset so the focused element is never fully hidden behind a floating panel.
- Also covers 2.1.2 (no keyboard trap) and 3.2.1/3.2.2 (no context change on focus/input).

## Performance notes
- Roving tabindex plus a windowed mirror keeps the accessibility tree small; the spec states a ceiling (materialised focusable surrogates per panel) so the a11y tree cannot grow with data volume and regress frame time, consistent with `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
- Specifies a dev-only focus-trace overlay (available behind the existing diagnostics overlay SCR-046) that logs focus transitions and their announcements, so focus-loss defects are reproducible from a recording rather than from memory.

## Definition of Done
- Focus/landmark spec merged into `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.4 as the normative expansion, with redlines in Figma.
- Every catalogued screen mapped to an archetype.
- Ring contrast evidence attached for all themes.
- QA confirms the spec is testable and has drafted at least the grid-escape and dialog-restore assertions.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E47-D02`.
- Feeds E47-D06 (surrogate focus), E47-D10 (CMP-039 contribution), and the Sprint 23–26 focus remediation stories.

## Branch
`design/e47-focus-model`

## References

- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-039, CMP-043, CMP-044, CMP-049

title: Accessibility settings hi-fi (SCR-117) incl. preference previews
body:
## Context
SCR-117 is described in `14-screens-catalogue.md` as "the exemplar" — the screen whose own quality bar is the standard the rest of the app is measured against. It is also the control surface for every accommodation E47 ships: reduced motion, canvas-animation disable, always-show table alternatives, focus-ring thickness, price-announcement policy, tape verbosity, keyboard-only mode, larger hit targets, announcement throttling.

US-SET-007 requires those preferences to apply *immediately across all views including WebGL surfaces*, to honour OS-level `prefers-reduced-motion`/`prefers-contrast` as the default with an explicit override, and to persist per user. The design problem is not the form; it is making each option's *effect* legible before the user commits — a trader will not flip "keyboard-only mode" on a live workspace to find out what it does.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Hi-fi for SCR-117** in all six themes at 100/125/150% font scale and at 200% browser zoom, using CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-086 SettingsNav/SettingsLayout, CMP-228 PreviewTile.
- **Per-option plain-language description** of the effect ("Heatmap trails stop fading and change instantly; the chart stops easing when it pans"), not a restatement of the label.
- **Preview tiles**: a live micro-preview per option group — motion (an animating heatmap cell that stops), focus (a focused control showing the chosen ring thickness), announcement policy (a transcript-style sample of what the screen reader would say under each setting), table-alternative default (a chart tile flipping to its table form).
- **OS-detection states**: "Following your system setting (reduced motion is on)" with an explicit override control and a clear indication of which value is currently effective; plus the state where the OS setting changes while the screen is open.
- **Announcement-policy control**: off / on significant change / always, with the throttle cadence control (default derived from E47-D01's measured recommendation) and an explanation of what "significant" includes (fills, rejects, auto-flatten, rule fired, WS disconnect, environment switch — the assertive class from §6.2).
- **Keyboard-only mode**: the design for what it *reveals* — the form equivalents of drag-only interactions (nudge order line, move drawing point, reposition rule-graph edge) — since the catalogue makes that its explicit function.
- **Link-out design** to the accessibility statement / conformance report (E47-D13) and to the hotkey cheatsheet (SCR-013).
- **States**: default, modified-from-default (with per-option reset), section reset with the change preview US-SET-001 requires, and the settings-search result presentation for a11y terms.

## Out of scope
- The performance-profile settings (SCR-118) — separate screen, separate owner.
- Appearance/theme controls (SCR-116, owned by E47-D03) beyond linking to them.
- Persistence, sync and backend schema (engineering chunk).
- The content of the announcement scripts themselves (E47-D07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every option explains its effect
  Given the hi-fi is complete
  When each option in SCR-117 is inspected
  Then it has a persistent visible label and a plain-language description of what changes when it is enabled
  And no option relies on placeholder text as its label

Scenario: OS preference is honoured and overridable
  Given the operating system reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When SCR-117 is opened
  Then reduced motion shows as on, attributed to the system setting
  And an explicit override is available, and the currently effective value is unambiguous

Scenario: OS preference changes while the screen is open (edge case)
  Given SCR-117 is open with reduced motion following the system
  When the OS setting flips to no-preference
  Then the effective value updates in place and the change is announced politely
  And any user override already set is not silently discarded

Scenario: The screen meets its own standard
  Given SCR-117 rendered at 200% zoom in the high-contrast theme
  When it is reviewed
  Then no content is clipped or requires two-dimensional scrolling
  And every control state change is announced on change

Scenario: Verbosity reduction is demonstrable (failure path)
  Given announcement verbosity is set to low
  When the preview tile plays the sample stream for a fast-moving symbol
  Then the sample shows only significant events, not per-tick narration
  And the design states the exact event classes that survive at low verbosity
```

## Technical notes / design
- Preview tiles must be honest: they render the real component under the pending setting rather than a static illustration, so the design specifies them as live component instances with a scripted data loop, and states that preview animation itself respects the currently-effective reduced-motion value (a preview that animates while demonstrating reduced motion is a defect).
- Effective-value resolution is `user override ?? OS signal ?? product default`; the UI shows the source of the effective value, because "why is motion still off?" is otherwise unanswerable.
- Every option maps to a stable preference key so the `a11y.preference_changed {key, value}` analytics event in the catalogue is meaningful; the key list is part of this deliverable and is consumed by the engineering chunk and by E47-D07.
- Larger-hit-target option raises targets beyond the 24 px floor rather than being the mechanism that reaches it — the floor is unconditional per §4/US-SET-004.

## Test plan
- Design QA against the catalogue's own sign-off checklist for SCR-117 (all five boxes) before requesting CDO sign-off.
- Keyboard-only and NVDA walkthrough of the prototype by the Accessibility role; every control reached, labelled and its state announced.
- Contrast check of the whole screen in all six themes via the token linter output from E47-D03.
- Review of the plain-language descriptions by someone outside the design org for comprehension (the descriptions are the deliverable most likely to be written for auditors rather than users).

## Security notes
- Accessibility preferences are per-user, non-sensitive, but the analytics event must remain aggregated as the catalogue states — it must not become a per-user disability profile. The design explicitly states that no free-text or identity-linked field is added to the event.
- Keyboard-only mode reveals form equivalents for destructive drag actions (e.g. moving a stop). Those forms inherit the destructive-action confirm policy (US-SET-003) and must not become a lower-friction path to the same irreversible action.

## Accessibility notes
- This screen is the exemplar: one `h1`, sectioned headings, fieldset/legend grouping for radio groups, descriptions associated via `aria-describedby`, no colour-only state, 24 px minimum targets, and full operation at 200% zoom and 150% font scale.
- The link to the accessibility statement is a real link with descriptive text, not "click here".

## Performance notes
- The catalogue states that enabling "prefer table alternatives" swaps panel default views *without reloading data*, and that disabling animation removes transition work from the frame budget entirely. The design must therefore not introduce any option whose application requires a panel remount or a data refetch; each option is specified as a runtime-switchable flag, and the preview tiles are budgeted so the settings screen itself never exceeds the idle-frame budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
- `a11y.preference_changed {key, value}` per the catalogue, aggregated. The design adds the effective-value source (user/os/default) to the payload so adoption analysis can distinguish deliberate choices from inherited OS settings.

## Definition of Done
- Hi-fi complete for all states, six themes, three font scales, 200% zoom; published in Figma and reflected in the SCR-117 catalogue entry.
- Preference key list published and accepted by the engineering chunk lead.
- Catalogue sign-off checklist for SCR-117 fully satisfied with evidence.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs.

title: Canvas accessibility design: DOM mirror, surrogates and table alternatives
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 names this the primary architectural risk of the whole standard: raw WebGL pixels are invisible to assistive technology, and CandleViewer renders its most valuable data — candles, footprint cells, heatmap, profiles, CVD, bubbles, DOM depth — to canvas. §6 mandates four complementary layers, all of them, not a choice among them.

E47 is where those layers stop being a promise and become verified conformance. The engine work exists (E11/E12/E18/E19/E23 shipped surrogate hooks), SCR-045 exists as the chart's table alternative, but the audit (E47-D02) will show gaps: surfaces with a mirror but no table, tables that are snapshots rather than live, sort/filter state that dies on every tick, and "(estimated)" provenance that exists visually but not accessibly. This ticket designs the complete, consistent treatment across every canvas surface so the remediation stories have one spec, not six improvisations.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Surface inventory**: every canvas-rendered data surface — chart panel (SCR-030), footprint, volume/delta/TPO profile (SCR-038), DOM ladder + liquidity heatmap, CVD/delta panes, big-trade bubbles, Deep-Stats rows (CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip) — each with its four-layer status and the design for whatever is missing.
- **Layer 1 — DOM mirror design**: what a focusable logical unit is per surface (bar, footprint cell, profile level, ladder row, bubble), its accessible name template, its alignment/size rule against the visual target (so pointer users hit the same region and target-size is satisfied), and the windowing rule that keeps the tree small.
- **Layer 3 — table alternatives**: hi-fi for SCR-045 (chart/footprint table, the normative equivalent of SCR-030) plus the profile table and the DOM-ladder table with exactly the column sets fixed in §6.3; sort tri-state with `aria-sort`, filter toolbar with the live-region filter announcement, the in-place patch model that preserves focus and sort across updates, the "data is for bar X, no longer in view" stale banner, and the paginate/load-more control.
- **Provenance in the accessible layer**: the "(estimated)" badge and its reason (`iceberg`, `stop-run`, `order-count proxy`) present as text in both the mirror label and the table column, satisfying the heuristic-data caveat the standard calls out — this is the accuracy-risk control, not decoration.
- **Parity rule and its proof**: a documented per-surface mapping showing every visual datum has an accessible counterpart, used by QA as the parity test oracle.
- **Layer 4 — canvas fallback labels**: the `role="img"` rolling-summary template per surface (the chart's is already sketched in SCR-030's catalogue entry) with the update trigger and throttle.
- **Equal-status placement**: the table toggle reachable from the panel header (`Alt+T`), not buried in settings, per SCR-045's sign-off checklist.

## Out of scope
- Live-region announcement policy and verbosity (E47-D07).
- Engine implementation of the mirror/query surface (chart-engine team; the API requirement is already stated in `26-chart-engine-design.md` per §6.1).
- New analytical data — the tables expose existing data only.
- Export formats beyond the TSV copy and CSV export already catalogued on SCR-045.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every canvas surface has all four layers designed
  Given the surface inventory
  When the spec is published
  Then each surface states its DOM-mirror unit, its live-region class, its table alternative, and its canvas role and label template
  And no surface is granted an exemption on density or performance grounds

Scenario: Table and canvas expose the same data
  Given a footprint bar with bid volume, ask volume, delta, an imbalance flag and an estimated badge
  When the bar is read through the table alternative
  Then every one of those values is present, with the delta sign as text and the imbalance and estimated flags as text labels
  And the parity mapping records the visual-to-accessible correspondence for each

Scenario: Live update preserves interaction state
  Given the DOM-ladder table is open, sorted by cumulative depth, with the my-levels filter active and focus on a row
  When the throttled update tick patches values
  Then sort order, filter state and focus position survive the update
  And rows are patched in place rather than the table being rebuilt

Scenario: Focused unit scrolls out of view (edge case)
  Given the table is showing data for a bar the user has since scrolled past
  When the bar is no longer in the visible range
  Then a banner states the data is for that bar and is no longer in view, with a keyboard-operable refresh to current
  And stale values are never presented as if they were live

Scenario: Mirror stays bounded under load (failure path)
  Given 100,000 bars are loaded
  When the mirror is materialised
  Then only the currently visible and focusable units exist in the accessibility tree, within the stated ceiling
  And the design states what happens when the user jumps to a distant range (re-window, announce the new range) rather than materialising everything
```

## Technical notes / design
- Surrogate elements are visually hidden via off-screen/clip-path positioning, never `display:none`, and are sized/aligned to the visual target so target-size and focus-visible are satisfied by the same element — stated in §6.1 and re-asserted here because it is the detail most often lost in implementation.
- The mirror and the table read from the *same* windowed query surface the engine exposes; the table is explicitly not a snapshot or an export, which is what makes the "equal status" claim defensible.
- Sort resets to the surface's natural default when the focused unit changes (new bar = new default view) — deliberate, to avoid stale-sort confusion; the design shows the announcement that accompanies the reset.
- Update cadence for the table matches the ambient live-region throttle (default 1 update / 2 s, user-configurable in SCR-117) so a screen-reader user is not fighting a re-reading table.
- The chart's canvas `aria-label` is a rolling summary (symbol, interval, visible bar count, last close, delta), regenerated on data change and throttled identically; a stale summary is worse than none, so the spec states its refresh trigger.

## Test plan
- Parity test oracle handed to QA: for a fixed recorded Bybit fixture, every visual cell value must be retrievable through the table and through the mirror label; QA automates a diff of the two.
- NVDA and JAWS walkthrough of a coded prototype of the footprint table: table-mode navigation, sort announcement via `aria-sort`, filter announcement, in-place patch behaviour.
- Accessibility-tree size measurement at 100k bars to confirm the windowing ceiling holds.
- Design QA of SCR-045 against its catalogue sign-off checklist (equal-status placement, column set, keyboard navigation within the grid, export control, per-bar cell expansion).

## Security notes
- The mirror and tables must respect the same RBAC and environment scoping as the visual surface: a Viewer must not obtain, via the accessible layer, order or position data the visual layer withholds. The spec states that the accessible layer is rendered from the same filtered view-model, never from an unfiltered source.
- The "My orders" column in the DOM-ladder table exposes own working orders; it inherits the panel's account scoping so a fan-out across accounts cannot leak another account's working orders into a mirror label.

## Accessibility notes
- Directly implements WCAG 1.1.1 (non-text content), 1.3.1 (info and relationships), 2.1.1 (keyboard), 4.1.2 (name/role/value) for the canvas surfaces, and is the mechanism by which the documented canvas exclusion in §1 is discharged rather than accepted.
- Table alternatives are full-fidelity by rule: a stripped "compliance minimum" table is an explicit failure condition of this ticket.

## Performance notes
- The mirror is windowed and frame-synchronised with the engine's LOD/culling, per §6.1 and `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; the spec states the per-panel materialised-node ceiling and requires the table to virtualise (SCR-045 catalogue: 100k rows, ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame, no extra fetch).
- Because both layers read the existing in-memory series, enabling them must not add a network request or a second data path; any design that would is rejected.

## Observability
- `chart.data_table_opened` and `chart.data_table_exported` already exist; the design adds a surface identifier so adoption per canvas surface is visible, and requests a counter for mirror-window rebuilds so pathological re-windowing shows up in telemetry rather than as a user complaint.

## Definition of Done
- Four-layer spec published per surface and merged into the standard's §6 as the normative expansion.
- SCR-045 hi-fi plus profile-table and ladder-table hi-fi complete, all states including the stale banner and the empty/no-data case.
- Parity mapping published and accepted by QA as a test oracle.
- Prototype SR walkthrough evidence attached (NVDA + JAWS).
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs; chart-engine lead confirms the required engine query surface is already available or files the engine task.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E47-D02` (audit gaps), `E47-D04` (focus contract the surrogates obey).
- Feeds E47-D07 (announcements read from the same units), E47-D11 handoff, Sprint 23–26 canvas remediation stories.

title: Live-region announcement design: content, politeness and throttling
body:
## Context
A trading terminal streaming at 10 Hz+ will, with naive live regions, produce a screen reader that talks continuously and communicates nothing. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2 sets the architecture — polite regions for throttled ambient values, assertive/`role="alert"` reserved for discrete high-importance events, pre-rendered region containers whose text content is swapped — but it does not write the *words*. This ticket does.

The stakes are asymmetric and that asymmetry drives the design: missing an ambient price update costs nothing; missing "order rejected" or "position auto-flattened by risk engine" can cost money. So the event taxonomy, not the cadence, is the core deliverable, and every assertive event must be announced once, in full, unthrottled and uncoalesced.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Event taxonomy** covering every announceable event in the product, each classified `ambient-polite` / `significant-assertive` / `silent`, with the owning surface and the user-facing class name shown in SCR-117's announcement-policy control:
  - Assertive (never throttled, never coalesced): order filled / partially filled, order rejected with reason, position auto-flattened by the risk engine, kill-switch engaged, rule triggered, risk cap or lockout hit, WS disconnected / reconnected, Demo↔Live switch confirmed, alert fired, native SL placement failure.
  - Polite (throttled, latest-value-wins): best bid/ask, mark price, unrealized P&L, CVD value, position size change from own fills already announced assertively, connection quality.
  - Silent (available in the mirror/table, never narrated): per-tick tape prints, individual heatmap cell decay, bubble spawns, chart redraws.
- **Announcement copy** per event: exact template strings with token slots, written to be parseable by ear — symbol first, then the fact, then the qualifiers ("Rejected. Limit buy 0.5 BTCUSDT at 64,000. Reason: insufficient margin."), with sign spoken as a word where ambiguity is possible.
- **Throttle model**: default cadence (seeded by E47-D01's measured recommendation), the per-field latest-value-wins rule, the coalescing rule for bursts, and the interaction with SCR-117's verbosity levels (off / significant only / always) so each level has a defined, demonstrable output.
- **Region hygiene spec**: which regions exist, where they live in the shell, that they are pre-rendered empty and only text content is swapped, and the rule that a region is never destroyed/recreated.
- **Interaction with focus**: an announcement never moves focus; events that *must* draw attention (kill-switch, auto-flatten) additionally surface a persistent CMP-045 Toast and a CMP-061 notification-log entry so nothing is loss-by-timing (WCAG 2.2.1).
- **Duplicate-suppression rule**: an event already announced assertively is not re-announced by the polite channel as a state change.
- **Transcript fixtures**: annotated sample transcripts for three scenarios (quiet market, fast market, incident: reject + disconnect + auto-flatten within 5 s), used as the QA oracle and as SCR-117's preview content.

## Out of scope
- Visual toast/alert design (already catalogued: CMP-045, CMP-061).
- Alert routing and delivery channels (E40).
- The SCR-117 control UI (E47-D05 owns it; this ticket supplies the class names and the preview transcripts).
- Localisation of the copy (English only in v1).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every announceable event is classified
  Given the taxonomy is published
  When any event in 24-internal-schemas.md that surfaces to the user is looked up
  Then it has exactly one classification and, if announced, an exact copy template
  And events classified silent state where the user can still obtain the information

Scenario: Assertive events are never lost to throttling
  Given verbosity is set to low and the market is fast
  When an order is rejected
  Then the rejection is announced once, in full, including the reason
  And it is not coalesced with, delayed behind, or replaced by any ambient update

Scenario: Ambient updates do not flood
  Given a symbol updating at 10 ticks per second with default settings
  When ambient announcements are measured over one minute
  Then the polite channel emits at most the configured cadence per field
  And each emission presents the latest value rather than a queued backlog

Scenario: Simultaneous incident events (edge case)
  Given a reject, a WS disconnect and an auto-flatten occur within two seconds
  When they are announced
  Then all three are announced in full in priority order with the auto-flatten first
  And none is dropped or truncated, and each also appears in the notification log

Scenario: Announcements never steal focus (failure path)
  Given focus is inside the order ticket price field
  When an assertive announcement fires
  Then focus and the in-progress input value are unchanged
  And the announcement does not close or reset the ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Priority ordering within the assertive channel is required because simultaneous events are normal during an incident: risk/safety events (auto-flatten, kill-switch, SL failure) outrank execution events (fill, reject), which outrank connectivity events.
- Latest-value-wins for polite fields is implemented as text-content replacement on a stable node; the design forbids appending, which would otherwise queue a backlog the screen reader reads minutes late.
- Copy is written for ear, not eye: no glyph-only content, no reliance on plus/minus glyphs being spoken, numbers grouped so "64,000" is not read digit by digit where the SR supports formatting hints.
- Because announcements are a safety surface, the taxonomy is versioned in `24-internal-schemas.md` terms (event name → class) so a new domain event cannot ship unclassified — the engineering chunk is asked to add a check that fails when a user-surfaced event has no classification.

## Test plan
- Transcript-diff testing: QA replays the three fixture scenarios against a recorded Bybit fixture and diffs the produced NVDA speech log against the annotated expected transcript; drift fails.
- Flood test: 10 Hz symbol for 5 minutes at each verbosity level; announcements-per-minute recorded against the target.
- Incident test: forced reject + forced WS drop + simulated risk-engine flatten within a 2 s window, verifying all three announced in priority order and logged.
- Manual pass with NVDA and JAWS per §8.2 item 3, with the Owner listening to the fast-market transcript to confirm it is usable rather than merely compliant.

## Security notes
- Announcements must never speak secrets: API-key values, masked fields, 2FA codes or recovery codes are classified silent and the design states it explicitly (secret fields already auto-hide; their auto-hide countdown is announced, the value is not).
- Announcement content is account-scoped: in a multi-account trade-group fan-out, an announcement names the account it belongs to, and a user without RBAC visibility of an account receives no announcement for it.
- Rejection reasons are surfaced from the exchange; the design requires reason strings to be mapped to a known vocabulary before announcement rather than announcing raw upstream text, to avoid injecting unbounded content into an assertive channel.

## Accessibility notes
- Implements WCAG 4.1.3 (status messages), 2.2.1 (timing adjustable — nothing is loss-by-timing because every assertive event is also persisted to the notification log), and keeps attention-drawing to audio/text rather than flashing (2.3.1).
- Verbosity control is a first-class accommodation, not a hidden developer flag; its levels are demonstrable in SCR-117's preview.

## Performance notes
- Live-region text swaps are cheap but must not be driven per-tick from the render loop; the design specifies a single throttled scheduler shared by all polite regions, consistent with the update-coalescing model in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, so the announcement layer adds bounded work per second regardless of message rate.

## Observability
- Requests counters for announcements emitted per channel per minute and for assertive events suppressed or dropped (which must be zero); a non-zero drop counter is an alerting condition because it means a safety announcement was lost.

## Definition of Done
- Taxonomy, copy templates, throttle model and region-hygiene spec merged into the standard's §6.2 expansion and cross-referenced from `24-internal-schemas.md`.
- Three annotated transcript fixtures published and accepted by QA as oracles.
- SCR-117 preview content handed to E47-D05.
- NVDA + JAWS validation evidence attached.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs; Security engineer confirms the no-secrets and account-scoping rules.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E47-D05` (verbosity control surface), `E47-D06` (announcements read the same logical units as the mirror).
- Feeds the Sprint 23–26 announcement remediation stories and the QA screen-reader scripts.
