title: Motion design: reduced-motion variants and flash-rate safety
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §7 treats motion as a safety issue, not a taste issue: the heatmap decay trail, big-trade bubble pop, price-flash-on-tick and liquidation flash are all animations driven by *market data rate*, which means a naive implementation exceeds the WCAG 2.3.1 three-flashes-per-second seizure threshold on any fast symbol without anyone intending it. The standard makes flash-rate a hard automated **and** manual gate, and requires reduced motion to be a design-system token/mode consumed by every animated component, never a per-component CSS override.

By Sprint 21 the product has accumulated animation across many epics (heatmap, bubbles, toasts, panel transitions, chart inertia, replay scrubbing, rule-graph edge animation, alert entrances). This ticket produces the single motion spec that E47's remediation stories apply, and — critically — the flash-rate budget that makes the CI gate implementable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion inventory**: every animated surface in the product with its trigger, duration, easing, amplitude and whether it is data-rate-driven or interaction-driven.
- **Paired variants**: for each, a `motion-safe` and a `motion-reduce` definition. `motion-reduce` is instant state change or a single low-amplitude cross-fade with no motion or scale — the standard's wording, made concrete per component.
- **Flash-rate budget**: a per-surface maximum visual-state-change rate with the coalescing rule that enforces it (e.g. price-flash is throttled to at most 2 Hz and coalesced across ticks; bubble bursts are batched per frame window; liquidation flash is rate-limited independently of event rate). The budget is expressed so CI can assert it.
- **Pause/stop/hide controls** for auto-moving content lasting >5 s (WCAG 2.2.2): replay auto-play, any ticker-tape scroller, auto-following live price at the right edge — with the rule that auto-follow remains functional (it is not decorative) but gains an accessible pause.
- **Motion tokens** contributed to the design system: duration scale, easing set, amplitude caps, and the `motion-safe`/`motion-reduce` variant pair contract every animated component must consume.
- **Override design**: the in-app reduced-motion override (`Ctrl+Shift+M` per §3.2) and its relationship to the OS setting and to SCR-117's control, including the toast/announcement confirming the change.
- **Redlines** applied to the affected catalogue entries and Figma frames.

## Out of scope
- Colour values (E47-D03).
- The SCR-117 control UI (E47-D05).
- Implementation and the CI flash-rate check itself (engineering/QA chunks consume this budget).
- Replay engine scrubbing mechanics beyond its auto-play pause control.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animation has a reduced variant
  Given the motion inventory
  When the spec is published
  Then every entry has both a motion-safe and a motion-reduce definition
  And no entry resolves its reduced variant to "unchanged" unless it is already static

Scenario: Flash rate is bounded independently of data rate
  Given a symbol printing 40 trades per second
  When price-flash, bubble burst and liquidation flash are all active
  Then the combined visual-state-change rate on any single region stays at or below the budgeted maximum, below three per second
  And the budget states the coalescing window that produces that result

Scenario: Reduced motion is honoured end to end
  Given the OS reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When the workspace is opened
  Then heatmap trails, bubble pops, price-flash pulses and panel transitions use their reduced variants
  And the chart still functions, including auto-follow, without easing animation

Scenario: Auto-moving content can be paused (edge case)
  Given replay auto-play is running for longer than five seconds
  When the user reaches the pause control by keyboard
  Then playback pauses and the control's state change is announced
  And the pause control is reachable without first stopping to use a mouse

Scenario: Override conflicts with OS setting (failure path)
  Given the OS requests reduced motion and the user sets the in-app override to full motion
  When the override is applied
  Then full motion is used and the UI states that a system preference is being overridden
  And the flash-rate budget still applies, because it is a safety limit and not a motion preference
```

## Technical notes / design
- The flash-rate budget applies **in both motion modes**. Reduced motion removes easing and trails; it does not by itself guarantee sub-3 Hz state change, because an instant colour swap per tick is still a flash. This distinction is the single most important sentence in the spec and is called out as such.
- Data-rate-driven animation is specified as "coalesce to a fixed cadence, then animate" rather than "animate per event" — the same shape as the update coalescing already used for rendering, so the motion layer inherits an existing guarantee instead of inventing one.
- Reduced-motion is resolved once at the app level and exposed as a token/mode; components must not read `prefers-reduced-motion` individually, so a single override point exists.
- Auto-follow-at-right-edge is classified as functional, not decorative, with its pause exposed through the existing chart controls; the spec states that pausing auto-follow is distinct from pausing the data feed and must not be confused with it in the copy.

## Test plan
- Automated: a frame-sampling harness measures visual-state-change rate per region against a high-rate recorded fixture; exceeding the budget fails. Handed to QA/engineering as the specification for the §9 gate.
- Manual: reduced-motion pass with the OS setting on and off across chart, heatmap, bubbles, toasts, panel transitions, rule-graph and replay; recorded as video evidence.
- Vestibular review: at least one reviewer sensitive to motion (or an external participant from E47-D01's pool) confirms the reduced variants are actually comfortable, not merely shorter.
- Keyboard reachability of every pause control verified.

## Security notes
- Motion is a signalling channel for safety-relevant state (kill-switch engaged, Live environment, armed rules). Reducing motion must never remove the *signal*, only its animation — the spec requires each such indicator to remain identifiable statically through icon and text, so a reduced-motion user is never less informed about a dangerous state.

## Accessibility notes
- Covers WCAG 2.3.1 (three flashes), 2.3.3 (animation from interactions, AAA — adopted as a hard requirement here), 2.2.2 (pause, stop, hide).
- Reduced motion is a token/mode per §7.4; ad hoc per-component overrides are an explicit failure condition of this ticket.

## Performance notes
- Disabling animation must measurably remove work from the frame budget (the SCR-117 catalogue entry promises exactly that), so the spec requires reduced variants to skip the animation pipeline rather than run a zero-duration tween; the difference is measurable and QA is asked to measure it.
- Coalescing windows are chosen to align with the existing render cadence so the motion layer adds no additional timer cascade.

## Observability
- Requests a counter for flash-budget clamps applied per surface per minute: a clamp firing constantly indicates an upstream implementation that animates per event, which is the defect pattern this spec exists to prevent, and it is far cheaper to see in telemetry than in a seizure report.

## Definition of Done
- Motion inventory, paired variants, flash-rate budget and pause-control spec merged into `16-design-system-brief.md` and cross-referenced from `05-accessibility-standard.md` §7.
- Motion tokens accepted by the design-system team (E47-D10 consumes them).
- Video evidence of reduced-motion behaviour on every animated surface attached.
- Flash-rate budget accepted by QA as implementable for the CI gate.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E47-D03` (theme values the flashes use), `E47-D05` (the override control surface).
- Feeds E47-D10, the Sprint 23–26 motion remediation stories, and the QA flash-rate gate.

## Branch
`design/e47-motion-reduced-motion`

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §7, §9
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (motion tokens)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-038, SCR-117, replay and DOM/heatmap entries
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-045, CMP-061, CMP-074

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e47-motion-reduced-motion`

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-D08>`

title: Keyboard operability design: cheatsheet, command palette and drag alternatives
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 states a rule with very wide consequences: *no functionality may depend on hover-only or drag-only interaction*. CandleViewer is full of drag: dragging an order line to move a stop, dragging drawing-tool handles, dragging rule-graph edges between nodes, dragging panel splitters, dragging the chart to pan, dragging a profile's anchor range. Each needs a designed keyboard equivalent, and those equivalents need to be discoverable — which is what SCR-013 (hotkey cheatsheet) and SCR-012 (command palette, explicitly called "a critical a11y escape hatch" in §3.2) are for.

E47-D04 designed *where focus goes*. This ticket designs *what the keyboard can do once it is there*, and closes the discoverability loop so a keyboard-only user can find the equivalent without reading documentation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Drag-equivalent catalogue**: every drag- or hover-only interaction in the product with its keyboard equivalent, specified as select → adjust → commit/cancel (e.g. order line: Tab or click to select, arrow keys nudge by one tick, Shift+arrows by ten, Enter commits, Esc cancels, with the pending value announced during adjustment).
- **Chart control surrogate**: the full keyboard pan/zoom/crosshair model from §3.1.7 (arrows move crosshair by one bar or one tick, Shift+arrows pan, +/− zoom, Home/End to oldest/latest), including what is announced on each move and how it interacts with the DOM mirror from E47-D06.
- **Rule node-graph keyboard model**: select node, move node, create an edge between two nodes, delete an edge, and navigate the graph — the densest drag surface in the product, and the one most likely to have been built drag-only.
- **SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet hi-fi**: shows *current* bindings including user remaps, searchable, grouped by the categories in §3.2, reachable from anywhere by `?`, itself fully keyboard operable and dismissible.
- **SCR-012 command palette hi-fi** as the escape hatch: every command reachable by name including the ones with no default binding, with the binding shown next to each entry, fuzzy search, and clear empty/no-match states.
- **SCR-113 hotkey editor a11y review**: bind-time conflict detection presentation (US-SET-002 requires both actions shown and resolution before saving), reserved-key refusal copy, and the "restore defaults" affordance — reviewed and redlined, not redesigned from scratch.
- **"Inert here" feedback**: US-SET-002 requires a binding valid elsewhere but inert in the current view to explain itself on press; the design specifies that explanation as an announced, non-modal message rather than silence.

## Out of scope
- Changing the default keymap in §3.2 (it is locked; this ticket documents and surfaces it).
- The focus model itself (E47-D04).
- Implementation of remapping persistence (engineering chunk).
- Voice control and switch-device input (not in the standard's scope).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every drag interaction has a keyboard equivalent
  Given the drag-equivalent catalogue
  When any drag- or hover-only interaction in the product is looked up
  Then it has a specified select, adjust, commit and cancel key sequence
  And the adjustment granularity and its coarse modifier are stated

Scenario: Moving a stop by keyboard is safe and reversible
  Given a working order line is selected on the chart
  When arrow keys adjust its price and Escape is pressed before committing
  Then the order is unchanged and the pending adjustment is discarded
  And the pending price was announced during adjustment so the user knew what would be committed

Scenario: Command palette reaches unbound commands
  Given a command has no default keyboard binding
  When the user opens the command palette and searches for it by name
  Then it is listed and can be executed from the palette
  And its current binding, or the absence of one, is shown

Scenario: Cheatsheet reflects remaps (edge case)
  Given the user has remapped flatten to Ctrl+Shift+F
  When the cheatsheet is opened
  Then it shows Ctrl+Shift+F for flatten, not the default binding
  And the entry is findable by searching either the action name or the key

Scenario: Inert binding explains itself (failure path)
  Given a binding that is valid in the order ticket is pressed while focus is in the journal
  When the key is pressed
  Then a non-modal message explains that the action is not available in this view and where it is available
  And nothing happens silently
```

## Technical notes / design
- The select→adjust→commit pattern is specified once and reused, so drawing handles, order lines, profile anchors and graph nodes all behave identically; divergence per surface is the failure mode this ticket exists to prevent.
- Adjustment is announced on a polite channel with coalescing (holding an arrow key must not produce one announcement per repeat) — this interlocks with E47-D07's throttle model and is cross-referenced there.
- The palette is the guaranteed escape hatch, so the design requires *every* command to be registered in it, including commands whose only surface is a context menu or a drag gesture; a command absent from the palette is a defect by definition.
- Panel splitters get keyboard resize (focus splitter, arrows resize, Home/End for min/max) because workspace layout is otherwise mouse-only, which would strand a keyboard-only user in an unusable layout.

## Test plan
- Keyboard-only traversal of each drag-equivalent against a checklist, performed by the Accessibility role on a prototype or the current build; every equivalent must be completable without a mouse and without documentation.
- Palette completeness check: enumerate all commands from the command registry and assert each appears in the palette — handed to QA as an automatable assertion.
- Cheatsheet remap test: remap three bindings, confirm the cheatsheet and palette both reflect them.
- NVDA pass over the adjustment announcements to confirm hold-to-repeat does not flood.

## Security notes
- Keyboard equivalents for destructive actions inherit the destructive-action confirm policy (US-SET-003) — arrow-nudging a stop to a new price is a real order amendment and must not bypass the confirm path that the drag interaction uses.
- The command palette must be RBAC-filtered: a Viewer must not see order-placing or admin commands listed, since the palette would otherwise enumerate capabilities the user cannot exercise and disclose the shape of privileged functionality.
- Reserved-key refusal copy must not disclose OS or shell internals beyond the reason for refusal.

## Accessibility notes
- Covers WCAG 2.1.1 (keyboard), 2.1.4 (character key shortcuts — single-key bindings such as `B`/`S` are scoped to a focus context and remappable, which is the permitted mitigation), 2.5.1 (pointer gestures), 2.5.7 (dragging movements, new in 2.2 and the direct driver of this ticket), 3.3.1 (error identification for the inert-binding case).
- SC 2.5.7 is called out explicitly in the spec so reviewers understand this is a 2.2-level requirement, not a nicety.

## Performance notes

title: Design-system contribution: a11y primitives, patterns and Storybook a11y stories
body:
## Context
E47's remediation could be done screen by screen — and would then rot within two sprints, because the next component built would repeat the same mistakes. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §11 exists precisely to prevent that: the fixes must land in the **design system**, so accessibility becomes the default behaviour of the primitives rather than a per-screen effort.

This ticket consolidates the outputs of D03 (tokens, non-colour encodings), D04 (focus model, CMP-039 FocusRing), D07 (live-region contracts) and D08 (motion tokens) into a single, versioned contribution to the design-system package: updated component a11y contracts across all 238 catalogue entries, new/changed primitives, and the Storybook a11y stories and axe test requirements that keep them honest.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Component a11y contract sweep**: every entry in `15-component-catalogue.md` reviewed against its stated **A11y** field (role, keyboard, ARIA, focus contract) and updated where D02's audit found the contract wrong, vague or absent. Output is a diff against the catalogue, not a parallel document.
- **Primitives added or hardened**:
  - CMP-039 FocusRing — finalised geometry, per-theme colour, high-visibility variant, canvas-surrogate usage contract.
  - A `LiveRegion` primitive implementing D07's politeness/throttle contract, so no component hand-rolls `aria-live`.
  - A `VisuallyHidden`/surrogate primitive implementing the off-screen-not-display-none rule from §6.1.
  - A `MotionVariant` utility exposing the `motion-safe`/`motion-reduce` pair so animated components cannot read the media query directly.
  - A `NonColorState` helper codifying glyph/sign/pattern encodings for side, sign and flagged state from D03.
- **Pattern documentation** for the WAI-ARIA APG patterns the product relies on (combobox, listbox, tabs, dialog, menu, grid) with the CandleViewer-specific decisions recorded so implementers are not re-deciding them per screen.
- **Storybook a11y stories**: per component, a story exercising keyboard operation, focus visibility, a reduced-motion variant, a high-contrast variant, and (where applicable) its live-region behaviour; each wired to the axe addon.
- **Test requirements update**: the catalogue's per-component **Test requirements** field updated so axe and interaction tests are named obligations, and the design-system package's CI gates (contrast linter, axe, visual regression across all six themes) are specified.
- **Deprecation list**: ad hoc per-component focus rings, hand-rolled live regions and local `prefers-reduced-motion` reads, each with the replacement primitive named.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the primitives (engineering chunk consumes this spec).
- New product features or new components unrelated to accessibility.
- Screen-level remediation (owned by the per-screen stories).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every component has a correct a11y contract
  Given the 15-component-catalogue.md entries
  When the sweep is complete
  Then every entry states role, keyboard model, ARIA and focus contract, or explicitly states that it is non-interactive and why
  And every audit finding routed here is reflected in the corresponding entry

Scenario: Accessibility behaviour is inherited, not reimplemented
  Given a component needs a focus ring, a live region, a hidden surrogate or an animation
  When its contract is read
  Then it names the shared primitive it must consume
  And the deprecation list names any existing local implementation it replaces

Scenario: Storybook proves the contract
  Given a component with a keyboard model
  When its Storybook a11y story is opened
  Then the story demonstrates keyboard operation, focus visibility, reduced motion and high contrast
  And the axe addon reports no serious or critical violations for that story

Scenario: A theme is added later (edge case)
  Given a seventh theme is contributed after this ticket
  When the design-system CI runs
  Then the contrast linter evaluates the new theme across every token pair without requiring per-component changes
  And a missing token in the new theme fails the build rather than falling back silently

Scenario: A component ships without its a11y story (failure path)
  Given a new or changed component is submitted to the design system
  When it has no a11y story or fails axe
  Then the design-system CI blocks the change
  And the failure names the missing obligation explicitly
```

## Technical notes / design
- The contribution is a single versioned release of the design-system package so consuming screens upgrade once rather than piecemeal — piecemeal adoption is how a11y regressions re-enter.
- Primitives are deliberately restrictive: `LiveRegion` exposes politeness and event class, not raw `aria-live`, so D07's taxonomy cannot be bypassed by a component that "just needs one quick announcement".
- Contracts are expressed in the catalogue's existing fields rather than a new document, because a second source of truth guarantees drift.
- Visual-regression baselines are captured per theme; six themes multiply the baseline count, so the spec states which components need all six (anything encoding side/sign/state) and which need dark+high-contrast only.

## Test plan
- Design-system CI: contrast linter over all themes, axe over every story, visual regression across the specified theme matrix, keyboard interaction tests for every interactive primitive.
- Migration check: a sample of five consuming screens is re-rendered against the new package version to confirm no visual or behavioural regression beyond the intended fixes.
- Review of the deprecation list by the frontend leads to confirm every deprecated local implementation has a real replacement and a migration path.

## Security notes
- The `LiveRegion` primitive is a potential secret-leak channel; its API requires an event class from D07's taxonomy, and the taxonomy classifies secret-bearing fields as silent, so the primitive structurally prevents announcing a masked value.
- Surrogate/visually-hidden content is present in the DOM and therefore in the accessibility tree and in any DOM dump: the contract states that visually-hidden must never be used to stash data the visual layer intentionally withholds (masked keys, other accounts' orders), because hidden is not the same as absent.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket is the durability mechanism for the entire epic: it is what makes AA conformance survive the next feature, and its absence would make E47 a point-in-time exercise.
- Implements §11 of the standard (design-system requirements) and supplies the components §9's automated gates run against.

## Performance notes
- Primitives are specified to avoid per-instance observers: one app-level reduced-motion resolver, one throttled live-region scheduler, one shared focus-ring stylesheet. Per-instance media-query listeners across hundreds of ladder rows would be a measurable regression against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, so the shared-resolver rule is stated as a performance requirement, not only a tidiness one.

## Observability
- Design-system CI publishes per-release counts of axe violations, contrast failures and components lacking an a11y story; these are tracked as the system's health metric so decay is visible between releases rather than discovered at the next audit.

## Definition of Done
- Catalogue diff merged into `15-component-catalogue.md`; every component contract current.
- Primitives specified to implementation-ready detail and accepted by the frontend leads.
- Storybook a11y story requirements and CI gate definitions accepted by QA and the design-system team.
- Deprecation list published with migration paths.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs.

title: Handoff pack: a11y remediation specs, redlines and acceptance checklists
body:
## Context
The Sprint 23–26 remediation stories are the last frontend work before GA, run at high parallelism across five frontend engineers, against a finding register of (on the audit's expected scale) well over a hundred items. That combination fails badly if engineers have to interpret design intent per finding. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 makes this explicit: a Story cannot enter Ready without a linked design artifact at Status Done, enumerated states, and catalogue-registered components.

This ticket assembles the single handoff pack that satisfies DoR for every remediation story at once: per-finding specs with redlines, the primitive each fix must consume, the states to implement, and a per-story acceptance checklist an engineer can self-verify against before opening a PR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Per-screen remediation spec sheets**, one per screen with findings, each containing: the finding IDs addressed, the redlined frame, the before/after behaviour, the design-system primitive to consume (from E47-D10), the states to implement (default, focused, error, empty, loading, high-density), and the exact acceptance checklist.
- **Figma organisation**: a dedicated E47 remediation page per screen band with dev-mode-ready frames, named layers matching component IDs, and a token-inspection-ready structure so engineers read values rather than eyedrop them.
- **Spec index**: a machine-readable map `finding_id → {screen, spec_frame, primitive, acceptance_checklist_id, owning_story}` so the engineering chunk can attach the right spec to each story automatically and nothing is orphaned.
- **Copy deck**: every user-facing string this epic introduces or changes — option descriptions (D05), announcement templates (D07), inert-binding messages (D09), stale-data banners (D06), contrast warnings (D03) — in one reviewed deck so copy is not invented in code.
- **Known-deviation register**: anywhere the design deliberately diverges from a naive reading of a WCAG technique, with the rationale, so reviewers and the conformance report (E47-D13) do not re-litigate it per PR.
- **Handoff sessions**: two walkthroughs with the frontend team (one for canvas/engine surfaces, one for chrome/settings/admin), recorded, with a written Q&A appendix folded back into the specs.
- **Open-questions log**: resolved before sign-off; unresolved items cannot be left to the implementing engineer.

## Out of scope
- Writing the remediation stories themselves (engineering chunk).
- Implementation or code review.
- Post-build verification (E47-D12 design QA).
- The conformance report (E47-D13), which consumes this pack's deviation register.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every finding has a spec
  Given the audit register from E47-D02
  When the spec index is published
  Then every finding not marked engineering-only maps to a spec frame and an acceptance checklist
  And every engineering-only finding states what an engineer should do without a design artifact

Scenario: An engineer can implement without asking
  Given a randomly selected remediation spec sheet
  When a frontend engineer who did not attend the handoff reads it
  Then they can state the target behaviour, the primitive to use, the states to build and how they will verify it
  And any question they cannot answer from the sheet is recorded and the sheet is amended before sign-off

Scenario: Copy is not invented in code
  Given a user-facing string introduced by this epic
  When it is looked up
  Then it exists in the copy deck with its context and its announcement class where applicable
  And strings absent from the deck are treated as a blocker for the consuming story

Scenario: A spec conflicts with the design system (edge case)
  Given a spec sheet requires behaviour the current design-system primitive does not provide
  When the conflict is found during handoff
  Then either the primitive is extended under E47-D10 or the spec is changed, and the resolution is recorded
  And a one-off local implementation is not accepted as the resolution

Scenario: Handoff is incomplete at sprint start (failure path)
  Given a remediation story is about to enter Sprint 23 without a Done spec sheet
  When Definition of Ready is checked
  Then the story cannot enter the sprint without a recorded Architect or CDO waiver
  And the gap is raised at planning rather than absorbed silently
```

## Technical notes / design
- The pack is organised by *screen*, not by finding, because remediation PRs are naturally screen-scoped and a finding-ordered pack would scatter one PR's context across a dozen documents.
- Acceptance checklists are phrased as verifiable assertions ("focus ring visible at 3:1 over the brightest heatmap cell in all six themes") so they double as PR-description checklists and as design-QA input for E47-D12.
- The spec index schema is versioned; the engineering chunk's story generator fails loudly on shape drift rather than silently dropping findings.
- Deviations are registered up front because a conformance claim (D13) that cannot explain its deviations is not defensible to an auditor.

## Test plan
- Dry-run: one engineer implements a single medium finding purely from the pack, with no designer contact, before sign-off; every question they need to ask is a defect in the pack and is fixed.
- Completeness check: assert the spec index covers every routed finding from E47-D02.
- Copy review by the CDO and one engineer for tone, accuracy and ear-readability of the announcement strings.
- DoR dry-check against `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 for three sample stories.

## Security notes
- Spec frames and the copy deck must use fixture data only; no real account identifiers, key metadata or manager identities in shared Figma frames, which are visible to the whole engineering org.
- Announcement copy in the deck is reviewed against the no-secrets rule from E47-D07 before publication, so a secret-bearing template cannot enter the codebase via the copy deck.

## Accessibility notes
- The pack itself is accessible: specs are structured documents with text descriptions of every redline, not screenshot-only annotations, so a designer or engineer using AT can consume them.
- Each acceptance checklist names the WCAG 2.2 success criterion it satisfies, so implementers learn the criterion rather than only the fix.

## Performance notes
- Any remediation with a frame-budget implication (surrogate materialisation, table virtualisation, live-region scheduling, motion coalescing) carries its budget number in the spec sheet, so an engineer knows the ceiling before implementing rather than discovering it in a perf review.

## Observability
- The spec index doubles as the epic's burn-down source: findings with a merged story are countable, so E47 progress is reportable without manual tallying and the same index is re-used by E47-D12 and E47-D13.

## Definition of Done
- All spec sheets published; spec index merged and covering every routed finding.
- Copy deck reviewed and frozen.
- Deviation register published.
- Two handoff sessions held and recorded; Q&A appendix merged; open-questions log empty.
- Dry-run implementation completed and pack amended.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Frontend lead confirms readiness to start Sprint 23.

- `blocked_by: E47-D06, E47-D09, E47-D10` (the specs it packages).
- Blocks every Sprint 23–26 remediation story reaching Ready.

title: Accessibility statement and VPAT-shaped conformance report design
body:
## Context
The roadmap's E47 scope line ends with "a published accessibility conformance report (VPAT-shaped)". `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 is careful that there is no external legal AA mandate for a private internal tool — which makes the report's purpose *internal honesty* rather than external compliance marketing: a durable, criterion-by-criterion record of what conforms, what partially conforms, what does not, and what the documented alternatives are.

This ticket designs both the in-product accessibility statement (linked from SCR-117 and SCR-119 Help & About) and the report's structure and authoring process. It is authored early — Sprint 22, before remediation — deliberately: the report's skeleton and evidence requirements must exist *before* the fixes, so evidence is captured as work happens instead of reconstructed at GA.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Report structure** at `docs/plan/a11y/47-conformance-report.md`: WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA criteria enumerated, each with conformance level (Supports / Partially Supports / Does Not Support / Not Applicable), remarks, the evidence reference (audit finding ID, design-QA verdict, QA screen-reader pass, or CI gate), and the documented alternative where a criterion is only partially supported.
- **Evidence-capture contract**: which artefact substantiates each criterion (axe CI run, Lighthouse score, contrast linter output, keyboard-only Playwright suite, NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver pass records, E47-D12 exit report), so the report is assembled from existing outputs rather than written from memory.
- **In-product accessibility statement**: hi-fi for the statement surface reached from SCR-117 and SCR-119 — conformance target, what is supported, known limitations in plain language, the documented alternatives (table alternatives, keyboard equivalents, verbosity controls), the feedback path, and the date and version the statement applies to.
- **Known-limitations register**: each limitation with its user impact, its workaround, and either a fix ticket or an explicit accepted-risk decision with an owner — the mechanism that prevents a limitation from becoming permanent by silence.
- **Update cadence and ownership**: the statement carries a version and review date; the process states who re-issues it and when (per release, and on any change touching an in-scope screen), and where the pinned AT-version changelog from §8.1 lives.
- **Honest-claims rule**: explicit guidance that Supports may only be claimed with evidence attached, and that any criterion without evidence is reported as Partially Supports or Does Not Support.

## Out of scope
- Legal review or an externally-filed VPAT (no external mandate; the shape is borrowed, the filing is not).
- Marketing copy.
- Remediating anything the report exposes (that is the remediation stories and their follow-ups).
- Non-WCAG frameworks (Section 508, EN 301 549) beyond noting they are not claimed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every criterion has a determination and evidence
  Given the WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA criteria
  When the report is compiled at GA
  Then each has a conformance level, remarks and an evidence reference
  And no criterion is marked Supports without an attached evidence artefact

Scenario: Limitations are stated in plain language
  Given a criterion that is only partially supported
  When the in-product statement is read
  Then the limitation is described in plain language with its practical impact and the available alternative
  And the description avoids criterion numbers as the only explanation

Scenario: The statement is reachable and current
  Given the accessibility settings screen
  When the statement link is followed
  Then the statement opens, states the product version and date it applies to, and offers a feedback path
  And a statement older than the current release is flagged for re-issue rather than displayed as current

Scenario: Evidence is missing at compile time (failure path)
  Given a criterion whose evidence artefact was never produced
  When the report is compiled
  Then that criterion is reported as Partially Supports or Does Not Support with a remark saying evidence was not produced
  And it is not upgraded on the basis of a reviewer's confidence

Scenario: A limitation has no owner (edge case)
  Given a known limitation with no fix ticket and no accepted-risk decision
  When the register is reviewed before GA
  Then the limitation blocks the report's sign-off until an owner and a disposition are recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
- Authoring early is the key design decision: the evidence-capture contract is published in Sprint 22 so Sprints 23–26 produce the artefacts as a by-product, which is the difference between a report that is true and one that is assembled.
- The report is generated from the same finding register and design-QA disposition data used by E47-D02 and E47-D12, so it cannot diverge from the epic's own burn-down.
- The canvas exclusion documented in §1 is discharged in the report explicitly: the canvas criteria are supported *via* the four-layer strategy, and the report says so with the mechanism named, rather than claiming the canvas itself is accessible.
- The statement is versioned content in the product, not a static page baked into a build, so a re-issue does not require a code change to the surrounding screen.

## Test plan
- Compile a dry-run report at Sprint 22 using the current (pre-remediation) evidence to prove the pipeline works and to establish the honest starting position.
- Review the plain-language limitation descriptions with a non-specialist reader for comprehension.
- Verify the statement surface itself meets the standard (it would be a notable failure for the accessibility statement to be inaccessible) at 200% zoom in all themes, keyboard-only, with an NVDA read-through.
- Cross-check ten randomly chosen criteria against their cited evidence to confirm the citation actually substantiates the claim.

## Security notes
- The report and statement are internal artefacts but describe the product's weaknesses; the known-limitations register must not describe a limitation in a way that discloses an exploitable control gap (for example, naming an RBAC-related accessibility-tree leak in user-facing copy). Such items are described generically in the statement and fully in the internal register, with the Security engineer reviewing the split.
- The feedback path must not collect more personal data than necessary; a simple internal channel, no health or disability disclosure requested or stored.

## Accessibility notes
- The statement is a model artefact: semantic headings, no colour-only status, tables with real headers, plain language, and every conformance level expressed as a word rather than a symbol or colour.
- It names the alternatives explicitly (Alt+T table views, keyboard equivalents, verbosity controls) so a user encountering a limitation learns the workaround at the point of need.

## Performance notes
- Not a runtime surface of consequence; the statement is static content loaded on demand and must not be bundled into the main workspace entry chunk, so it costs nothing in the trading path.

## Observability
- Track statement views and feedback submissions (aggregated) as the only signal that a user hit a limitation and looked for a workaround; a spike after a release is an early warning of a regression the CI gates missed.

- Report structure and evidence-capture contract published and adopted by the Sprint 23–26 stories.

- Known-limitations register established with owners and dispositions.

title: Standing a11y design-review gate for all new and changed UI
body:
## Context
E47 brings the product to WCAG 2.2 AA at a point in time. Nothing in the process, as it stands, prevents the next feature from reintroducing a colour-only encoding, a drag-only interaction or an unthrottled live region — and a re-audit costs far more than a review at design time. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.3 already makes the Accessibility role a required reviewer for PRs touching the DOM-mirror layer, live-region logic and design-system a11y primitives; this ticket extends that principle upstream, to the point where the mistake is cheapest to fix: the design review.

It is a small, process-shaped deliverable, and it is what makes the epic durable rather than a snapshot.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **A11y design-review checklist** (one page, ≤20 items) applied to every new or changed screen or component design before it can reach Status Done: keyboard model stated; focus order and initial focus stated; no colour-only encoding; contrast measured against tokens; states enumerated including error and empty; motion variants paired; announcements classified against the D07 taxonomy; canvas surfaces declare their four layers; target sizes ≥24 px; labels visible and persistent; drag interactions have keyboard equivalents; design-system primitives consumed rather than re-implemented.
- **Gate definition**: the checklist becomes a required item in the design ticket template, with the Accessibility role (or a trained delegate) as a required reviewer; a design ticket cannot reach Done with unchecked items and no recorded waiver.
- **Waiver path**: an explicit, recorded waiver with reason and expiry, signed by the CDO, for the rare case where an item genuinely does not apply — matching the DoR/DoD rule that N/A must be stated with a reason, never silently skipped.
- **Trained-delegate model**: the criteria for a designer to act as a delegate reviewer (has run one screen-reader pass, has completed the checklist on three designs under supervision), so the gate does not bottleneck on one person — a direct mitigation of the key-person risk (R10) the risk register already tracks for specialist roles.
- **Template updates**: design ticket template, the `14-screens-catalogue.md` per-screen sign-off checklist convention, and the `15-component-catalogue.md` A11y field expectations updated so the gate is embedded in the artefacts people already use.
- **Quarterly calibration**: a recurring short session where reviewers re-score a sample of recent designs together to prevent drift, with the pinned AT-version changelog reviewed at the same time.

## Out of scope
- Code-level review gates and CI checks (already defined in §9 and owned by the engineering and QA chunks).
- Re-reviewing designs completed before this gate exists (E47-D02's audit covers the existing surface).
- Hiring or staffing decisions for the accessibility role.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The gate is enforced on new design work
  Given a new screen design ticket
  When it is moved toward Done
  Then the a11y design-review checklist is complete and a reviewer is recorded
  And unchecked items block the transition unless a waiver is recorded

Scenario: Waivers are explicit and bounded
  Given a checklist item that genuinely does not apply
  When it is waived
  Then the waiver records the reason, the approver and an expiry
  And an expired waiver resurfaces the item rather than lapsing into permanent exemption

Scenario: The gate does not bottleneck
  Given the accessibility role is unavailable for a week
  When design tickets need review
  Then a trained delegate can perform the review under the documented criteria
  And the delegate's reviews are sampled at the next calibration session

Scenario: A design passes the checklist but fails in build (edge case)
  Given a design that passed review is later found non-conformant during design QA
  When the cause is analysed
  Then the checklist is amended if the gap was a missing item
  And the amendment is recorded so the same gap cannot recur silently

Scenario: Checklist becomes a rubber stamp (failure path)
  Given calibration finds two reviewers scoring the same design differently on more than a fifth of items
  When the drift is detected
  Then a calibration session is held before further solo reviews by the affected reviewers
  And the ambiguous items are rewritten to be objectively verifiable
```

## Technical notes / design
- The checklist is deliberately short. A 60-item checklist is not completed honestly; a 20-item checklist that blocks Done is. Items are phrased as objective assertions, not judgement calls, so two reviewers reach the same verdict.
- The gate lives in the artefacts people already use (ticket template, catalogue sign-off checklists) rather than a separate process document, because a separate document is the first thing skipped under delivery pressure.
- Delegation is the R10 mitigation: a single accessibility reviewer is a key-person dependency, and a gate that stalls gets removed. The delegate criteria are therefore part of the deliverable, not an afterthought.

## Test plan
- Pilot the checklist on three in-flight designs and measure review time; if a review takes longer than 30 minutes the checklist is too long and is trimmed before adoption.
- Inter-rater check: two reviewers independently score the same three designs; >20% disagreement triggers a rewrite of the ambiguous items.
- Confirm the template changes actually block the Done transition on the board rather than being advisory text.

## Security notes
- One checklist item covers the accessibility-tree disclosure rule from E47-D10: RBAC-hidden or masked content must be absent from the accessible layer, not merely visually hidden. This keeps a security-relevant class of defect inside a routine design review rather than relying on a security review catching it later.

## Accessibility notes
- This is the sustainability mechanism for the epic's conformance claim: without it, E47-D13's report is accurate only on its publication date.
- The checklist explicitly references WCAG 2.2 success criteria per item so reviewers build criterion fluency over time rather than pattern-matching a list.

## Performance notes
- Two checklist items carry performance implications (windowed surrogates, coalesced announcements and motion), keeping the accessibility/performance interaction visible at design time, where it is cheap, instead of surfacing at a perf review after implementation.

## Observability
- Track checklist completion rate and waiver count per quarter; a rising waiver count is the early signal that the gate is decaying into a formality and triggers a review of the checklist's realism.

## Definition of Done
- Checklist published and embedded in the design ticket template and the catalogue sign-off conventions.
- Gate active on the board with the required-reviewer rule in force.
- Delegate criteria published and at least one delegate qualified.
- Pilot and inter-rater evidence attached; calibration cadence scheduled.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs.

- `blocked_by: E47-D10` (the checklist references the primitives designs must consume).
- Complements E47-D12 and sustains E47-D13's claim beyond GA.

title: Spike: audit methodology, tooling and screen-reader harness baseline
body:
## Context
`14-screens-catalogue.md` defines 159 screens, most with several states (empty, loading, error, populated, edge-density). A naive "open every screen and run axe" sweep either misses the states where defects actually live, or takes longer than the three sprints R5 allocates. Before committing 40 points of remediation we need to know: how the sweep is driven, what a finding record looks like, and whether the pinned screen-reader matrix in `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1 can be executed inside an Electron production build repeatably enough to sign off on.

This spike is timeboxed to one sprint-week and produces decisions, not product code. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6 governs Spike DoR/DoD: a written question, a timebox, and a recorded decision with rationale.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Decide the sweep driver: reuse the existing Playwright E2E fixtures (which already navigate to every screen for the keyboard-only smoke suite) versus a dedicated route/state enumeration harness. Prototype both against 10 representative screens including **SCR-030**, **SCR-045**, **SCR-050**, **SCR-082**, **SCR-117**, **SCR-152** (disconnected), **SCR-156** (error boundary).
- Decide how panel *states* are enumerated: state fixtures already used by Storybook/visual-regression versus runtime state injection over the WS mock. Record which screens have no reachable fixture for a state and therefore need a manual entry in the matrix.
- Define the **finding record schema** (screen id, component id, WCAG SC, level A/AA, severity, reproduction, detection source automated/manual, owning ticket, status) and where it lives (a checked-in JSON file under `docs/plan/` so the conformance report can be generated from it, not a spreadsheet).
- Validate the SR harness: run the §8.2 task script fragment on NVDA against the production Electron build; measure how long one full screen pass takes and whether speech output can be captured for evidence.
- Produce the sprint-level plan: which screens get a deep manual pass (canvas/dense/destructive surfaces) versus an automated pass plus spot check, with the rationale written down.

## Out of scope
- Fixing anything found during the spike (findings are recorded, then fixed by **E47-T01**'s children).
- Building the full harness — **E47-T04**.
- Procuring or upgrading JAWS/VoiceOver hardware; assume the matrix in §8.1 is available.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A decision exists, with rationale
  When the spike closes
  Then a written decision names the sweep driver, the state-enumeration approach and the finding schema
  And each alternative considered is recorded with why it was rejected

Scenario: The estimate is grounded in measurement
  Given the 10-screen prototype ran
  Then the extrapolated cost of the full sweep is stated in hours with the measured per-screen figure it derives from
  And if that extrapolation exceeds the E47-T01 estimate, a scope proposal is attached

Scenario: The SR harness is proven or the risk is escalated
  Given NVDA was run against the production Electron build
  Then either a repeatable capture procedure is documented
  Or an explicit risk entry is filed stating that SR evidence will be manual-notes-only, with Owner visibility

Scenario: Unreachable states are surfaced early
  Given a screen state has no fixture and cannot be induced
  Then it is listed as a manual-only row in the plan rather than silently dropped from the matrix
```

## Technical notes / design
Prefer reusing existing fixtures: the keyboard-only E2E suite (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §9.4) already knows how to reach every screen without a mouse, and reuse keeps one navigation model rather than two that drift. The finding file is checked in precisely so that **E47-T05**'s report is generated, not transcribed — a transcribed report goes stale between the sweep and GA.

## Test plan
Spike output is reviewed by the Accessibility role, QA lead and Architect. The 10-screen prototype's findings are re-run once by a second person to confirm the procedure is reproducible by someone who did not write it.

## Security notes
The sweep runs against a demo-environment build with synthetic accounts only; captured speech output and screenshots must not contain live account identifiers or API-key material. Any captured evidence is stored in the repo only after review for such content.

## Accessibility notes
The spike's own artefacts (the plan document, the finding schema docs) are plain markdown/JSON and readable with assistive technology; no findings are recorded as images without a text equivalent.

## Performance notes
Measure and record per-screen sweep wall-clock time; the full automated sweep must fit inside the CI budget for a nightly job (target ≤20 min) or it will not be run often enough to matter.

## Observability
None (spike). The finding-file location and generation command are documented so downstream jobs can consume them.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Timebox respected; decision document merged under `docs/plan/`.
- [ ] Finding-record schema agreed and an example file committed.
- [ ] Per-screen cost measured and the full-sweep estimate stated.
- [ ] SR capture procedure documented or risk escalated.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets (E47-T01, E47-T04) updated with the spike's conclusions before they enter a sprint.

`blocked_by`: none. Blocks **E47-T01** and **E47-T04**.

`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8, §9; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`; `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.

title: Black-box accessibility test plan for the E47 remediation story groups
body:
## Context
E47 is the epic that converts `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` from a written standard into demonstrated WCAG 2.2 AA conformance across every screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`. R5 exit criterion 2 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 9.3 requires a published, evidence-backed conformance report (VPAT-shaped); a report is only credible if the underlying test pass is written down, repeatable and executable by someone who did not build the features.

Today the E47 remediation stories (`E47-S01`..`E47-S04`) say *what to fix*. There is no single artefact a QA engineer can run against a staging build to assert "CandleViewer meets AA". `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 makes a recorded black-box QA pass non-skippable per Story, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 11 requires a written per-feature test plan plus a white-box review checklist. This ticket produces that artefact for the accessibility dimension specifically.

The plan is deliberately black-box: it is written against screen ids, hotkeys, announced strings and rendered contrast - never against React component internals - so it survives the refactors that remediation inevitably causes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e47-accessibility-test-plan.md`, organised as six executable groups mirroring the standard:
  1. **Keyboard operation** (standard section 3) - SCR-010 app shell, SCR-011 navigation rail, SCR-012 command palette, SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet, SCR-020/021 workspace + dock, SCR-030 chart panel, SCR-037 drawing toolbar, SCR-050 heatmap + DOM ladder, SCR-060/061 order tickets, SCR-081/082 rule editors (form + node graph), SCR-121 admin users. Verifies `US-SET-002` (global hotkey layer) and the keyboard-only mode of `US-SET-007`.
  2. **Screen-reader semantics and streaming announcements** (standard sections 6.1, 6.2, 8) - DOM mirror and live-region behaviour on SCR-030, SCR-050, SCR-052, SCR-053, SCR-063, SCR-092.
  3. **Table alternatives and data parity** (standard section 6.3) - SCR-045 chart data-table alternative vs SCR-030 canvas; footprint cell parity; profile and heatmap table equivalents; `Alt+T` reachability from the panel header (equal status, per the SCR-045 sign-off checklist).
  4. **Colour-independence and contrast** (standard sections 4, 5) - every buy/sell, bid/ask, P&L, order-status, connection-health and Demo/Live surface across SCR-060, SCR-063, SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-143, in dark, light, high-contrast and the three CVD-safe themes delivered by `E47-D01`/`E47-T03`.
  5. **Reduced motion, flash and zoom** (standard section 7) - heatmap trails, big-trade bubbles, price flash, toasts; `Ctrl+Shift+M` override; SCR-117 preferences; 200% zoom and 400% reflow on SCR-110..SCR-119.
  6. **Preferences, statement and report surfaces** - SCR-116 appearance/density, SCR-117 accessibility settings, the accessibility statement page and the conformance report page designed in `E47-D02`; persistence via `GET|PUT /api/v1/me/preferences` and `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*`, tables `settings` and `hotkey_profiles`.
- Per case: id `E47-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (seeded user, theme, AT combo from the standard section 8.1 matrix), steps expressed as keystrokes, expected observable result (including the *exact expected announcement text* where applicable), the `US-SET-*` / WCAG 2.2 success criterion verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E47-Q03`, or manual-only).
- **Fixture appendix**: seeded owner / manager / viewer accounts; a demo-environment account with open positions and working orders so P&L, status and fill announcements can be observed; a replay session pinned to a high-tick-rate window so the streaming-announcement throttle can be exercised deterministically; a symbol with a wide tick size and one with a very fine tick size for the ladder.
- **Traceability table**: WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria x screens x test cases, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, so `E47-T06` can cite this file directly as report evidence.
- **White-box review checklist** for reviewers: no `outline: none` without a compliant replacement, no `aria-live` region mounted inside a virtualised list, no focus call inside a WS message handler, every canvas has an `aria-label` and a mirror root.
- Defect severity mapping: a task in the standard section 8.2 script that cannot be completed keyboard+SR-only is `priority/p0` and a release blocker; awkward-but-completable is P1/P2 per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.3.

## Out of scope
- Executing the manual screen-reader passes (that is `E47-Q02`) and running the automated suites (`E47-Q03`, `E47-Q04`).
- Design-time review of tokens and redlines - owned by `E47-D01` and `E47-D03`.
- Writing the conformance report itself (`E47-T06`); this plan supplies its evidence rows only.
- Non-web surfaces: there is no Android client in scope, and no non-Electron browser is a shipped target.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: E47 accessibility black-box test plan

  Scenario: Every in-scope screen and criterion is covered
    Given the published qa/plans/e47-accessibility-test-plan.md
    When its traceability table is checked against docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
    Then every screen listed in that catalogue maps to at least one case
    And every WCAG 2.2 AA success criterion maps to at least one case or to an explicit, justified "not applicable" row

  Scenario: A case is executable by someone new to the epic
    Given a QA engineer who has never worked on CandleViewer
    When they execute group 3 against a staging build using only the fixture appendix
    Then they can reach a pass/fail verdict on every case without asking the authors a question
    And each expected announcement is quoted precisely enough to judge a mismatch

  Scenario: Failure case - announcement flooding is specified as a defect
    Given the replay fixture pinned to a 2000 messages per second window
    When the tape panel is focused with NVDA running and verbosity at default
    Then the plan requires announcements to be coalesced per 05-accessibility-standard.md section 6.2
    And continuous announcement of every print is recorded as a P0 defect, not a preference

  Scenario: Edge case - table alternative must not silently diverge
    Given a bar whose footprint cells include an imbalance-flagged cell
    When the same bar is read in SCR-045 and inspected on the SCR-030 canvas
    Then the plan requires numeric parity for price, bid, ask, delta and the imbalance flag
    And any divergence is a P0 defect because the table is the normative equivalent

  Scenario: Plan is reviewed and merged
    When the plan PR is opened
    Then it carries approvals from the Accessibility role and the SDET
    And it is linked from the E47 epic ticket and referenced by E47-T06
```

## Technical notes / design
- Structure by *observable surface and success criterion*, not by component; remediation will move code around and the plan must not need rewriting.
- Expected announcements are recorded as quoted strings with tolerated variance noted (for example, NVDA may prefix the role); this avoids arguments at execution time.
- The AT combos and their pinned versions come from `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8.1 - the plan references that table rather than duplicating versions, so the quarterly version bump happens in one place.
- Cases that depend on the high-contrast or CVD-safe themes must name the token pair under test so a failure can be handed straight to `E47-T03`'s contrast linter as a reproduction.
- Group 5 must use the replay fixture rather than live market data so the flash-rate observations are deterministic and re-runnable.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan; its own verification is a dry run. Execute group 1 and group 4 end-to-end against the current staging build, record execution timings, ambiguities and dead cases, then fix the plan before merge. Attach the dry-run log so "executable" is evidenced rather than asserted. Record the time taken per group; `E47-Q09` uses these figures to size the release-candidate regression window.

## Security notes
- Fixtures must use the demo environment only; no live API keys, no real account identifiers, no real P&L in any attached evidence, matching the redaction rule established in `E47-D02`.
- Group 2 must include a negative assertion: no live region, DOM mirror node or table export ever contains an API-key fragment, session token, account id or the full email of another user. Deeper adversarial versions live in `E47-X02`.
- Any screenshot or SR transcript attached to a case is reviewed for sensitive strings before it is committed.

## Accessibility notes
The deliverable is itself an accessibility artefact: the plan is a markdown document with a proper heading hierarchy, tables with header rows, and no information conveyed by colour alone (pass/fail is written as a word, never a coloured cell). The traceability table must be readable as plain text.

## Performance notes
The plan must state a time budget per group so a full pass fits inside the release-candidate window defined in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`. Group 2 is the expensive one (manual SR); the plan marks the minimum subset that must run for every RC versus the full pass that runs before GA.

## Observability
- Case results are recorded in the QA result store used by `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, tagged `epic:E47` and `criterion:<wcag-id>` so the conformance report can be generated by query rather than by hand.
- Defects filed carry the `a11y` label plus the screen id, feeding the burn-down dashboard maintained in `E47-Q04`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `qa/plans/e47-accessibility-test-plan.md` merged with all six groups, the fixture appendix and the traceability table.
- [ ] Dry-run log for groups 1 and 4 attached, with measured durations.
- [ ] Every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md` and every AA success criterion mapped or explicitly marked not applicable with a reason.
- [ ] Approved by the Accessibility role and the SDET; linked from the E47 epic and from `E47-T06`.
- [ ] Automation status column agreed with `E47-Q03` so there is no gap and no duplication.

## Dependencies
- `E47-D01` - contrast and CVD expectations must exist before group 4 can state expected results.
- `E47-D02` - the statement and report surfaces must be designed before group 6 can be written.

## Branch
`chore/e47-a11y-test-plan` (docs-only; PR well under the 400 LOC preference).

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3-10 (the normative source for every case).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 11 (per-feature test plans, severity taxonomy) and its accessibility-testing section.
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` (DoR/DoD gates, `a11y` label conditions).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (per-screen a11y notes; SCR-045, SCR-116, SCR-117 in particular).
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` (component a11y contracts).
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 27 SET (US-SET-001..009).
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` (traceability table conventions).
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` sections 9.2-9.3 (R5 scope and exit criterion 2).

## Agent execution brief

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Branch & PR**
