title: axe-core, pa11y and Lighthouse CI gates with a violation burn-down dashboard
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 items 1, 2 and 7 require axe-core to run against every screen on every frontend PR with zero new serious/critical violations as a merge blocker, a Lighthouse Accessibility score of at least 95 on every top-level screen tracked over time, and both to be required checks on `main` exactly like the security scans in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Moderate and minor violations are to be tracked as backlog with a burn-down.

Partial versions of these checks may exist from earlier epics as advisory steps. E47 is where they become enforcing, complete (every screen, not a sample) and visible (a dashboard the Accessibility role and the owner can read).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **axe-core via `@axe-core/playwright`** executed against every screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` that can be reached in a test harness, including modal, empty, error, degraded, disconnected and rate-limited states (SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-151..SCR-159) which are routinely missed by happy-path scans.
- A **baseline file** recording the currently-accepted moderate/minor violations, each with an owner, a ticket and a target date; the gate fails on any new serious/critical violation and on any regression above baseline.
- **pa11y-ci** configured as the secondary engine so rules axe does not implement are still covered; disagreement between engines is triaged rather than suppressed.
- **Lighthouse CI** on the tracked top-level screens (chart workspace SCR-020/030, order ticket SCR-060, positions SCR-063, admin users SCR-121, journal SCR-093, watchlist SCR-100, settings SCR-110, alerts SCR-090), asserting score >= 95 and storing the score history.
- **Burn-down dashboard**: a generated page (and a Grafana panel where the metric fits the existing stack) showing open a11y defects by severity, by screen and by WCAG criterion, plus the axe/Lighthouse/keyboard-suite trend; sourced from the same QA result store `E47-Q01` and `E47-Q02` write to.
- Suppression policy: a suppression requires an inline justification, an owner, an expiry date and a linked ticket; expired suppressions fail the build. No blanket rule disables.
- CI wiring as required checks on `main`, mirroring the security-gate placement in `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the violations - remediation stories own that.
- Keyboard journeys and a11y-tree snapshots - `E47-Q03`.
- Token contrast linting - that is `E47-T03`'s design-system CI job; this ticket only surfaces its result on the dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Automated accessibility gates and burn-down

  Scenario: Every screen is scanned, including its error and empty states
    Given the screen inventory from docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
    When the axe job runs
    Then every screen id appears in the scan report with a result
    And a screen absent from the report fails the job rather than passing silently

  Scenario: A new serious violation blocks merge
    Given a PR introducing an input without an accessible name
    When the axe gate runs
    Then the check fails naming the rule, the screen and the selector
    And the PR cannot be merged

  Scenario: Failure case - an expired suppression fails the build
    Given a suppression whose expiry date has passed
    When the gate runs
    Then the build fails with the suppression owner and ticket in the message

  Scenario: Edge case - a Lighthouse score drop is caught even when axe is clean
    Given a change that degrades heading structure without producing an axe violation
    When Lighthouse CI runs on the affected top-level screen
    Then the score falls below 95 and the build fails

  Scenario: The dashboard reflects reality
    Given defects filed by E47-Q01 and E47-Q02
    When the dashboard refreshes
    Then open counts by severity, screen and WCAG criterion match the QA result store
    And the burn-down trend is visible over at least the last four sprints
```

## Technical notes / design
- Screens are enumerated from a machine-readable inventory derived from the catalogue so "new screen, unscanned" is impossible; adding a screen without a scan entry fails CI. This inventory is the same one `E47-Q03` uses for snapshots.
- Error/empty/degraded states are reached via test hooks that force the state rather than by trying to provoke real failures, keeping the scan deterministic.
- Baseline entries are keyed by rule plus a stable selector path, not by DOM index, so trivial markup moves do not invalidate the baseline.
- Lighthouse runs against the built Electron-renderer bundle in headless Chromium matching the shell's Chromium version, per the standard section 9.2, otherwise scores are not comparable with the shipped surface.
- The dashboard reads the QA result store rather than parsing CI logs; log-scraping dashboards rot the first time output format changes.

## Test plan
- Fault injection: introduce one serious axe violation, one heading-structure regression and one expired suppression on a scratch branch; each must fail its respective gate with an actionable message.
- Determinism: run the axe job five times on an unchanged build; the violation set must be identical. Non-determinism (usually animation-dependent scans) is fixed by disabling motion during scans via the reduced-motion override.
- Verify the baseline genuinely blocks regressions by re-adding a baselined violation on a second screen and confirming failure.

## Security notes
- Scan reports embed DOM snippets. The report post-processor must redact values from fields that can hold secrets or personal data (API-key inputs on SCR-126/SCR-127, TOTP fields on SCR-002/SCR-003, email fields on SCR-121/SCR-123) before artefacts are uploaded.
- CI credentials for the scan harness are seeded demo users only; the harness must not be able to authenticate against the live environment.
- Dashboard access follows existing RBAC on observability surfaces; it exposes defect counts, not user data.

## Accessibility notes
The dashboard is itself held to the standard: it is one of the screens scanned, has a table with proper headers, conveys severity with text as well as colour, and its charts have an accessible table equivalent (the same rule the product applies to canvas surfaces).

## Performance notes
- The axe matrix across all screens is the slowest a11y job; shard by screen group so the per-PR envelope from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` is respected. Full-inventory scans may run on merge to `main` and nightly, with the per-PR job scoped to changed areas plus a fixed smoke set - this split must be documented, not implicit.
- Lighthouse runs on a pinned CI machine class; score comparisons across machine classes are meaningless and must be prevented by tagging results with the runner class.

## Observability
- Metrics published: `a11y_axe_violations{severity,screen}`, `a11y_lighthouse_score{screen}`, `a11y_open_defects{severity}`, `a11y_suppressions_active`, `a11y_suppressions_expiring_7d`.
- Alerting: a serious/critical violation reaching `main` (for example via an admin override) raises a notification to the Accessibility role.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] axe, pa11y-ci and Lighthouse CI jobs merged, covering the full screen inventory including non-happy-path states.
- [ ] Baseline file committed with owners, tickets and target dates; suppression policy enforced including expiry.
- [ ] Checks required on `main`; fault-injection evidence attached.
- [ ] Burn-down dashboard live and reading from the QA result store.
- [ ] Per-PR versus nightly scan split documented in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.
- [ ] Handover note to E48/E49 describing how a new screen joins the inventory.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q01` - the screen inventory and severity conventions come from the plan.

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-ci-gates`.

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 (items 1, 2, 3, 7).
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (gate placement pattern this mirrors).
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (where the scan split is documented).
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (CI budget, regression-gate philosophy).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (screen inventory, incl. SCR-151..SCR-159 state screens).

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e47-a11y-ci-gates`
- PR title: "E47-Q04: axe-core, pa11y and Lighthouse CI gates with a violation burn-down dashboard"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-Q04>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/test, area/design-system, priority/p0, qa, a11y

**Done means**
- axe, pa11y-ci and Lighthouse CI jobs merged, covering the full screen inventory including non-happy-path states.
- Baseline file committed with owners, tickets and target dates; suppression policy enforced including expiry.
- Checks required on `main`; fault-injection evidence attached.
- Burn-down dashboard live and reading from the QA result store.
- Per-PR versus nightly scan split documented in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Handover note to E48/E49 describing how a new screen joins the inventory.

**Do NOT**
- Fixing the violations - remediation stories own that.
- Keyboard journeys and a11y-tree snapshots - `E47-Q03`.
- Token contrast linting - that is `E47-T03`'s design-system CI job; this ticket only surfaces its result on the dashboard.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-Q04` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Accessibility preferences applied everywhere incl. WebGL (SCR-117)
body:
## Context
**US-SET-007 Accessibility preferences (Must)** is the one SET story whose whole subject is accessibility, and its NFR is the demanding part: "preferences persist per user and apply immediately across all views **including WebGL surfaces**". A preference that reflows the DOM but leaves the canvas animating, or that requires a reload, fails the story.

**SCR-117** enumerates the option set: reduced motion, disable canvas animation, always show data-table alternatives, increase focus-ring thickness, announce price updates (off / on significant change / always), screen-reader verbosity for the tape, keyboard-only mode (disables drag-only interactions and reveals their form equivalents), and a link to the accessibility statement. Its catalogue entry also sets the bar for the screen itself: "This screen is itself the exemplar" and "the page passes its own standard at 200% zoom".

## Scope / Deliverables
- The preference model as a scoped key set inside the existing `settings` JSONB document, read/written via `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings` and mirrored on `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`; per-user scope, applied on load and on change without a reload.
- **SCR-117** built/remediated to the catalogue spec: every control has a visible persistent label plus a plain-language description of its effect; OS-level `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-contrast` detection shown as the default with an explicit override; the announcement-throttle control; links to the accessibility statement and the hotkey cheatsheet (**SCR-013**).
- Propagation: a single preference context consumed by DOM components *and* by the engine — canvas animation, heatmap fade, chart inertia and flash-on-tick all read the same flags; changing a flag takes effect on the next frame.
- `keyboard-only mode`: drag-only affordances hide and their discrete equivalents (nudge controls, numeric position fields, "…" repositioning menus) are revealed across chart drawings, order lines, node editor and panel resize.
- `always show data-table alternatives`: panels default to their table view (SCR-045 and the order-flow equivalents) without re-fetching data.
- Verbosity and announce-price-updates settings feed the live-region throttling used by **E47-S01** and **E47-S02**.
- Components: CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-086 SettingsNav/SettingsLayout, CMP-228 PreviewTile.

## Out of scope
- Theme and density selection — **SCR-116** / **E47-S06** (US-SET-004, US-SET-005).
- Performance profile settings — **SCR-118**, US-SET-008, **E46**.
- Adding preferences beyond the SCR-117 option set.
- Server-side enforcement of any preference (they are presentation-only).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A preference applies immediately, canvas included
  Given the chart is animating and the heatmap is fading
  When "disable canvas animation" is enabled on SCR-117
  Then within one frame the canvas stops animating and the heatmap updates instantly
  And no reload or re-subscription occurs

Scenario: OS preference is the default, not the ceiling
  Given the operating system reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then the reduced-motion control shows "On (from system)" as its default
  And an explicit user override to "Off" is honoured and persisted

Scenario: Verbosity limits announcements
  Given screen-reader verbosity is set to low
  When prices tick rapidly
  Then the live region announces only significant events rather than every update
  And raising verbosity restores per-cadence announcements without a reload

Scenario: Keyboard-only mode reveals the alternatives
  When keyboard-only mode is enabled
  Then drag-only affordances are hidden and their discrete equivalents are visible on chart drawings, order lines, node editor and panel resize

Scenario: Preferences persist per user
  Given preferences are changed and the app is restarted
  Then the same preferences are restored for that user and are unchanged for any other user

Scenario: The screen passes its own standard
  Then SCR-117 at 200% zoom shows no clipping or lost functionality
  And axe reports zero serious or critical violations on it

Scenario: A failed save does not silently lie
  Given the settings API returns an error on save
  Then the failure is announced and the control reverts to its persisted value with a retry offered
```

## Technical notes / design
One preference context, two consumers: React components subscribe directly; the engine receives a flags message on change so the worker/render loop reads plain booleans rather than querying React. Defaults derive from OS media queries evaluated at load and re-evaluated on change, with an explicit "user override" tri-state (`system` / `on` / `off`) so an override is distinguishable from a coincidence. Disabling animation must remove the transition work from the frame budget — a measurable reduction, per the SCR-117 performance note, not a no-op that merely sets duration to zero on a still-running loop.

## Test plan
Unit: tri-state resolution against media-query changes; flags propagation to the engine message. Integration: preference change while streaming, asserting no re-subscription. E2E keyboard-only: traverse and set every control on SCR-117. Visual/perf: frame-time measurement before and after disabling animation, asserting a real reduction. Gates: axe, Lighthouse, a11y-tree snapshot on SCR-117 at 100% and 200% zoom.

## Security notes
Preferences are per-user and written through the authenticated settings endpoint; the API must reject writes scoped to another user's id. Preference values are a closed enum set — no free-form values are persisted or echoed. No preference may disable a security-relevant confirm, the arm-token requirement, or the LIVE/DEMO badge.

## Accessibility notes
This screen is the exemplar per SCR-117: persistent labels, effect descriptions, state announced on change, 200% zoom clean. Implements `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2 (announcement throttling as a user-configurable cadence), §7 (reduced motion), §3.4.6 (focus-ring thickness). WCAG SCs: 1.4.4, 1.4.10, 1.4.12, 2.4.7, 3.2.2, 3.3.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Preference propagation must not cause a full re-render of the workspace; the engine receives flags, not a scene rebuild. Enabling every accommodation at once must stay within the 1 ms/frame ceiling stated on the Epic; measure with the E46 harness and report the before/after frame time as evidence for the SCR-117 claim.

## Observability

title: Full WCAG 2.2 AA sweep of SCR-001..SCR-159 into a findings register
body:
## Context
This is the audit itself: the single pass over every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md` that turns "we followed the standard" into a list of specific, reproducible defects with WCAG success-criterion references. `30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 names it first in E47's scope ("Full WCAG 2.2 AA audit of every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md`"), and §9.3 exit criterion 2 requires per-screen evidence.

The method and finding schema come from **E47-K01**; the automated gates from **E47-T02** have already pre-populated the easy half. What this Task adds is coverage of what automation cannot judge: announcement quality, focus intent, whether an offscreen mirror actually corresponds to what is drawn, whether a dense grid is navigable in practice rather than in principle, and the six WCAG 2.2-specific criteria (2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8) that tooling detects poorly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the sweep across **SCR-001…SCR-159** and their enumerated states, per the K01 plan: automated pass for every screen/state; deep manual pass for the canvas, dense, destructive and authentication surfaces (**SCR-001…SCR-006**, **SCR-030**, **SCR-032**, **SCR-045**, **SCR-050**, **SCR-052**, **SCR-053**, **SCR-060/061**, **SCR-063**, **SCR-064**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-074/075/076**, **SCR-081**, **SCR-082**, **SCR-090**, **SCR-093**, **SCR-097**, **SCR-113**, **SCR-116**, **SCR-117**, **SCR-121**, **SCR-135**, **SCR-143**, **SCR-152**, **SCR-156**).
- Record every finding in the checked-in register with: screen id, CMP id where applicable, WCAG SC and level, severity, reproduction steps, detection source, and the remediation ticket it is assigned to.
- Group findings by **pattern** (canvas surrogate, roving-tabindex grid, dialog focus-return, motion token, colour-only encoding, target size, drag-only interaction, label/name mismatch) and assign each group to one of **E47-S01…S06**; anything that fits no group and is small becomes a directly-attached remediation item on this Task.
- Produce the per-screen conformance matrix skeleton (one row per screen, columns for each evidence type) that **E47-T05** publishes.
- Triage: every Level A finding is P0/P1 and must be fixed in R5; AA findings are sized and either scheduled or nominated as exceptions with a compensating control proposal.

## Out of scope
- Remediation of grouped findings — **E47-S01…S06**.
- The manual screen-reader *sign-off* passes — **E47-T04** runs the pinned matrix after remediation; this sweep uses SR only as a detection instrument.
- Non-accessibility design-QA findings (spacing, token drift, copy) — routed to **E49**.
- Bugs in feature behaviour discovered incidentally — filed as ordinary bugs against the owning epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Coverage is complete and provable
  When the sweep closes
  Then every screen from SCR-001 to SCR-159 has at least one register entry or an explicit "no findings" record
  And every state listed in the screen's catalogue entry is marked covered or marked unreachable with a reason

Scenario: A finding is actionable by someone who did not find it
  Given any register entry
  Then it states the WCAG success criterion and level, exact reproduction steps, the observed and expected behaviour
  And a second engineer can reproduce it from the entry alone

Scenario: WCAG 2.2-specific criteria are explicitly checked
  Then each of 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7 and 3.3.8 has a recorded check result per applicable screen
  And these are not inferred from the axe result, which does not fully cover them

Scenario: Level A findings cannot be deferred
  Given a finding is classified Level A
  Then it is assigned priority P0 or P1 and a remediation ticket in R5
  And it cannot be moved to the exception register

Scenario: Duplicates collapse into patterns
  Given the same defect appears on eight screens
  Then it is recorded once as a pattern finding listing all eight screens
  And remediation is scheduled against the shared component, not eight times
```

## Technical notes / design
The register is the Epic's spine: E47-S01…S06 are scoped *by* it, E47-T05 is generated *from* it, and E49 consumes its leftovers. Keeping it as a checked-in structured file (schema from K01) is what makes the published report reproducible months later. Pattern grouping is done during the sweep, not after — retrofitting grouping onto 300 flat findings is where audits usually lose a sprint.

## Test plan
Quality control on the audit itself: 10% of screens are re-audited by a second auditor and inter-rater agreement is recorded; disagreements are adjudicated by the Accessibility role and the criteria clarified in the method doc. Automated results are cross-checked against manual results on the deep-pass screens to calibrate what automation is missing.

## Security notes
The sweep runs in the demo environment against synthetic accounts; reproduction steps must not embed live credentials, account ids or API keys. Findings on authentication screens (**SCR-001…SCR-006**, **SCR-149**) are handled with the same care as security findings — no screenshots of tokens, and 3.3.8 checks must not weaken 2FA requirements.

## Accessibility notes
The deep-pass protocol follows `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2 task scripts and §3/§4/§5/§6/§7 rules. Auditors record not just "does it pass" but "is the announced text useful" — a technically-labelled control that announces "button button" is a finding even if axe is silent.

## Performance notes
The automated portion must fit the nightly budget established in E47-T02. During the deep passes, record any case where the DOM mirror or live regions visibly lag the canvas — those become E46 tickets rather than being absorbed silently.

## Observability
Register metrics published per build: open findings by level and severity, findings per screen band, pattern-group sizes; a burn-down chart that GA readiness is judged against.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Register complete for all 159 screens with covered/unreachable state accounting.
- [ ] Findings grouped into patterns and assigned to remediation tickets.
- [ ] Conformance matrix skeleton generated.
- [ ] Inter-rater check executed on ≥10% of screens with results recorded.
- [ ] Level A findings all scheduled; AA exception nominations documented with compensating controls.
- [ ] Accessibility role and QA lead sign off that the sweep is complete.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-K01** (method and schema), **E47-T02** (gates pre-populate and prevent drift during the sweep). Blocks **E47-S01**, **E47-S02**, **E47-S03**, **E47-S05**; feeds **E47-T05** and **E49**.

title: Promote the six accessibility CI gates to required checks
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §9 specifies six automated gates and §9.7 requires them to be *required checks* on `main` per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`. Through R0–R4 several of them have run advisory (reporting without blocking) so that feature trains were not stopped by pre-existing violations. R5 exit criterion 2 depends on those gates being real: a published conformance report is worthless if the next merge can silently break it.

This Task flips them on. It runs early in the Epic on purpose — the gates then *find* much of what **E47-T01** would otherwise have to find by hand, and they immediately prevent remediation work from being undone by parallel E46/E48/E49 work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **axe-core** (Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright`) across every screen state: fail on any new serious/critical violation; existing moderate/minor violations captured into the findings register with a baseline file so the gate blocks *regressions* from day one and *absolute* violations once E47-T01's remediation lands.
- **Lighthouse accessibility ≥95** on the tracked top-level screens (chart workspace SCR-020/030, order ticket SCR-060, positions SCR-063, admin users SCR-121, journal SCR-093, watchlist SCR-100), run against the built Electron-renderer bundle in headless Chromium.
- **Contrast-token linter** on any change to design-system token files, validating text, non-text and chart data-ink pairs for the dark, light and high-contrast themes (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §5.4).
- **Keyboard-only E2E** suite: no mouse events dispatched, driving the §8.2 task script (submit an order in demo, switch symbol, toggle the SCR-045 table view, trigger the reduced-motion override).
- **Motion/flash audit script**: frame-capture + luminance-delta analysis against heatmap, big-trade bubbles and price-flash at a fixed high-tick-rate fixture, asserting <3 flashes/second (§7.3).
- **Accessibility-tree snapshot** diff per top-level screen, reviewable in the PR.
- Branch-protection configuration updated so all six are required; a documented, time-limited break-glass path for an infrastructure outage (not for a genuine violation).

## Out of scope
- Fixing the violations the gates surface — that is the remediation Stories' job; this Task only establishes the baseline and the block.
- Performance budget gates — **E46**.
- Adding new screens to the tracked Lighthouse set beyond the six named (a deliberate cost decision; the axe gate covers the rest).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A regression is blocked
  Given main is green
  When a PR introduces a serious axe violation on any in-scope screen
  Then the axe check fails, the merge queue rejects the PR, and the output names the screen, rule and node

Scenario: The baseline cannot be silently widened
  When a PR modifies the axe baseline file
  Then CODEOWNERS requires the Accessibility role's review on that file
  And the PR description must state which finding id justifies the change

Scenario: Infrastructure failure is distinguishable from a violation
  Given the Lighthouse runner cannot start
  Then the check reports an infrastructure error distinct from a score failure
  And the documented break-glass path is usable without disabling the gate for violations

Scenario: Flash threshold is enforced on a realistic fixture
  Given the high-tick-rate fixture is replayed against the heatmap and bubble components
  When luminance deltas are analysed
  Then any component exceeding 3 flashes per second fails the build with the offending component named

Scenario: Gate runtime stays affordable
  Then the combined per-PR accessibility gate wall-clock time is under 12 minutes
  And the full nightly sweep is under 20 minutes
```

## Technical notes / design
Baselining is the crux: a hard "zero violations" flip on day one would block every unrelated PR in R5 and would be waived within a day, which is worse than not having the gate. So: snapshot current violations into a reviewed baseline file, block anything new immediately, and shrink the baseline to empty as **E47-S01…S06** land. The baseline file is CODEOWNERS-protected so shrinking is the only easy direction. Accessibility-tree snapshots are stored as text so PR diffs are human-reviewable.

## Test plan
Meta-tests: deliberately inject a keyboard trap, a colour-only status, a 5 Hz flash and a contrast-failing token in a scratch branch and assert each gate fails with an actionable message; assert a clean branch passes. Measure gate runtime on the CI runner class actually used.

## Security notes
Gate runs use a demo-environment build with synthetic fixtures — never live credentials. Lighthouse/axe artefacts (HTML reports, traces) may embed page content and are retained only on the internal CI artefact store with the same retention as other build artefacts, not published.

## Accessibility notes
Gate output itself must be readable: failures are reported as text in the check summary (screen, rule, selector, WCAG SC), not only as an attached HTML report or screenshot.

## Performance notes
Gates run in parallel with the existing test matrix; the nightly full sweep runs off the PR path. If the per-PR budget is exceeded, the axe sweep is sharded by screen band rather than sampled — sampling would make the gate non-deterministic.

## Observability
Per-build metrics: axe violation count by severity, Lighthouse a11y score per tracked screen, keyboard-E2E pass rate, baseline file size. Dashboard panel plus an alert when the baseline file grows.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six checks configured as required on `main` with break-glass documented.
- [ ] Baseline file committed, CODEOWNERS-protected, and its shrink-only policy documented in `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`.
- [ ] Meta-tests for all six gates pass (injected defect fails, clean branch passes).
- [ ] Runtime budgets measured and recorded.
- [ ] `05-accessibility-standard.md` §9 updated to reflect the gates as shipped.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: none (runs first deliberately). Feeds **E47-T01** by pre-populating the findings register; constrains **E47-S01…S06**, **E46**, **E48**, **E49**.

## Branch
`chore/e47-a11y-required-checks`

title: Contrast and colour-vision validation matrix for every theme and data-ink token
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §5.4 requires that candle body/wick colours, footprint cell background+text pairs, heatmap gradient stops and profile-histogram bars each independently meet 3:1 against the chart background **at every point in the gradient**, validated by an automated script producing a pass/fail matrix per token pair — "not just spot-checked visually". §4.2 additionally requires deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulation of every buy/sell and heatmap palette.

Today the design system validates the *chrome* palette. What has never been validated end-to-end is the **data-ink** palette: the continuous gradients the order-flow surfaces use, which are generated at runtime and were exempt from the token linter because they are not discrete tokens. That exemption is exactly where a conformance report gets challenged.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Extend the contrast validator to sample **continuous gradients** (heatmap intensity ramp, delta divergence ramp, profile histogram fill, liquidation intensity) at N stops (N≥16, configurable) and evaluate each against the theme background, failing if any stop falls below 3:1.
- Cover all three themes: dark (default), light, high-contrast (`Ctrl+Shift+H`, §5.6, ≥7:1 body text) — plus both density modes, since compact density changes text sizes and therefore the applicable ratio (§5.1 large-text threshold).
- Cover the **CVD-safe palettes** shipped under US-SET-005: each alternative palette is validated to the same bar, not just the default.
- Produce the machine-readable pass/fail matrix (token pair × theme × density) checked in and consumed by **E47-T05**'s report.
- Add CVD simulation output (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) for buy/sell, bid/ask and imbalance encodings, with a discriminability assertion between the paired colours after simulation — a pair that collapses to the same simulated colour fails.
- Wire both into the **E47-T02** contrast-linter gate.

## Out of scope
- Changing palettes to fix failures — that is **E47-S06**; this Task produces the evidence and the failing list.
- The no-hue-alone structural rule (glyphs, signs, patterns) — audited under **E47-S06** and **E47-T01**.
- Print/export colour fidelity.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every gradient stop is evaluated
  Given the heatmap intensity ramp is defined for the dark theme
  When the validator runs
  Then at least 16 sampled stops are each evaluated against the chart background
  And a single failing stop fails the whole ramp with the stop's position and ratio reported

Scenario: CVD-collapsing pairs are caught
  Given the buy and sell tokens under deuteranopia simulation
  When their simulated values differ by less than the configured discriminability threshold
  Then the pair fails with both simulated values reported

Scenario: High-contrast theme is held to its own bar
  Given the high-contrast theme is selected
  Then body-text pairs are evaluated at 7:1, not 4.5:1
  And a pair passing AA but failing the high-contrast bar fails only in that theme's column

Scenario: The matrix is generated, never hand-maintained
  When the token files change
  Then the matrix file is regenerated in CI and a stale checked-in matrix fails the build

Scenario: Compact density does not silently lower the bar
  Given compact density reduces a label below the large-text threshold
  Then that pair is evaluated at 4.5:1 rather than 3:1 in the compact column
```

## Technical notes / design
Gradients are evaluated by sampling the same interpolation function the renderer uses — importing it, not reimplementing it — so the matrix cannot drift from what is drawn. Contrast uses the WCAG relative-luminance formula; CVD uses a standard published transform matrix, with the chosen transform and its source recorded so results are defensible. Discriminability threshold is a documented, reviewed constant, not a magic number.

## Test plan
Unit tests for the luminance and CVD transforms against published reference values. Fixture tests: a deliberately failing ramp and a deliberately CVD-collapsing pair must both fail; a known-good pair must pass. Snapshot test on the generated matrix.

## Security notes
None beyond standard supply-chain hygiene for any colour-science dependency added (pinned, SCA-scanned); prefer a small vendored transform over a large transitive dependency.

## Accessibility notes
This Task is a direct implementation of §4.2 and §5.4. The generated matrix is a text/markdown table with explicit pass/fail words, not a colour-coded grid — the accessibility evidence must itself not depend on colour.

## Performance notes
Matrix generation must complete in under 60 s so it can run on every token change; gradient sampling is pure computation with no rendering.

## Observability
CI metric: count of failing pairs per theme, trended per build so palette work is visibly converging.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Validator covers discrete tokens and continuous gradients across three themes and two densities.
- [ ] CVD simulation with discriminability assertion implemented and unit-tested against reference values.
- [ ] Matrix generated in CI, checked in, and consumed by the conformance report.
- [ ] Wired into the required contrast-linter gate from E47-T02.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` updated with the validated palette status and the transform used.

## Dependencies

title: STRIDE threat model for a11y surfaces: mirrors, live regions, preferences
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` require a STRIDE threat model per epic. E47 looks benign - it is "just" accessibility - but it introduces a genuinely new attack surface: a **parallel representation of every piece of data on screen**. The DOM mirror (standard section 6.1), the ARIA live regions (6.2) and the table alternatives (6.3) re-express canvas-rendered market data, order state, account P&L and admin content as DOM text. Any control applied to the visual surface that is not also applied to the mirror is a bypass.

The epic also adds persisted user preferences (SCR-116, SCR-117) written through `PUT /api/v1/me/preferences` and hotkey profiles via `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*`, backed by the `settings` and `hotkey_profiles` tables, plus a published accessibility statement and conformance report (`E47-D02`, `E47-T06`) that are, by design, documents describing exactly how the system behaves.

There is also a safety-critical interaction: accessibility affordances must never weaken trading-safety controls. The Demo/Live distinction (SCR-074, SCR-075), destructive-action confirmations (US-SET-003), the arming flow (`/settings/arm`) and the RBAC-gated admin screens all have accessible equivalents that must carry the same guarantees.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model (`docs/security/threat-models/e47-accessibility.md`) over a data-flow diagram covering: canvas -> DOM mirror -> AT; event -> live region -> AT; table alternative -> clipboard/export; preference UI -> `/api/v1/me/preferences` -> `settings` table; hotkey profile UI -> `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*` -> `hotkey_profiles` table; statement/report content -> renderer.
- Per STRIDE category, at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: an accessible name or announcement that misrepresents environment (Demo announced where Live is active) or account identity; focus-visible styling faked by content.
  - **Tampering**: a persisted preference or hotkey profile modified so a destructive action loses its confirmation, or a hotkey rebound onto a trading action; injection of markup into mirror text.
  - **Repudiation**: a preference change (for example disabling confirmations or widening arming) that is not audited, leaving no record of who weakened a control.
  - **Information disclosure**: mirror or live-region text exposing data the visual surface redacts (masked API-key fragments on SCR-127/SCR-128, other users' emails on SCR-121, balances for accounts outside the user's `user_account_access`); table export (`Ctrl+C` TSV on SCR-045) as an exfiltration path; the conformance report disclosing internal architecture.
  - **Denial of service**: announcement flooding and unbounded mirror growth as a client-side DoS; a table alternative materialising an unbounded range.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a viewer reaching an owner-only control because it is present-but-hidden visually yet exposed in the accessibility tree, or a keyboard path that skips the SCR-149 admin re-authentication gate.
- Ranked findings with owners, each mapped to a mitigation in a specific ticket (`E47-S0x`, `E47-X02`, `E47-X03`) or accepted with a recorded rationale.
- A control checklist handed to `E47-X04` for the review, and to `E47-Q03`/`E47-Q06` as assertions where mechanically checkable.

## Out of scope
- Threat modelling of the underlying trading, auth and admin functionality - owned by their own epics' models; this model assumes those controls exist and asks only whether the accessible surface preserves them.
- Penetration testing - performed before R4 live enablement per the security program; this is a design-time analysis.
- Abuse-case construction and exploit attempts - `E47-X02`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: STRIDE threat model for E47

  Scenario: Every data flow is modelled
    Given the data-flow diagram in the model
    When it is compared with the surfaces E47 introduces
    Then the mirror, live-region, table-alternative, preference and hotkey flows each appear with trust boundaries marked

  Scenario: Every category yields a considered result
    Given the six STRIDE categories
    When the model is reviewed
    Then each category has at least one analysed threat with a rating and a disposition
    And a category dismissed as not applicable states why

  Scenario: Failure case - parity gap between visual and accessible surfaces
    Given a field masked in the visual UI
    When the accessible representation is analysed
    And the mirror or live region would expose the unmasked value
    Then the finding is rated high and assigned to a remediation ticket before GA

  Scenario: Edge case - a preference that weakens a safety control is audited
    Given a user disables destructive-action confirmations or increases arming scope
    When the model analyses repudiation
    Then an audit-log requirement is specified for that preference change
    And its absence is filed as a finding

  Scenario: The model is reviewed and owned
    When the model PR is opened
    Then it is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Accessibility role
    And every finding has an owner and a disposition of mitigate, transfer or accept with rationale
```

## Technical notes / design
- Trust boundaries: the AT process is outside the app's process boundary - text handed to a screen reader leaves the application's control entirely (it may be spoken aloud in a shared room, logged by AT software, or routed to a braille display). That physical-context exposure is a real consideration for a product displaying account balances, and belongs in the model rather than being waved away.
- The mirror must be derived from the *same authorisation-filtered data* the renderer receives, never from a pre-filter source. A finding template is provided for reviewers to check this per surface.
- Hotkey rebinding is a genuine tampering vector precisely because E47 expands keyboard reach; the model must consider whether any single keystroke can reach an irreversible trading action without confirmation, tying back to US-SET-002 and US-SET-003.
- Follow the existing model template and rating scale in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` so E47's findings aggregate with other epics' rather than using a bespoke scale.

## Test plan
- The model is validated by a walkthrough with the frontend a11y engineer and the Security engineer, tracing three concrete scenarios end-to-end: a viewer opening a chart on a permitted symbol, a manager opening the admin users screen, and an owner rotating an API key on SCR-127 - each read entirely through the accessible surface.
- Every mechanically checkable mitigation is written as an assertion into `E47-Q03` or `E47-Q06` and confirmed to fail on a deliberately vulnerable build.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis. Two standing conclusions must be stated explicitly even if no finding materialises: (1) the accessibility surface is subject to the same RBAC and data scoping as the visual surface, with no exception; (2) no accessibility accommodation may remove a confirmation, an arming step or the Demo/Live signal - accommodations may change modality, never remove a control. Both become review criteria in `E47-X04`.

## Accessibility notes
The model must not produce mitigations that degrade accessibility - "do not mirror sensitive screens" is not an acceptable mitigation, because it would make those screens unusable with a screen reader. Correct mitigations preserve equivalent access while applying the same protections the visual surface has. This constraint is written into the model's ground rules.

## Performance notes
The DoS analysis overlaps with `E47-Q05`: announcement flooding and unbounded mirror growth are simultaneously an availability threat and a performance defect. The model references the measured budgets rather than inventing separate thresholds.

## Observability
- Findings are tracked in the security findings register per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, tagged `epic:E47`.
- Any mitigation implemented as an audit-log requirement must specify the event name and fields so the admin audit screens (SCR-135, SCR-136) can surface it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Threat model merged with a data-flow diagram, trust boundaries and all six STRIDE categories analysed.
- [ ] Findings rated, owned and dispositioned; mitigations mapped to tickets.
- [ ] Walkthrough completed with the three traced scenarios recorded.
- [ ] Mechanically checkable mitigations written into `E47-Q03` / `E47-Q06`.
- [ ] Control checklist handed to `E47-X04`.
- [ ] Reviewed and approved by the Security engineer and the Accessibility role.

## Dependencies
- `E47-D01`, `E47-D02` - the designed surfaces (themes, statement, report) define part of what is modelled.

## Branch
`chore/e47-threat-model` (docs-only).

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE template, rating scale, findings register).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3.2-3.3 (hotkeys), 6.1-6.3 (mirror, live regions, table alternative).
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/me/preferences`, `/settings`, `/settings/arm`, `/settings/hotkeys`, `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}`, `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}/activate`.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` `settings`, `hotkey_profiles`, `users`, `user_account_access`.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-045, SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-116, SCR-117, SCR-121, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-135, SCR-136, SCR-149.
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-002, US-SET-003, US-SET-007.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e47-threat-model`
- PR title: "E47-X01: STRIDE threat model for a11y surfaces: mirrors, live regions, preferences"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-X01>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/security, area/design-system, priority/p1, security, a11y

**Done means**

- Findings rated, owned and dispositioned; mitigations mapped to tickets.
- Walkthrough completed with the three traced scenarios recorded.
- Mechanically checkable mitigations written into `E47-Q03` / `E47-Q06`.
- Control checklist handed to `E47-X04`.
- Reviewed and approved by the Security engineer and the Accessibility role.

**Do NOT**
- Threat modelling of the underlying trading, auth and admin functionality - owned by their own epics' models; this model assumes those controls exist and asks only whether the accessible surface preserves them.
- Penetration testing - performed before R4 live enablement per the security program; this is a design-time analysis.
- Abuse-case construction and exploit attempts - `E47-X02`.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

title: Manual screen-reader passes across the NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver matrix
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8 defines a pinned screen-reader coverage matrix (NVDA 2024.x in the Electron shell as the P0 release blocker, JAWS 2024.x as a P1 that must fully pass before R4, Chromium+NVDA as the fast-iteration gate, VoiceOver on macOS 14 as a P1 that must fully pass before GA) and a manual protocol: setup, landmark/structure pass, task-based pass, regression checklist, severity bar. R5 is the release where those "before GA" obligations come due.

Automation cannot substitute here. axe-core does not know whether a fill announcement arrives before the user has moved on, whether the DOM mirror of a footprint grid is *comprehensible*, or whether the node-graph rule editor can actually be operated by a blind user. This ticket executes the human passes and turns them into defects and evidence.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Full execution of the standard section 8.2 protocol on the release-candidate build for each matrix row:
  - Row 1 (Electron + NVDA, Windows 11): **full pass**, all six task scripts, every top-level screen's landmark/heading structure.
  - Row 2 (Electron + JAWS): **full pass** - the R4 obligation is re-verified here plus the R5 delta.
  - Row 4 (macOS 14 + VoiceOver): **full pass** - this is the GA gate that has never been run in full.
  - Row 3 (Chromium headless/manual + NVDA): spot-check only, to confirm the CI surface still matches the shell.
- Task scripts executed keyboard+SR only, from the standard section 8.2 item 3 and extended for E47 scope: symbol switch from the watchlist (SCR-100 -> SCR-030); limit order placement on SCR-060 including the SCR-076 confirmation; footprint navigation via the DOM mirror and independently via SCR-045; simulated rule-engine flatten with the position-closed announcement (SCR-063, SCR-087); Demo -> Live switch on SCR-074 with the SCR-075 badge change; admin user creation and permission scope assignment on SCR-121/SCR-122; alert creation and trigger on SCR-091/SCR-092; both rule editors on SCR-081 and SCR-082.
- A **transcript** per task per AT: keystrokes issued and announcements heard, in a plain-text log committed under `qa/evidence/e47/<at>-<date>/`.
- Defect filing for every finding with the `a11y` label, the screen id, the WCAG criterion, the AT and version, severity per the standard section 8.2 item 5, and a reproduction that names keystrokes.
- An updated **living regression checklist** (the file referenced by `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`) recording what was checked, what changed since the previous pass, and the pinned AT versions used.
- A pass summary table feeding `E47-T06` (the conformance report) and `E47-Q09` (sign-off): screen x AT x verdict x blocking defects.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects found - remediation is `E47-S01`..`E47-S04` and follow-on tickets.
- Automated axe/Lighthouse/keyboard-E2E execution (`E47-Q03`, `E47-Q04`).
- Any mobile screen reader (TalkBack, iOS VoiceOver) - no mobile client is in scope.
- Non-Electron browsers as production targets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Manual screen-reader conformance passes

  Scenario: NVDA full pass completes on the release candidate
    Given the RC Electron build on Windows 11 23H2 with NVDA 2024.x at default verbosity
    And the tester uses no pointing device for the entire pass
    When every task in the E47 task script is attempted
    Then each task is either completed with correct announcements or filed as a defect
    And a transcript exists for every task

  Scenario: VoiceOver GA gate is executed for the first time in full
    Given the RC Electron build on macOS 14 Sonnoma or later with VoiceOver
    When the full protocol is executed
    Then a verdict is recorded per screen
    And any macOS-only defect is filed separately from its Windows equivalent

  Scenario: Failure case - a task cannot be completed keyboard and SR only
    Given the node-graph rule editor on SCR-082
    When the tester attempts to connect two nodes without a pointing device
    And no documented non-drag equivalent is discoverable
    Then a P0 release-blocking defect is filed against that screen
    And E47-T06 records the screen as non-conformant until the defect is closed

  Scenario: Edge case - streaming data does not steal focus
    Given the tester is midway through the SCR-060 order ticket with the tape streaming
    When a burst of market updates arrives
    Then focus remains on the control the tester left it on
    And any silent focus move is a P0 defect regardless of cause

  Scenario: Regression checklist is updated and versions are pinned
    When the passes complete
    Then the living regression checklist records the exact AT and OS versions used
    And any AT version drift from the standard section 8.1 matrix is recorded as a dated changelog entry
```

## Technical notes / design
- Each pass starts from a **fresh profile** with the default hotkey map and default theme, per the protocol; a pass run on a customised profile is void.
- The replay fixture from `E47-Q01` is used for any task that needs market motion, so two testers on two machines observe the same data.
- JAWS and NVDA disagree on table and grid verbosity; the plan records the AT-specific expected behaviour rather than treating a difference as a defect by default. The rule is: information must be *obtainable*, not identical.
- VoiceOver in Electron historically needs `NSAccessibility` activation; the setup section of the log records the exact launch flags used so the pass is reproducible.
- Findings on canvas surfaces are triaged against the three-layer strategy in the standard section 6 - a missing mirror node is an engine defect (`E47-S02`), a wrong announcement policy is a live-region defect.

## Test plan
The pass is the test. Its own quality gate is a **calibration exercise**: two testers independently run task 3 (footprint navigation) on the same build; their verdicts must agree, and any disagreement is resolved by the Accessibility role and written back into `E47-Q01` as a clarified expected result before the main pass proceeds.

## Security notes
- Passes run against the demo environment. Live credentials are never used, so no real order can be emitted by a tester exploring the order ticket.
- The Demo -> Live switch task is executed against a demo-flagged build where the "Live" target is a sandbox, so the badge and confirm behaviour is exercised without live trading capability.
- Transcripts are scanned for secrets before commit; any accidental capture of a key fragment, token or real account id is scrubbed and reported per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` incident handling.

## Accessibility notes
This entire ticket is accessibility work. Two constraints on the work itself: at least one pass should be run or co-run by a tester who uses a screen reader daily (engaged via the UX research function) rather than only by sighted testers simulating; and evidence artefacts (transcripts, checklists) are plain text so they are themselves accessible.

## Performance notes
The streaming-announcement tasks double as a perceived-performance check: if the DOM mirror or live-region updates cause the UI to stutter under the replay fixture, that is filed as a perf defect against `E47-Q05` rather than dismissed as an AT quirk. The standard's budget is that mirror and live-region work shares the frame budget discipline of `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
- Verdicts land in the QA result store tagged `epic:E47`, `at:<nvda|jaws|voiceover>`, `screen:<SCR-id>`, so the conformance report and the burn-down dashboard both read from one source.
- The pass summary is posted to the release-candidate checklist in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` as a PRR input.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver full passes executed on the RC build, with transcripts committed.
- [ ] Every finding filed with severity, AT, version, screen and WCAG criterion.
- [ ] Living regression checklist updated with the pinned versions and the delta since the previous pass.
- [ ] Calibration exercise completed and any clarified expectations written back into `E47-Q01`.
- [ ] Pass summary table handed to `E47-T06` and `E47-Q09`.
- [ ] Accessibility role signs the passes.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q01` - the task script and expected announcements come from the plan.
- `E47-S01`, `E47-S02` - remediation of the chrome and canvas layers must land or the pass degenerates into re-finding known defects.

## Branch
`chore/e47-sr-passes` (evidence and checklist only; no product code).

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 6 (canvas strategy), 8.1 (matrix), 8.2 (protocol), 8.3 (ownership).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (manual SR cadence, living regression checklist).
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (RC checklist and PRR gates).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-050, SCR-060, SCR-074, SCR-081, SCR-082, SCR-121.
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (DOM-mirror sync API and canvas aria requirements).
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (evidence handling, incident reporting).

## Agent execution brief

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Branch & PR**

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-Q02>`

title: Keyboard-only Playwright E2E suite and accessibility-tree snapshot regression
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 items 4 and 6 mandate two automated gates that do not exist yet: a **keyboard-only E2E smoke suite** that never dispatches a mouse event and drives the section 8.2 task script programmatically, and a **focus-order/landmark accessibility-tree snapshot** per top-level screen, diffed on every PR so semantic regressions surface as reviewable diffs rather than silent losses.

Without these, every regression is caught only by the expensive manual passes in `E47-Q02`, which run per release candidate rather than per PR. The economics are the point: keyboard traps and focus loss are the two defect classes most likely to be reintroduced by ordinary feature work in E48/E49 and beyond, and they are cheap to detect automatically.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A Playwright project `e2e/a11y-keyboard/` that runs against the built Electron renderer bundle and enforces, via a test-level guard, that no `page.mouse`, `click()` or pointer event is issued - any attempt fails the test.
- Keyboard-only journeys covering the `E47-Q01` group 1 script: app shell navigation and skip links (SCR-010, SCR-011), command palette (SCR-012), hotkey cheatsheet (SCR-013), workspace/pane focus cycling with `F6` and `Ctrl+Tab` (SCR-020, SCR-021), chart focus and data cursor movement (SCR-030), toggling the table alternative with `Alt+T` and reading a bar (SCR-045), placing and confirming a limit order (SCR-060, SCR-076), cancelling an order from the grid (SCR-063), reduced-motion override `Ctrl+Shift+M` and high-contrast `Ctrl+Shift+H` (SCR-116, SCR-117), rule editor form mode (SCR-081) and the non-drag node-connection equivalent (SCR-082), admin user creation (SCR-121, SCR-123).
- **Keyboard-trap detection helper**: for each journey, tab forward through the whole screen and assert the focus sequence returns to the starting element within N stops and that every stop is a visible, named element; a focus stop on an element with no accessible name fails.
- **Focus-visibility assertion**: computed outline/box-shadow present and its contrast against the adjacent background is >= 3:1, using the same contrast function as the `E47-T03` token linter so the two never disagree.
- **Accessibility-tree snapshots** per top-level screen (`accessibility.snapshot()`), committed as fixtures, with a reviewer-friendly diff on change; landmark and heading structure asserted against the structure defined in the standard section 3.4.1.
- **Live-region assertions**: after a simulated fill, exactly one assertive announcement node is present with the expected text shape; after a burst of market updates, the polite region's mutation count stays within the coalescing budget of the standard section 6.2.
- CI wiring: the suite runs on every PR touching `web/` or the design-system package, as a required check per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`; snapshot updates require an explicit flag and a reviewer note.
- A short `README` for the suite explaining how to add a journey when a new screen ships (the mechanism E48/E49 will reuse).

## Out of scope
- axe-core, pa11y and Lighthouse gates and their burn-down dashboard - `E47-Q04`.
- Motion/flash frame analysis - `E47-Q05`.
- Manual screen-reader verification - `E47-Q02`. This suite asserts structure and reachability, never "it sounds right".
- Visual regression of themes - covered by design QA in `E47-D03`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Keyboard-only E2E and a11y-tree snapshot gates

  Scenario: The suite cannot cheat with a mouse
    Given a journey that calls page.click
    When the suite runs
    Then the guard fails that test with a message naming the forbidden API

  Scenario: A keyboard trap fails the build
    Given a branch that removes the Escape handler from the SCR-076 order confirmation modal
    When the keyboard-only suite runs in CI
    Then the trap-detection helper fails
    And the PR cannot merge because the check is required on main

  Scenario: Failure case - a lost accessible name is caught
    Given a refactor that replaces a labelled button with an icon-only button
    When the accessibility-tree snapshot is compared
    Then the diff shows the name loss and the check fails
    And updating the snapshot requires an explicit flag and a reviewer note

  Scenario: Edge case - focus must survive a streaming update
    Given the order ticket has focus on the quantity field
    When a scripted burst of 500 market messages is injected
    Then focus remains on the quantity field at the end of the burst
    And the polite live region mutated no more times than the coalescing budget allows

  Scenario: The suite is fast enough to be a per-PR gate
    When the suite runs on CI hardware
    Then the whole keyboard-only project completes within its agreed wall-clock budget
    And a timeout is reported as an infrastructure failure, not silently retried into a pass
```

## Technical notes / design
- Market data is injected through the deterministic replay/fixture path rather than a live WS, so the streaming assertions are reproducible; the fixture is the same one `E47-Q01` defines.
- The forbidden-mouse guard is implemented by wrapping the Playwright page object in a proxy in the project's fixture, so the ban is structural rather than a review convention.
- Snapshots are stored per screen and normalised (volatile values such as prices, timestamps and ids are masked) so diffs show semantic change only; an unmasked value causing daily churn is a bug in the normaliser.
- The contrast helper must import the same implementation used by the token linter in `E47-T03`; duplicating the formula is explicitly forbidden because a drift between the two produces unfalsifiable disagreements.
- Node-graph keyboard journeys assert the documented non-drag equivalent from SCR-082; if the product has no such equivalent, the test is written as an expected failure referencing the remediation ticket rather than skipped silently.

## Test plan
- Self-verification by fault injection: deliberately break the Escape handler, remove an `aria-label`, drop a focus ring and introduce a focus-stealing `focus()` in a WS handler on a scratch branch; each must fail the corresponding assertion. Record the four injected-fault runs as evidence.
- Flake budget: the suite runs 20 consecutive times on the fixture; any test failing non-deterministically is fixed or quarantined with a linked ticket before the gate becomes required.

## Security notes
- Test fixtures use seeded demo users with deterministic throwaway credentials held in CI secrets, never live Bybit keys; the admin journeys must not require a real API key.
- Accessibility-tree snapshots are committed artefacts - the normaliser must mask account identifiers, emails and balances so the repository does not accumulate real user data through snapshot files.
- The suite runs against a staging/demo backend on the tailnet; CI must not be able to reach the live environment.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the automated enforcement arm of the accessibility standard. It deliberately encodes *structural* accessibility (reachability, names, roles, landmarks, focus) and leaves *experiential* accessibility to `E47-Q02`; the README states that division explicitly so future contributors do not assume a green suite means conformance.

## Performance notes
- Budget the whole keyboard-only project to fit the per-PR check envelope agreed in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; parallelise by screen.

title: Motion/flash audit script and accessibility-overhead performance benchmarks
body:
## Context
Two accessibility requirements are measurable rather than reviewable, and both are performance work.

First, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 item 5 requires an automated **motion/flash audit**: frame capture plus luminance-delta analysis against the heatmap, big-trade bubbles and price-flash components at a fixed high-tick-rate scenario, asserting the flash rate stays below the WCAG three-flashes-per-second threshold (section 7.3). In a trading terminal the risk is real - a heatmap under a liquidation cascade and a price flash on every tick are exactly the patterns that produce photosensitive-seizure hazards.

Second, the accessibility machinery itself costs frames. The DOM mirror (standard section 6.1), the live regions (6.2) and the table alternatives (6.3) all run inside the same frame budget the WebGL engine defends in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`. If enabling accommodations makes the terminal unusable, users will turn them off, which is a conformance failure dressed as a preference.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion/flash audit harness** (`perf/a11y-motion-audit/`): drives a fixed replay scenario at a pinned high tick rate, captures frames off the canvas, computes relative-luminance deltas over the flashing region per the WCAG general and red flash thresholds, and asserts fewer than three flashes per second for the heatmap (SCR-050), big-trade bubbles (SCR-053), price flash on the ladder and positions grid (SCR-050, SCR-063), alert toasts (SCR-092) and connection-state banners (SCR-152).
- The same harness run with **reduced motion enabled** (OS setting and the in-app `Ctrl+Shift+M` override surfaced on SCR-117), asserting the motion-reduce variants are used and that animation work disappears from the frame profile rather than merely being visually hidden - the SCR-117 performance note requires a *measurable* reduction.
- **Accessibility-overhead benchmarks**: frame-time p50/p95 and dropped-frame counts on the SCR-030 chart with footprint at the standard benchmark scenario, measured in four configurations - baseline, DOM mirror on, live-region announcements on at each SCR-117 verbosity setting, and table alternative open alongside the canvas (SCR-045 + SCR-030). Budget: accommodations must not push p95 frame time past the engine budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- **Table-alternative scale benchmark**: SCR-045 renders 100k virtualised rows with scripting under the 8 ms per scroll frame stated in its catalogue entry, and issues no extra data fetch (it reads the same in-memory series).
- **Announcement-throttle load script**: inject 500, 2000 and 5000 messages per second through the fixture and record live-region mutation counts, announcement latency and main-thread cost per verbosity level; assert coalescing holds at every level.
- CI wiring: motion audit runs on any change to the listed components' animation code and before every release; overhead benchmarks run nightly with a regression gate against stored baselines.
- A results appendix handed to `E47-T06` (the conformance report needs a defensible statement about SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold) and to `E47-Q09`.

## Out of scope
- Engine-level rendering optimisation - if a benchmark fails, this ticket files the defect; the fix lands in the engine or remediation tickets.
- Backend load testing - the accommodations are client-side; WS fan-out load is owned by the data-plane epics.
- Subjective judgement about whether an animation is pleasant - that is design QA in `E47-D03`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Motion/flash audit and accessibility-overhead benchmarks

  Scenario: Flash threshold is enforced automatically
    Given the pinned liquidation-cascade replay scenario
    When the motion audit runs against the heatmap and big-trade bubbles
    Then the measured flash rate for every analysed region is below three per second
    And the report records the measured rate, not merely a pass verdict

  Scenario: Reduced motion removes work, not just visuals
    Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled via the Ctrl+Shift+M override
    When the same scenario is profiled
    Then animation-related scripting and GPU work is measurably lower than the motion-safe run
    And a run where only opacity is forced constant while the animation loop still executes fails the check

  Scenario: Failure case - an accommodation blows the frame budget
    Given the DOM mirror and always-on announcements are enabled on SCR-030 with footprint
    When the benchmark scenario runs
    And p95 frame time exceeds the engine budget
    Then the benchmark fails and a perf defect is filed against the owning component
    And the conformance report cannot claim the accommodation is usable until it is closed

  Scenario: Edge case - extreme message rate degrades by coalescing, not by dropping frames
    Given 5000 messages per second injected at the highest verbosity
    When the announcement-throttle script runs
    Then live-region mutations stay within the coalescing budget
    And the main thread remains responsive to keyboard input within its interaction budget

  Scenario: Baselines make regressions visible
    Given stored baselines from the previous nightly run
    When a change increases p95 frame time beyond the agreed tolerance
    Then the nightly gate fails and names the configuration that regressed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Flash analysis operates on captured frames from a deterministic replay window, never live market data; reproducibility is the entire value of the check.
- Luminance delta uses the same relative-luminance implementation as the contrast helper in `E47-Q03` and the `E47-T03` token linter - one implementation, three consumers.
- Regions analysed are declared per component (a rectangle or selector-derived bounding box) so a flash is not averaged away across a mostly-static screen; whole-viewport averaging is the classic way these audits produce false passes.
- Benchmarks pin renderer configuration via the SCR-118 settings (renderer mode, FPS cap) and record it with the result; comparing results across renderer modes is invalid and is blocked by tagging.
- The overhead benchmark must include compact density, because dense layouts are where mirror node counts are largest.

## Test plan
- Validate the audit with a **known-bad synthetic component** flashing at 6 Hz: the harness must fail it. Validate with a known-good 1 Hz component: it must pass. Both fixtures are committed so future analyser changes can be re-validated.
- Validate the overhead benchmark by artificially inflating mirror node counts tenfold and confirming the regression gate trips.
- Run the full set three times to establish variance, and set the regression tolerance from measured variance rather than a guessed percentage.

## Security notes
- Captured frames may contain account balances, position sizes and symbol exposure. Captures run against seeded demo data only; the harness deletes raw frame captures after analysis, retaining aggregate numbers plus at most one redacted sample image per finding.
- Benchmark artefacts uploaded to CI are scanned for the same sensitive-string set used by `E47-Q04`'s report post-processor.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket protects two groups directly: photosensitive users (flash thresholds) and AT users (accommodations must remain usable at speed). A passing benchmark with a failing flash audit is not a trade-off to negotiate - the flash threshold is a hard WCAG requirement at AA and blocks release.

## Performance notes
- Budgets are referenced, not redefined: engine frame budget and interaction budget come from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; SCR-045's 8 ms scripting per scroll frame and SCR-118's renderer settings come from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Results feed the same performance dashboard used by the engine epics, so accessibility overhead is visible alongside ordinary render metrics rather than in a silo.

## Observability
- Metrics: `a11y_flash_rate{component,scenario}`, `a11y_frame_p95_ms{config,density}`, `a11y_live_region_mutations_per_s{verbosity,rate}`, `a11y_table_scroll_script_ms`.
- Nightly results posted to the release dashboard; a flash-threshold breach pages the Accessibility role and blocks the release candidate.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Motion/flash harness merged, validated against known-good and known-bad fixtures, wired to run on animation-code changes and per release.
- [ ] Overhead benchmarks merged with baselines, variance-derived tolerances and a nightly regression gate.
- [ ] Announcement-throttle load script merged with results at 500/2000/5000 messages per second.
- [ ] Any breach filed as a defect with an owner; no breach accepted without recorded owner sign-off.
- [ ] Results appendix delivered to `E47-T06` and `E47-Q09`.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q01` - scenarios and fixtures.
- `E47-T05` - motion-reduce variants must exist before the reduced-motion comparison is meaningful.

## Branch
`feat/e47-motion-audit`.

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 6.1-6.3 (canvas strategy cost), 7 (reduced motion, flash), 9.5 (motion audit gate).
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (frame and interaction budgets, regression-gate philosophy).
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (DOM-mirror sync API, windowed accessibility tree).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-045, SCR-050, SCR-053, SCR-063, SCR-092, SCR-117, SCR-118, SCR-152.
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-007, US-SET-008, US-CHART-014.
