title: Chart canvas surrogate and table alternative reach AA (SCR-030, SCR-045)
body:
## Context
The chart is the product, and it is a WebGL canvas — opaque to assistive technology by default. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 mandates three complementary layers for it: the offscreen DOM mirror (§6.1), throttled ARIA live regions (§6.2), and the equal-status data-table alternative **SCR-045** (§6/§5.4), whose catalogue entry states plainly: "this is the normative accessible equivalent of SCR-030 and must reach feature parity for reading data; verified in every a11y test pass." **US-CHART-014** owns the table alternative; §3.1.7 of the standard requires that pan, zoom and the crosshair be fully keyboard operable (arrow keys per bar, `Shift+arrows` pan, `+`/`-` zoom, `Home`/`End` jump).

These pieces shipped across E11/E12 as each feature landed. This Story closes the gap between "shipped" and "conformant" using the E47-T01 findings: mirror/canvas correspondence, announcement usefulness at real tick rates, focus never being stolen by a price update (§3.4.3), and true parity of the table view.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-030 chart panel**: canvas exposes an accessible name and role; the windowed DOM mirror materialises exactly the focusable units in view; keyboard crosshair navigation announces the focused bar as a useful sentence (time, O/H/L/C, volume, delta) rather than a number soup; `Home`/`End`/`Shift+arrow`/`+`/`-` behave per §3.2.
- **Live-region discipline**: ambient fields (last price, best bid/ask, mark, unrealised P&L) on a polite region throttled to the user's configured cadence, always presenting the latest value and never queueing intermediate ticks; discrete events (WS disconnect, data gap) on assertive/`role="alert"`.
- **Focus stability**: assert that no streaming update, reconnect, or auto-scroll moves keyboard focus (§3.4.3); a reconnect that re-mounts the chart restores the previously focused bar.
- **SCR-045 parity**: `Alt+T` from any chart; arrow-key grid navigation; `Enter` expands a bar's footprint cells; `Ctrl+C` copies TSV; per-row actions (create alert here, replay from here, add note) reachable by keyboard; the table is opened from the chart panel header (equal status) and not buried in settings; virtualised rendering keeps the accessibility tree windowed.
- Remediation of every E47-T01 finding tagged to the chart surrogate pattern, including target-size and focus-obscured issues on the chart chrome (CMP-180…CMP-199 primitives, chart chrome CMP-200+ band).

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell grid, DOM ladder and heatmap surrogates — **E47-S02**.
- Rendering performance optimisation of the mirror — **E46** (this Story files tickets if the mirror exceeds its budget).
- New chart features or new table columns beyond what SCR-045 specifies.
- Drawing-tool keyboard creation, already delivered under E14 and only re-verified here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A blind trader reads the chart
  Given NVDA is running on the Electron build and BTCUSDT 1m is displayed
  When the trader focuses the chart and presses the left arrow key
  Then focus moves to the previous bar and the screen reader announces its time, open, high, low, close, volume and delta
  And the announcement is a single coherent utterance, not one field per event

Scenario: Streaming does not flood or steal
  Given the symbol is ticking at 20 updates per second and announcement cadence is the 2 s default
  Then the polite region is updated at most once per 2 s per field with the latest value
  And keyboard focus remains on the bar the trader selected throughout

Scenario: The table alternative has parity
  Given the chart shows a visible range with footprint data
  When Alt+T is pressed
  Then a keyboard-navigable grid of that same range opens from the panel header
  And expanding a row reveals that bar's footprint cells with price, bid, ask, delta and imbalance flag
  And every datum visible on the canvas is present in the grid

Scenario: Reconnect preserves context
  Given the WS connection drops while bar 13:58 is focused
  When the connection is restored and the chart re-subscribes
  Then the disconnect and reconnect are announced assertively
  And focus returns to bar 13:58 rather than to the document body or the latest bar

Scenario: Mirror stays windowed
  Given 100 000 bars are loaded
  Then the accessibility tree contains only the focusable units for the visible range plus a small buffer
  And the axe and accessibility-tree snapshot gates pass on SCR-030 and SCR-045

Scenario: No-data and error states are announced
  Given the chart enters the SCR-047 empty state or the SCR-048 error state
  Then the state is conveyed as text to the screen reader with the recovery action reachable by keyboard
```

## Technical notes / design
The engine already exposes the "current visible window + current focused unit" query surface that `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 made a binding engine-design requirement and `26-chart-engine-design.md` implements; the React layer consumes it to keep mirror and draw calls frame-synchronised. Announcement composition happens in one place (a formatter shared with SCR-045) so canvas and table cannot describe the same bar differently. Throttling reads the user's cadence preference from the settings document rather than a hard-coded constant.

## Test plan
Unit: announcement formatter, throttle behaviour under burst input, mirror windowing at range boundaries. Integration: focus-stability test driving a synthetic 20 Hz tick stream. E2E keyboard-only: crosshair traversal, `Alt+T` round trip, TSV copy, row actions. Manual SR: NVDA task script on SCR-030 and SCR-045 (JAWS and VoiceOver covered in **E47-T04**). Gates: axe, accessibility-tree snapshot, Lighthouse on the workspace screen.

## Security notes
The mirror and table render the same data the canvas is authorised to show — they must derive from the same RBAC-filtered series, never a broader fetch. TSV copy is clipboard-only and must not include account identifiers unless they are already on screen. Announcements must not read API keys or session tokens under any state.

## Accessibility notes
Direct implementation of `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1–§6.3 and §3.1.7. Canvas carries `aria-label`; the mirror is visually hidden by off-screen positioning/clip-path, never `display:none`. Targets ≥24×24 CSS px; the dense-footprint essential exception is only claimed where SCR-045 provides the alternative. WCAG SCs in play: 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Mirror maintenance ≤1 ms per frame at the reference bar count; announcement throttling must not allocate per tick. The SCR-045 grid renders 100k rows virtualised at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame, per its catalogue entry. Regressions go to **E46** with measurements attached.

## Observability
`chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported` (already specified on SCR-045); client metrics `a11y_mirror_update_ms`, `a11y_announcements_per_minute`, `a11y_focus_steal_count` (expected zero — alert if non-zero).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test or a recorded manual SR step.
- [ ] All E47-T01 chart-surrogate findings closed or converted to registered exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the touched frontend packages; ≥85% on the engine package.
- [ ] axe, keyboard-E2E, Lighthouse and a11y-tree-snapshot gates green on SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-047, SCR-048.
- [ ] NVDA spot-check recorded; deferral to E47-T04 stated explicitly for JAWS/VoiceOver.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030/SCR-045 and `26-chart-engine-design.md` reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed keyboard-only at Sprint Review.

`blocked_by`: **E47-T01** (scopes the findings). Feeds **E47-T04** (SR sign-off scripts) and **E47-T05**.

`feat/e47-chart-a11y`

title: Footprint, DOM ladder and heatmap grids reach AA keyboard-only
body:
## Context
The footprint grid and the DOM ladder + liquidity heatmap are the densest surfaces in the product and the ones `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 explicitly refuses to exempt: "the DOM ladder, footprint grid and rule node-graph editor are dense, high-information-density surfaces; WCAG AA still applies — density is solved via information architecture (§4), not by exempting a screen." §3.4.2 prescribes the mechanism — roving tabindex per the WAI-ARIA APG grid pattern, "this prevents 200+ Tab presses to cross a DOM ladder" — and §4 forbids colour-only encoding of bid/ask, imbalance and delta sign anywhere.

The ladder is also a *trading* surface: `Enter` places a limit at the focused row, `Ctrl+Enter` goes aggressive, `Ctrl+Delete` cancels all at that row (§3.2). Accessibility defects here are not cosmetic — an ambiguous announcement before a keyboard order placement is a financial risk. This Story remediates the E47-T01 findings on these surfaces.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Footprint (SCR-030 footprint mode, SCR-032 settings)**: roving-tabindex cell grid with `role="grid"` semantics on the surrogate layer; arrow keys move cell focus, `PageUp`/`PageDown` by bar, announcements give price, bid volume, ask volume, delta with explicit sign, and imbalance status as words; imbalance-flagged cells carry a border/pattern distinction that survives grayscale (§4.3).
- **DOM ladder + heatmap (SCR-050, settings SCR-051)**: roving tabindex over ladder rows; each row announces price, bid size, ask size, side and any resting order/position at that price; the heatmap cell readout gives price, size and side on focus (§4.1); bid/ask side is conveyed by text and axis-side convention with a persistent legend, never hue alone.
- **Keyboard trading safety**: `Enter`/`Ctrl+Enter`/`Ctrl+Delete` at the focused row route through the confirm policy (**US-SET-003**) with the resolved price, side, quantity and account read back before commit; the 1-click ARMED state is announced and shown with icon + text (§3.1.5).
- **Adjacent panes** re-verified with the same pattern: **SCR-052** CVD/delta, **SCR-053** tape + bubbles, **SCR-055** speed of tape, **SCR-056** imbalance tracker, **SCR-038** profile panel — sign and side always carry `+`/`-` or a glyph.
- Target-size accounting: rows and cells ≥24×24 CSS px at default zoom, or the essential exception claimed with SCR-045/table alternatives named as the compensating control (§3.4.7).

## Out of scope
- Chart price-series surrogate and SCR-045 — **E47-S01**.
- Changing palettes — **E47-S06** (this Story consumes whatever palette ships and enforces the non-colour channel).
- Order-flow algorithm behaviour or detector methodology.
- Heatmap render-path optimisation — **E46**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crossing the ladder costs a few keystrokes, not two hundred
  Given the DOM ladder has 200 visible price rows and one row is focused
  When the trader presses Tab
  Then focus leaves the ladder as a single composite widget
  And arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End move within it

Scenario: A keyboard order is read back before it is placed
  Given a ladder row at 64 010 is focused and confirm policy is "dialog"
  When Enter is pressed
  Then a keyboard-operable confirmation announces side, price, quantity and the target account or accounts
  And Esc cancels with nothing sent

Scenario: Footprint imbalance survives grayscale
  Given a cell is flagged as an imbalance
  When the display is rendered in grayscale or a high-contrast theme
  Then the flag remains distinguishable by border or pattern
  And the screen reader announces the imbalance state as a word

Scenario: Delta sign is never colour-only
  Given a footprint cell with delta -8 and another with +8
  Then both render an explicit sign or glyph in addition to any colour
  And the automated no-hue-alone check passes for the footprint, CVD, tape and imbalance surfaces

Scenario: Dense targets are accounted for, not ignored
  Given footprint cells fall below 24 px at maximum zoom-out
  Then the essential exception is recorded with SCR-045 named as the alternative
  And at default zoom, ladder rows and cells meet the 24 px minimum

Scenario: A fill does not hijack the keyboard
  Given the trader is navigating ladder rows
  When an order fills
  Then the fill is announced assertively and focus stays on the current row
```

## Technical notes / design
One composite-grid implementation is shared by footprint, ladder and profile surrogates — `15-component-catalogue.md` §11.3 already requires the pattern be "specified once in the component catalogue and reused everywhere the pattern repeats", so this Story consolidates any divergent copies found by the sweep into CMP-113/CMP-136 and their shared grid behaviour. Announcement text is produced by the same formatter family as E47-S01 so a price reads identically everywhere. Keyboard order paths reuse the existing confirm-policy machinery rather than introducing a ladder-specific dialog.

## Test plan
Unit: roving-tabindex state machine at edges and on data churn; announcement formatting for zero, negative and very large sizes. Integration: focus stability under a replayed high-rate book fixture. E2E keyboard-only: navigate ladder, place and cancel a demo order, toggle 1-click and confirm the armed announcement. Visual: grayscale and high-contrast snapshots asserting imbalance distinguishability. Gates: axe, a11y-tree snapshot, no-hue-alone check on SCR-050, SCR-051, SCR-052, SCR-053, SCR-055, SCR-056.

## Security notes
Keyboard order entry is the highest-consequence path in this Story: the read-back must show the *resolved* per-account quantities (per §3.3.5, guarding the silent multi-account fat-finger), the arm token requirement for one-click entry is unchanged, and no accessibility preference may bypass the confirm policy or the native-SL invariant. Announcements must never expose accounts the user lacks RBAC access to.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §3.4.2 (roving tabindex), §3.4.7 (target size and essential exception), §4.1/§4.3 (non-colour encoding of side, status and sign), §6.1 (surrogate layer). WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 1.4.1, 1.4.11, 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.11, 2.5.8, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Surrogate rows are virtualised to the visible window; a full-depth ladder must not materialise 1 000 DOM nodes. Focus moves must not trigger a full re-render of the canvas layer. Measure surrogate update cost under the E46 harness and file E46 tickets for overruns rather than silently accepting them.

## Observability
Client metrics `a11y_grid_focus_move_ms`, `a11y_surrogate_nodes` (alert above the windowing ceiling); analytics `dom.keyboard_order_placed` to confirm the path is actually usable, not merely present.

title: Rule form and node-graph editors keyboard/screen-reader operable
body:
## Context
The node-graph rule editor is the third surface `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 names as dense-but-not-exempt, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §9.1 goal 2 calls it out by name — AA conformance "across every screen, including the chart surfaces and **the node editor**". A spatial, drag-and-connect canvas is the hardest possible case for WCAG 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements): every node move and every edge connection is natively a drag.

§3.2 already defines the keyboard model (`Ctrl+Shift+N` add node, `Enter` to connect after `Tab`-selecting source then target port, `Delete` to remove), and §3.3 item 6 requires **SCR-082**'s spec to cross-link to the global hotkey conflict rules rather than inventing its own. Both editors must merge or not at all (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.3 rule 5), so a form editor that is accessible and a node editor that is not still leaves a rule a user cannot author — the two are audited together here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-081 rule form editor**: every condition/action row fully labelled (persistent labels, not placeholder-only, per US-SET-001 NFR); dynamic row add/remove announced; validation errors associated with their fields and announced on submit; nested condition groups exposed with correct structural semantics so a screen reader can perceive the boolean nesting.
- **SCR-082 node-graph editor**: nodes and edges are focusable with a documented traversal order; arrow keys move focus between connected nodes; `Ctrl+Shift+N` adds, `Enter` connects a selected source port to a selected target port, `Delete` removes the focused node or edge; node *position* is adjustable by arrow-key nudge with discrete steps (WCAG 2.5.7 non-drag alternative); every node announces its type, its parameter summary, and its inbound/outbound connections.
- A **structural text view** of the graph (a tree/list of nodes and their connections) as the equal-status alternative for anyone who cannot perceive the canvas layout — the same principle SCR-045 applies to the chart; reachable from the editor header, not from settings.
- Conflict and error surfaces: **SCR-086** rule conflict resolver, **SCR-088** IR inspector and **SCR-085** arming dialog audited — arming is destructive and must satisfy the keyboard-operable confirm rules (§3.1.4).
- Remediation of all E47-T01 findings tagged to the rule-editor pattern, including focus return from node property popovers and focus-not-obscured (2.4.11) when the canvas pans a focused node under a floating toolbar.

## Out of scope
- Node-editor auto-layout and node search — descoped to R5 backlog per `30-release-roadmap.md` §12 row 8 and not resurrected here.
- Rule IR, compiler or runtime semantics — **E35**.
- Rule templates gallery visual polish — **E49**.
- New node types.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A rule is authored end to end without a mouse
  Given the node editor is open on an empty canvas
  When the user adds a trigger node, adds an action node, selects the source port, selects the target port and presses Enter
  Then the edge is created and announced
  And the rule validates and can be saved, all without a pointer event

Scenario: Dragging always has an alternative
  Given a node is focused
  When arrow keys are pressed
  Then the node moves by a discrete step and its new position is announced or otherwise conveyed
  And no repositioning capability exists that is reachable only by dragging

Scenario: Graph structure is perceivable without the canvas
  When the structural text view is opened from the editor header
  Then every node, its parameters and its inbound and outbound connections are listed and navigable
  And edits made there are reflected in the canvas and vice versa

Scenario: A focused node is never hidden behind chrome
  Given the canvas auto-pans to reveal a focused node
  Then the node is not fully obscured by the floating toolbar or the property panel

Scenario: Arming is a deliberate, keyboard-operable act
  Given a rule is ready to arm in the Live environment
  When the arm action is invoked from the keyboard
  Then the confirm surface states the environment, the rule and its actions, traps focus, is dismissible with Esc, and returns focus to the trigger on close

Scenario: Invalid input is announced, not merely coloured
  Given a required parameter is left empty in the form editor
  When save is attempted
  Then the error is programmatically associated with its field, announced, and focus moves to the first invalid field
```

## Technical notes / design
The structural text view is the pragmatic answer to a spatial canvas: rather than pretending arrow-key spatial navigation alone makes a graph perceivable, it exposes the same model in a linear form, which is also what the IR inspector (SCR-088) already renders — so this is a presentation of an existing model, not a second source of truth. Node traversal order is derived from the graph topology (trigger-first, then breadth-first over edges) rather than from canvas coordinates, which are meaningless to a non-visual user. Hotkey bindings register through the global layer (E47-S08's remap machinery) so conflicts surface at bind time per §3.3.

## Test plan
Unit: traversal-order derivation, port-selection state machine, nudge stepping. E2E keyboard-only: author, validate, save, arm and disarm a rule with zero pointer events. Manual SR: NVDA pass over both editors including the structural view. Gates: axe and a11y-tree snapshot on SCR-081, SCR-082, SCR-085, SCR-086, SCR-088.

## Security notes
Arming a rule in Live is a privileged, audited action; no accessibility affordance may bypass the confirm or the RBAC check, and the structural text view must respect the same rule-visibility permissions as the canvas. Rule names and parameters are user content rendered as text only. The IR inspector must not expose internal sandbox details beyond what the existing screen already permits.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §3.2 (rule-builder bindings), §3.3 item 6 (cross-linked conflict rules), §3.4.4 (dialog focus trap and return), §3.4.6 (focus not obscured), §3.4.8 (dragging alternatives). WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Focus traversal on a large graph must be O(degree) not O(nodes); the structural view is virtualised beyond a few hundred rows. Canvas auto-pan on focus is animated under the motion token pair so reduced-motion users get an instant jump.

## Observability
`rule.editor_keyboard_authored` analytics flag on save (records whether the session used any pointer event on the canvas — a direct measure of whether the keyboard path is genuinely complete); `rule.structural_view_opened`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named test or recorded manual step.
- [ ] All E47-T01 rule-editor findings closed or registered as exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the touched packages.
- [ ] axe, keyboard-E2E and a11y-tree-snapshot gates green on the listed screens.
- [ ] NVDA pass recorded over both editors.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 keyboard spec reconciled with shipped behaviour and its cross-link to `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.3 verified to resolve.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; keyboard-only authoring demoed at Sprint Review.

title: Reduced-motion coverage and the three-flashes-per-second ceiling
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §7 sets two rules that a fast-moving trading UI breaks easily. First, every animated component must consume a shared `motion-safe`/`motion-reduce` token pair — "reduced-motion is a design-system token/mode, not a per-component ad hoc CSS override" — and "a component cannot ship with only a hard-coded animation" (§11.4). Second, the seizure threshold: no content flashes more than three times per second, audited explicitly for big-trade bubble bursts, liquidation-heatmap flash, alert-toast entrance and price-flash-on-tick, because "it is easy for a naive flash green/red on every tick implementation to exceed 3 Hz on a fast-moving symbol".

This is the one accessibility area where a defect can cause physical harm, and the one most likely to have regressed silently as order-flow features were tuned for visual punch through R2.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Audit every animated surface for a motion token pair: chart inertia and auto-pan, heatmap fade and trail, big-trade bubbles (**SCR-053**), liquidation flashes (**SCR-054**), price flash on tick, toast entrance (**SCR-015**), panel/dock transitions (**SCR-021**), coach marks (**SCR-018**), skeleton shimmer (CMP-015), spinner (CMP-014), node-editor canvas pan. Replace any hard-coded animation with the token pair.
- Under reduced motion (OS preference or the in-app override, including the `Ctrl+Shift+M` session toggle from §3.2): animations are disabled or replaced with instant changes; parallax and inertia stop; nothing animates longer than 5 s without a pause control.
- Enforce the flash ceiling in the *implementation*, not only in the test: price-flash and bubble-burst effects coalesce so that at any tick rate the visible flash frequency is capped below 3 Hz, degrading to a sustained state change rather than a faster blink.
- Wire and calibrate the motion/flash audit script from **E47-T02** against a recorded high-tick-rate fixture for each named component, with the luminance-delta threshold and its justification documented.
- Remediate every E47-T01 finding in the motion pattern.

## Out of scope
- Adding new animations or motion design work — **E49** / design.
- Frame-rate optimisation — **E46**.
- The preference UI itself — **E47-S07**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion is honoured everywhere
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is reduce
  When the heatmap updates, a bubble fires, a toast appears and a panel is docked
  Then each uses its motion-reduce variant with no easing, inertia or parallax

Scenario: The flash ceiling holds under a fast symbol
  Given a recorded fixture ticking at 40 updates per second
  When price flash and big-trade bubbles render
  Then the measured flash frequency for each component stays below 3 per second
  And the effect degrades to a sustained state change rather than a faster blink

Scenario: The session override works without settings
  When Ctrl+Shift+M is pressed
  Then reduced motion toggles for the session, the new state is announced, and it does not overwrite the persisted preference

Scenario: No hard-coded animation survives
  Given the design-system lint runs over component styles
  Then any animation or transition lacking a motion-safe/motion-reduce token pair fails the build with the component named

Scenario: Long animations offer control
  Given any animation would run longer than 5 seconds
  Then a pause or stop control is available, or the animation is not shipped

Scenario: The audit script catches a regression
  Given a change makes the liquidation flash fire at 5 Hz
  When CI runs the motion audit
  Then the build fails naming the component and the measured rate
```

## Technical notes / design
Coalescing is the real fix: capping flash rate by throttling the *effect trigger* (one flash per 400 ms window, carrying the net direction of the ticks in that window) preserves the visual signal traders rely on while making the 3 Hz bound structural rather than incidental. The motion token pair lives in the design system so the lint can enforce it; components consume variants, never raw durations. The `Ctrl+Shift+M` override is session state layered over the persisted preference from E47-S07, not a write to it.

## Test plan
Unit: coalescing window behaviour at burst and idle rates; token-pair resolution under both modes. Automated: the luminance-delta audit over each named component against the recorded fixture. Lint: hard-coded-animation check across the component library. E2E: reduced-motion toggle end to end including the session override. Manual: a reviewer with the fixture confirms the degraded effect is still readable as a signal.

## Security notes
None directly; the flash coalescer must not be usable to suppress a *safety* signal — risk-breach and kill-switch surfaces convey state by persistent text and icon (§4.4), never by flashing alone, so coalescing cannot hide them.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §7.1–§7.4 and §11.4. WCAG SCs: 2.2.2 (pause/stop/hide), 2.3.1 (three flashes), 2.3.3 (animation from interactions, AAA-adjacent but adopted here via the preference). Reduced motion must never remove *information*, only motion — a bubble that no longer animates must still appear.

## Performance notes
Disabling animation must measurably reduce frame work (the SCR-117 claim this Story makes true); record before/after frame times for the heatmap and bubble scenes. Coalescing reduces draw work at high tick rates, so it should improve, never worsen, the hot path.

## Observability
Client metrics `motion_reduced_active` (share of sessions) and `flash_events_per_minute{component}`; a CI-published flash-rate table per audited component.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests.
- [ ] Every animated component consumes a motion token pair; lint enforces it.
- [ ] Flash audit calibrated, documented and green for all named components.
- [ ] E47-T01 motion findings closed or registered as exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages; before/after frame-time measurements attached.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` motion tokens reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review with the high-tick fixture.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-S07** (preference substrate and the session override). Uses the audit gate from **E47-T02**; feeds **E47-T05**.

## Branch
`feat/e47-reduced-motion-flash`

## References
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2, §7, §9.5, §11.4; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-015, SCR-018, SCR-021, SCR-053, SCR-054, SCR-117; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-007.

title: Abuse cases: accessible-surface leakage, hotkey tampering, announcement DoS
body:
## Context
`E47-X01` identifies threats analytically; this ticket tries to make them happen. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires abuse cases to be executed, not merely enumerated, and the accessible surface is the least-tested surface in the product - precisely the condition under which parity bugs survive to production.

The central hypothesis under test: **the accessible representation of a screen is subject to exactly the same authorisation, masking and confirmation controls as the visual representation**. Every abuse case below is an attempt to falsify it.

## Scope / Deliverables
An executed abuse-case suite (`security/abuse-cases/e47/`) with a result per case, automated where feasible in the `E47-Q03` harness and manual otherwise:
1. **Masked-value leakage**: on SCR-127 (API key rotation) and SCR-128 (key health), read every accessible name, description, live-region text and DOM-mirror node; assert no unmasked key material, no full secret, and no value the visual surface masks.
2. **Cross-account exposure via the mirror**: as a user whose `user_account_access` covers account A only, open surfaces that aggregate accounts (SCR-063 positions, SCR-071 risk dashboard, SCR-062 trade-group manager) and assert no account-B identifier, balance or position appears in any accessible node - including nodes rendered but visually clipped or collapsed.
3. **Hidden-but-exposed controls**: as a viewer, enumerate the full accessibility tree of owner/manager screens (SCR-120..SCR-149) and assert no owner-only action is present, focusable or activatable; specifically attempt activation of any node found.
4. **Re-auth bypass**: attempt to reach an admin action requiring the SCR-149 re-authentication gate purely by keyboard and AT navigation, including via the command palette (SCR-012) and hotkeys, asserting the gate always interposes.
5. **Confirmation stripping via preferences**: modify `PUT /api/v1/me/preferences` payloads directly (including values the UI cannot produce) and attempt to disable destructive-action confirmations (US-SET-003), the Demo/Live confirm (SCR-074) or the arming requirement; assert server-side rejection and that safety controls are not client-configurable.
6. **Hotkey tampering**: craft a hotkey profile via `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys` binding a single unmodified key to an irreversible trading action, activate it, and assert either rejection or that the confirmation still interposes; assert the change is audited.
7. **Announcement and mirror DoS**: drive extreme update rates and extreme visible ranges to attempt unbounded live-region or mirror growth, and attempt to open SCR-045 over an unbounded range; assert coalescing, windowing and range caps hold and the client stays responsive.
8. **Table-export exfiltration**: use the SCR-045 `Ctrl+C` TSV export and any CSV export on the table alternatives to attempt extraction of data beyond the user's scope; assert exports are scoped and, where the security program requires it, audited.
9. **Injection into accessible text**: place attacker-controlled strings (symbol aliases, watchlist names, journal tags, rule names, user display names) into fields that flow into accessible names and announcements; assert they are treated as text, cannot break out of the accessible name, and cannot forge a system message such as a fake Live-environment warning.
10. **Report/statement disclosure**: review the published accessibility statement and conformance report for internal hostnames, architecture detail, account identifiers or screenshots with real data.

Deliverables: a result table (case, method, expected, actual, verdict), defects for every failure with severity per `04-security-program.md`, and regression assertions added to `E47-Q03` or the security suite for every confirmed issue.

## Out of scope
- Network-level and backend-only attacks - owned by the API and auth epics.
- Full penetration testing (performed before R4 live enablement).
- Social-engineering scenarios.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: E47 abuse cases executed

  Scenario: Every case is executed with a recorded verdict
    Given the ten abuse cases
    When the suite is run against the release-candidate build
    Then each case records method, expected result, actual result and verdict
    And a case that could not be executed states why and is not recorded as a pass

  Scenario: Accessible surface enforces the same scoping as the visual surface
    Given a user with access to one account only
    When the full accessibility tree of an aggregating screen is enumerated
    Then no identifier, balance or position of any other account is present in any node

  Scenario: Failure case - a viewer finds an owner-only action in the tree
    Given a viewer session on an admin screen
    When a control absent from the visual UI is found in the accessibility tree and activated
    Then a high-severity finding is filed
    And the fix must remove the control server-side or from the render tree, not merely hide it with aria-hidden

  Scenario: Edge case - safety controls are not client-configurable
    Given a crafted preferences payload disabling destructive-action confirmation
    When it is sent directly to the API
    Then the server rejects it
    And the client-side confirmation still interposes if the preference is somehow set

  Scenario: Edge case - attacker-controlled text cannot forge a system announcement
    Given a watchlist named so as to imitate a live-environment warning
    When the name is announced
    Then it is announced as user content and cannot be mistaken for a system message
    And no markup or role injection occurs
```

## Technical notes / design
- Enumerating the accessibility tree is done programmatically (Playwright `accessibility.snapshot()` plus a DOM walk including `aria-hidden` and visually clipped nodes) rather than by listening with a screen reader; the machine finds nodes a human listener would never reach.
- The `aria-hidden` caveat is central: hiding a privileged control from AT is not authorisation. Cases 3 and 4 explicitly test for controls that are merely hidden, and the accepted fix is server-side enforcement plus not rendering.
- Preference and hotkey tampering is executed at the API level with a direct client, because the point is to bypass UI validation entirely.
- Case 9 strings include the standard injection corpus adapted for accessible names (markup, RTL overrides, zero-width characters, very long strings, newline-bearing values that could split an announcement).
- Every confirmed issue gets a regression assertion so the fix cannot silently regress in a later epic.

## Test plan
- The suite is the test. Its own validation: run cases 1, 2 and 3 against a deliberately vulnerable build (unmasked key in an `aria-label`, unscoped mirror data, an owner action left in the tree with `aria-hidden`) and confirm every case detects the issue. Without this, a clean result is indistinguishable from a broken detector.
- Re-run the suite after remediation to confirm closure; record both runs.

## Security notes
- Execution uses seeded demo accounts across roles (owner, manager, viewer) and the demo environment only; no live keys and no live order flow.
- Any confirmed leakage of real data during testing triggers the incident process in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, including rotation if key material is involved.
- Findings and evidence are stored in the security findings register with restricted access; raw captures containing leaked values are not committed to the repository.

## Accessibility notes
Remediation must preserve accessibility: the correct fix for an exposed privileged control is to not render it for that role (matching the visual surface), never to strip the accessible name or add `aria-hidden` to a control the user is legitimately allowed to use. Every fix proposed by this ticket is reviewed against that rule by the Accessibility role before it is accepted.

## Performance notes
Cases 7 and 8 double as availability tests: acceptance is not only "no crash" but that keyboard interaction stays within the interaction budget from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` while under attack-rate load, using the measurement approach from `E47-Q05`.

## Observability
- Findings tagged `epic:E47`, `type:abuse-case` in the security register.
- Where a mitigation is an audit event (hotkey profile activation, preference change affecting a safety control), the abuse case verifies the event is actually emitted and visible on SCR-135.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten abuse cases executed with recorded verdicts and evidence references.
- [ ] Detector validation against a deliberately vulnerable build evidenced for cases 1-3.
- [ ] Findings filed, severity-rated, owned; high-severity items fixed and re-tested before GA.
- [ ] Regression assertions added for every confirmed issue.
- [ ] Results fed to `E47-X04` and `E47-Q09`.

## Dependencies
- `E47-X01` - the threat model defines which cases are worth executing.
- `E47-Q03` - the enumeration and keyboard harness is reused rather than rebuilt.

title: Design QA of a11y remediation across all screens
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` a default-on gate for net-new UI: the built screen is compared against the design spec by a designer, and discrepancies are fixed or filed with a priority. For E47 the stakes are higher than usual, because the epic's output *is* a conformance claim — a remediation that was implemented approximately produces a conformance report that is false.

This ticket is the verification pass across every screen touched in Sprints 23–26, run against the acceptance checklists in the E47-D11 handoff pack and re-scored against the E47-D02 audit register so the epic's burn-down is evidence, not assertion. It deliberately sits *after* the build; unlike the other design tickets its input is code, not a blank frame.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Per-screen design-QA pass**: for every screen with findings, every acceptance checklist item verified against the built Electron build, with a pass/fail and evidence (screenshot, measured contrast value, keystroke trace, NVDA transcript excerpt as applicable).
- **Token-level fidelity check**: spacing, type scale, density, focus-ring geometry and colour values compared against the tokens rather than eyeballed, in dark, light and high-contrast at minimum, and in the three CVD palettes for any order-flow surface.
- **Re-scored audit register**: E47-D02's register updated per finding to `fixed` / `partially fixed` / `not fixed` / `superseded`, with the closing evidence attached, producing the blocker/major/minor counts the epic is measured against.
- **Discrepancy tickets**: every deviation either fixed within the sprint or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*` label and a named owner, per DoD §3.2 — never verbally waved through.
- **State coverage check**: each remediated screen verified in its empty, loading, error, populated and edge-density states (the catalogue's state convention), because remediation commonly fixes the populated state and leaves the error state inaccessible.
- **Regression check against untouched screens**: a sample of screens with no findings re-checked to confirm the design-system upgrade from E47-D10 did not regress them.
- **Exit report** summarising conformance status per screen, feeding E47-D13's conformance report directly.

## Out of scope
- Functional QA and the screen-reader test protocol passes (QA/SDET and the Accessibility role own those; this is design-fidelity and checklist verification).
- Writing fixes (filed as tickets or handled by the implementing engineer).
- Performance benchmarking (E46 and the perf-labelled stories).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every acceptance checklist item is verified with evidence
  Given the handoff pack's checklists
  When the design-QA pass completes
  Then every item has a pass or fail verdict with attached evidence
  And no item is marked pass on visual impression alone where a measured value was specified

Scenario: The audit register is re-scored honestly
  Given the original finding register
  When the pass completes
  Then every finding has a closing disposition with evidence
  And a finding whose fix is partial is recorded as partially fixed with the residual gap described, not closed

Scenario: Non-populated states are covered
  Given a remediated screen with error and empty states
  When those states are induced
  Then focus order, announcements, contrast and keyboard operation are verified in each state
  And a state that cannot be induced in the build is recorded as untested rather than assumed passing

Scenario: Design-system upgrade regressed an untouched screen (edge case)
  Given a screen with no findings that consumes the upgraded primitives
  When it is re-checked
  Then any regression is filed as a Bug against this epic with a priority label
  And the regression is not deferred past GA without an Owner decision

Scenario: A discrepancy is found late in Sprint 26 (failure path)
  Given a blocker discrepancy is found after the last remediation story is merged
  When it cannot be fixed before the sprint ends
  Then it is filed as a P0 Bug, the affected screen is marked non-conformant in the exit report
  And the conformance report in E47-D13 reflects that status rather than claiming full conformance
```

## Technical notes / design
- Verification uses the Electron production build, the only shipped surface per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1 — verifying a dev browser build would not substantiate the claim.
- Measured values (contrast ratios, target sizes, ring thickness) are captured with tooling and recorded numerically; "looks right" is not admissible evidence for this epic.
- The re-scored register uses the same schema and finding IDs as E47-D02 so the two can be diffed mechanically to produce the burn-down.
- The pass is run incrementally as stories merge (Sprints 23–26) with a consolidation pass in Sprint 25 and a final sweep at the end of Sprint 26, rather than one big-bang review that discovers everything too late to fix.

## Test plan
- Two reviewers split the screens; a 10% overlap sample is checked by both to detect verdict drift, with disagreements resolved by the Accessibility role.
- Every `not fixed` and `partially fixed` verdict is re-verified by a second reviewer before it is reported, because those verdicts carry release consequences.
- Evidence completeness audit: every pass verdict on a measured item must have a numeric value attached, checked automatically over the register.

## Security notes
- Design QA on admin and account screens uses seeded fixture data; evidence screenshots of SCR-120..129 must not capture real user identities or key metadata.
- Any accessibility discrepancy that is also a disclosure issue — e.g. an RBAC-hidden control reachable in the accessibility tree, or a masked value exposed to a surrogate — is escalated to the Security engineer immediately and filed at P0 regardless of its accessibility severity.

## Accessibility notes
- This pass is the design-side half of the evidence base; the QA/SDET screen-reader protocol passes (§8.2) are the other half, and the exit report states which findings were closed by which, so the conformance report can cite both.
- Reviewers perform every check keyboard-first, matching the user path being verified rather than clicking through with a mouse and inspecting afterwards.

## Performance notes
- Where a remediation carried a frame-budget number in its spec sheet, design QA records whether the built screen still meets it visually (no dropped frames on the canvas surfaces under live data); a visual regression is referred to E46 with the evidence rather than judged here.

## Observability
- The re-scored register publishes the epic's final blocker/major/minor counts against the E47-D02 baseline; that delta is the epic-level acceptance evidence required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2.

## Definition of Done
- All checklists verified with evidence; register re-scored and merged.
- All discrepancies fixed or filed with priority and owner.
- Exit report published and handed to E47-D13.
- Overlap-sample drift check completed.
- **CDO sign-off recorded as a comment; Status → Done only on that sign-off.** Accessibility role co-signs; QA/SDET acknowledges the exit report for the release checklist.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E47-D11` (the checklists it verifies against); in practice also gated by the Sprint 23–26 remediation stories merging.
- Feeds E47-D13 and the PRR/release checklist in `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Branch
`design/e47-design-qa`

## References

- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8, §9, §10
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (per-screen sign-off checklists and state conventions)

- `pnpm test:a11y`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e47-design-qa`
- PR title: "E47-D12: Design QA of a11y remediation across all screens"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-D12>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/design, area/design-system, priority/p0, design, design-qa, a11y

**Done means**

**Do NOT**
- Functional QA and the screen-reader test protocol passes (QA/SDET and the Accessibility role own those; this is design-fidelity and checklist verification).
- Writing fixes (filed as tickets or handled by the implementing engineer).
- Performance benchmarking (E46 and the perf-labelled stories).

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-D12` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Chaos scenarios: accessibility of degraded, disconnected and error states
body:
## Context
Accessibility audits overwhelmingly test happy paths, yet failure states are where accessible design matters most: a sighted user sees a banner turn amber and infers "data is stale"; a screen-reader user learns nothing unless the change is announced, and a keyboard user is stranded if a modal error boundary has no reachable action.

CandleViewer specifies a rich set of failure surfaces: SCR-152 disconnected/reconnecting, SCR-153 degraded mode, SCR-154 permission denied, SCR-155 not found, SCR-156 application error boundary, SCR-157 version mismatch, SCR-158 rate-limited, SCR-159 offline/shell states (browser offline, tailnet down, backend unreachable at boot, Electron GPU-process-crash recovery), plus SCR-047/SCR-048 chart empty and error states and SCR-073 lockout notice. These states are reached by chaos injection, not by clicking, so they need their own ticket.

This matters doubly for safety: a trader who cannot perceive that the feed is stale may act on dead prices. Connection and environment signalling is a risk control, not decoration.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A chaos suite (`e2e/a11y-chaos/`) inducing each condition and asserting its accessibility with the keyboard and announcement helpers from `E47-Q03`:
  1. **WS disconnect and reconnect** - SCR-152: the state change is announced assertively once (not per retry), the reconnect countdown is not a bare spinner, focus is not stolen, and the banner's retry action is keyboard-reachable.
  2. **Stale data / degraded mode** - SCR-153: staleness conveyed by text and icon, not only a dimmed colour; the degraded-capability list is readable; the DOM mirror reports the last-known-good timestamp.
  3. **Exchange 5xx and rate limit 10018** - SCR-158: the state names the condition in plain language and announces when normal operation resumes.
  4. **Backend unreachable / tailnet down / browser offline** - SCR-159: each state has a heading and a plain sentence, the Tailscale case names the exact condition, and recovery is announced automatically.
  5. **Renderer and GPU failure** - SCR-118 GPU-blacklisted and SCR-159 GPU-process-crash recovery: the software-fallback notice is announced, and SCR-045 still works when the canvas does not.
  6. **Application error boundary** - SCR-156: focus moves deliberately to the error region, which has a heading and a named recovery action, and no keyboard trap exists inside a broken subtree.
  7. **Permission denied and lockout** - SCR-154, SCR-073: the reason and remedy are announced; nothing communicates state only via a disabled-looking control.
  8. **Alert delivery under failure** - SCR-092: an alert triggered during a disconnect is still announced once and reachable from the notification centre SCR-014.
- Assertions per scenario: single announcement (no repetition storms), correct politeness level, focus preservation or deliberate focus move, keyboard reachability of every recovery action, non-colour-only state encoding, and contrast of state surfaces in all themes.
- A chaos-runbook appendix for states that cannot be automated reliably (real GPU-process crash, real tailnet loss), with an owner and a per-release cadence.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of reconnect, backoff and degraded behaviour - owned by data-plane and shell epics; this ticket asserts only how those states are perceived and operated.
- Backend-side chaos engineering and failover - owned by infra epics.
- Information-disclosure analysis of error messaging - `E47-X02`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Accessibility of failure states under chaos

  Scenario: A disconnect is announced exactly once and clearly
    Given the chart workspace is open with the tape streaming
    When the WebSocket connection is severed
    Then the disconnected state is announced assertively exactly once
    And the announcement names the condition and what to expect
    And no announcement repeats on each failed reconnect attempt

  Scenario: Recovery is perceivable without sight
    Given the application is in the reconnecting state
    When the connection is restored
    Then restoration is announced
    And any data gap is described rather than silently backfilled with no signal

  Scenario: Failure case - stale data conveyed only by colour is a defect
    Given degraded mode dims the price colour to indicate staleness
    When the grayscale and screen-reader checks run
    Then the absence of text or an icon conveying staleness fails the scenario
    And a P0 defect is filed because stale prices are a trading-safety signal

  Scenario: Edge case - the error boundary must not trap the keyboard
    Given a rendering error inside a docked panel triggers SCR-156
    When the user tabs through the resulting screen
    Then focus reaches the recovery action and can leave the error region
    And the error region has a heading and an accessible name

  Scenario: Edge case - canvas is dead but data is still readable
    Given the GPU process has crashed and software fallback is active
    When the user opens the SCR-045 table alternative
    Then the visible range data is still readable and navigable by keyboard
```

## Technical notes / design
- States are induced through deterministic test hooks and a proxy that can sever or delay the WS and return 429/5xx from REST, matching the fault taxonomy used by the data-plane chaos tests - this ticket reuses that harness rather than building a second one.
- "Announced exactly once" is implemented by counting live-region mutations over the scenario window, so a reconnect loop producing one announcement per attempt is caught. Announcement storms during outages are the most common real-world accessibility failure in trading UIs.
- Politeness policy comes from `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.2: conditions requiring user action (disconnect, lockout, rejected order) are assertive; informational changes are polite. A wrongly-assertive announcement is a defect because it interrupts.
- GPU-crash and tailnet-loss cases are automated where the harness allows and otherwise scripted in the runbook.

## Test plan
- Each scenario is self-validated twice: once confirming the assertion passes on the remediated build, once on a deliberately regressed build (announcement removed, focus stolen, colour-only staleness) confirming the assertion fails.
- Manual pass of the runbook items during the `E47-Q02` screen-reader window so a human confirms the automated verdicts are meaningful.

## Security notes
- Error states must not leak internals. The suite asserts that no scenario surfaces a stack trace, internal hostname, SQL fragment, API key or session token into a visible or announced string; the deep version is `E47-X02`, which this suite feeds with any hit.
- Permission-denied cases must not disclose the existence of resources the user cannot see; announced text must match visual text so the SR surface is not a disclosure side channel.

## Accessibility notes
Failure states are where the three-layer canvas strategy is proven: when the canvas cannot render, the DOM mirror and table alternative are not a nicety, they are the product. Any scenario where the fallback path is also broken is a P0.

## Performance notes
Reconnect storms create announcement storms, which create main-thread cost precisely while the client is recovering. The suite records live-region mutation rate and main-thread busy time during each chaos window and fails if announcement handling degrades keyboard responsiveness beyond the interaction budget.

## Observability
- Metrics: `a11y_chaos_announcements{scenario}`, `a11y_chaos_focus_lost{scenario}`, `a11y_chaos_recovery_announced{scenario}`.
- Failures are filed with the `a11y` label and appear on the `E47-Q04` burn-down; chaos results are part of the RC checklist in `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Chaos suite merged covering all eight scenario families, reusing the existing fault-injection harness.
- [ ] Regressed-build validation evidenced for every assertion class.
- [ ] Runbook appendix merged for non-automatable states with owner and cadence.
- [ ] Defects filed for every finding; no colour-only failure state remains.
- [ ] Results fed to `E47-T06` and the RC checklist.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q03` - reuses its keyboard, focus and live-region assertion helpers.
- `E47-S03` - remediation of state and notification surfaces must land first.

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-chaos`.

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-014, SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-073, SCR-092, SCR-118, SCR-152..SCR-159.

title: Exploratory accessibility charters with assistive-technology users
body:
## Context
Scripted passes find what they were written to find. The defects that matter most in a dense trading terminal - flows that are technically conformant but practically unusable - surface only when someone explores with intent. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` treats exploratory testing as first-class, and the accessibility standard's severity bar distinguishes "cannot complete" (P0) from "awkward but completable" (P1/P2), which is exactly the territory charters map.

E47 is also the last opportunity before GA to learn whether the accommodations designed in `E47-D01`/`E47-D02` and built in `E47-S01`..`E47-S04` actually help. A CVD-safe palette that passes simulation but leaves a trader unable to read a footprint at a glance is a failure no automated gate will report.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Six time-boxed exploratory charters (90 minutes each), in the standard charter form (explore <area> with <resources> to discover <information>):
  1. **Chart comprehension without sight** - SCR-030 + SCR-045 + the DOM mirror with NVDA: can a user form an accurate picture of recent price action and order flow, and how long does it take?
  2. **Executing a trade under time pressure** - SCR-060, SCR-076, SCR-063 keyboard-only: where does the flow become unsafe or ambiguous when hurrying?
  3. **Colour-vision-deficient order-flow reading** - SCR-050 heatmap, SCR-030 footprint, SCR-052 CVD under each CVD-safe palette: do bid/ask, buy/sell and imbalance remain distinguishable in practice?
  4. **Low-vision operation at 200-400% zoom** - the dense workspace SCR-020/021: reflow, clipping and hidden-control failures.
  5. **Rule building without a mouse** - SCR-081 form mode and SCR-082 node-graph mode: are the non-drag equivalents discoverable, not merely present?
  6. **Motor impairment and target size** - compact density across SCR-050, SCR-063, SCR-100: where is the 24px rule breached, and do documented essential exceptions have a workable alternative?
- **At least two sessions run with people who use assistive technology daily**, recruited via the UX research function; sessions are observed, not led, with a think-aloud protocol.
- Per charter: a session sheet (setup, duration, areas covered, risks found, defects filed, follow-up charters) committed under `qa/evidence/e47/exploratory/`.
- A consolidated findings memo separating conformance defects (feed the burn-down) from usability findings (feed `E49` polish and the design backlog), ranked by impact.
- Any newly discovered repeatable check is written back into `E47-Q01` (scripted case) or `E47-Q03` (automated assertion) - hardening the scripted suites is part of the deliverable.

## Out of scope
- Formal usability studies with statistical claims - these are qualitative charters.
- Remediation work; findings become tickets.
- Recruitment logistics beyond the brief handed to UX research.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Exploratory accessibility charters

  Scenario: All six charters are executed and recorded
    Given the charter set agreed with the Accessibility role
    When the sessions are run
    Then each charter has a session sheet stating what was covered and what was found
    And uncovered areas are stated explicitly rather than left implied

  Scenario: Real assistive-technology users are involved
    Given the recruitment brief sent to UX research
    When the sessions take place
    Then at least two sessions are run with participants who use assistive technology daily
    And their findings are recorded verbatim where they contradict the team's assumptions

  Scenario: Failure case - a technically conformant flow is unusable
    Given a flow that passes axe and the keyboard suite
    When a participant cannot complete it within the charter time box
    Then a defect is filed describing the practical obstacle
    And it is triaged against the severity bar rather than dismissed because the gates are green

  Scenario: Edge case - a CVD-safe palette passes simulation but fails in use
    Given the deuteranopia palette applied to the footprint
    When a participant cannot reliably identify imbalanced cells at a glance
    Then a design defect is filed against E47-D01 with the specific cell samples

  Scenario: Charters improve the scripted suites
    When the charters conclude
    Then every repeatable check discovered is added to E47-Q01 or E47-Q03
    And the memo names which suite each addition went to
```

## Technical notes / design
- Sessions run on the release-candidate build against the demo environment with the `E47-Q01` fixtures, so participants see realistic order flow with no live-trading capability.
- Time-boxing is enforced; an overrunning charter is split rather than extended, keeping findings attributable.
- Observers record keystrokes and announcements alongside commentary so a finding can be reproduced later by the team.
- Findings are triaged jointly by the Accessibility role and the SDET within two working days of each session, so remediation can still land inside R5.

## Test plan
The charters are the testing. Quality control on the activity itself: each session sheet is reviewed by someone who did not run the session, checking that findings are stated as observations (what happened) rather than conclusions (what should change), and that every finding has enough detail to reproduce.

## Security notes
- External participants must not see real account data. Sessions use the demo environment with seeded accounts and synthetic balances; screen sharing is reviewed beforehand for stray credentials or live windows.
- Participants sign the standard confidentiality terms; recordings are stored under the research retention policy and are never committed to the repository - only anonymised notes are.
- No participant is asked to authenticate with a real credential, and no session touches the live environment or a real API key.

## Accessibility notes
The research process must itself be accessible: materials are provided in plain text ahead of time, participants use their own AT setup and versions (recorded - differences from the pinned matrix are valuable data), and consent and instructions are given in whatever modality the participant prefers.

## Performance notes
Charters 1 and 3 run at least partly against the high-tick-rate replay fixture; perceived performance of the accommodations under load is exactly the finding that `E47-Q05` quantifies but does not interpret. Any perceived-lag report is cross-checked against the `E47-Q05` metrics.

## Observability
- Findings are filed into the QA result store with `epic:E47`, `source:exploratory`, so the burn-down separates scripted from exploratory discovery - the ratio is itself a signal about scripted coverage.
- The memo is an input to the R5 PRR and to the `E49` polish backlog.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Six charters executed and session sheets committed.
- [ ] At least two sessions run with daily AT users, via UX research.
- [ ] Consolidated memo merged, separating conformance defects from usability findings, ranked by impact.
- [ ] Every repeatable check written back into `E47-Q01` or `E47-Q03`, with the destination named.
- [ ] Findings triaged with owners; P0s scheduled inside R5.
- [ ] Participant data handled per the research retention policy; nothing sensitive committed.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q02` - scripted screen-reader passes run first so charters explore beyond known defects.

## Branch
`chore/e47-exploratory-a11y` (evidence and memo only).

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (exploratory testing, severity taxonomy).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3.4.7 (target size, essential exceptions), 4.2 (CVD), 8.2 item 5 (severity bar).
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md` (participant profiles to approximate).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-050, SCR-052, SCR-060, SCR-063, SCR-081, SCR-082, SCR-100.
- `docs/plan/backlog/E49.json` (where usability findings land).

2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Commands**

- `pnpm test:a11y`

- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e47-exploratory-a11y`

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-Q07>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/test, area/design-system, priority/p2, qa, a11y, ux-research

**Done means**

- Every repeatable check written back into `E47-Q01` or `E47-Q03`, with the destination named.
- Findings triaged with owners; P0s scheduled inside R5.
- Participant data handled per the research retention policy; nothing sensitive committed.

**Do NOT**
- Formal usability studies with statistical claims - these are qualitative charters.
- Remediation work; findings become tickets.

title: Accessibility regression pack and cross-epic guardrails for future screens
body:
## Context
Accessibility conformance decays. Every epic after E47 adds screens, components and streaming surfaces, and each is an opportunity to reintroduce a defect E47 paid to remove. The roadmap dependency `E47 -> E49` in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 exists because the polish epic inherits this obligation.

The gates built in `E47-Q03`..`E47-Q06` each protect one dimension. What does not exist is (a) a single curated **regression pack** constituting "the accessibility suite" for a release candidate, and (b) the **guardrails** that make it impossible for a new screen to ship without joining that pack.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A curated **regression pack** (`qa/packs/e47-a11y-regression.md` plus a CI target) composed of: the keyboard-only journeys, the accessibility-tree snapshots, the full-inventory axe and Lighthouse scan, the motion/flash audit, the chaos accessibility scenarios, and the manual screen-reader smoke subset identified in `E47-Q01`. It states which parts run per PR, per merge to `main`, nightly, and per release candidate.
- **Guardrails** preventing silent gaps:
  1. Screen-inventory check: any screen id in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` absent from the scan inventory and snapshot set fails CI.
  2. Component check: a design-system component added without a documented keyboard-interaction table and accessible-name/role table fails its own package CI (standard section 11.6, enforced).
  3. Ticket-template check: the `a11y` label conditions from `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` are asserted by the PR template checklist; a screen-touching PR without an accessibility acceptance-criteria block is flagged in review.
  4. Canvas check: any new `<canvas>` without an `aria-label` and a registered DOM-mirror root fails the keyboard/snapshot suite.
- A **new-screen onboarding recipe**: one page telling an engineer in a later epic exactly what to add (inventory entry, snapshot, journey, axe entry, AC block) when they create a screen, with worked examples.
- Ownership and cadence written into `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` so the pack has a named owner after E47 closes rather than becoming orphaned CI.
- A dry run of the full pack against the RC build with recorded wall-clock duration, so the RC window in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` can budget for it.

## Out of scope
- Building new checks - this ticket composes and guards what `E47-Q03`..`E47-Q06` built.
- Retrofitting checks to closed epics beyond the screen-inventory reconciliation.
- Product remediation of dry-run findings; those become defects.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Accessibility regression pack and guardrails

  Scenario: The pack is a single, runnable target
    Given the release-candidate build
    When an engineer runs the documented pack target
    Then every constituent suite executes and a consolidated report is produced
    And the report states pass/fail per dimension and overall

  Scenario: A new screen cannot skip the pack
    Given a PR adding a screen to the catalogue and to the app
    When the guardrail check runs
    And the screen has no scan entry and no accessibility-tree snapshot
    Then CI fails naming the screen id and the missing artefacts

  Scenario: Failure case - a new canvas without a mirror is blocked
    Given a new panel rendering data to a canvas element
    When the suite runs
    And the canvas has no aria-label and no registered DOM-mirror root
    Then the check fails referencing 05-accessibility-standard.md section 6

  Scenario: Edge case - a design-system component without a11y documentation is blocked
    Given a new component added to the shared library
    When the design-system package CI runs
    And the component lacks its keyboard-interaction or accessible-name table
    Then the component's own tests fail and it cannot be published

  Scenario: The pack fits the release window
    When the dry run completes
    Then its wall-clock duration is recorded
    And 07-release-and-prr.md is updated with the measured figure rather than an estimate
```

## Technical notes / design
- One inventory, many consumers: the machine-readable screen inventory from `E47-Q04` is the single source for scans, snapshots and guardrails. A second list would drift within a sprint.
- The canvas guardrail is a runtime assertion in test builds (walk the DOM for canvases, check label and mirror registry) rather than a lint rule, because canvases are created dynamically by the engine.
- The consolidated report is a generated artefact with a stable schema so `E47-T06` can consume it directly and the dashboard needs no bespoke parsing.
- Ownership after E47 is named in `03-testing-strategy.md` as the Accessibility role with SDET as delegate, matching standard section 8.3.

## Test plan
- Guardrail validation by injection: add a fake screen with no scan entry, a canvas with no label, and a component with no a11y tables on a scratch branch; all three must fail with actionable messages.
- Run the full pack twice on an unchanged build to confirm determinism and measure duration variance.
- Generate the consolidated report from two runs and diff the structure to confirm schema stability.

## Security notes
- The consolidated report aggregates artefacts from suites capturing DOM, frames and transcripts; it inherits the redaction post-processing from `E47-Q04` and `E47-Q05` rather than re-exposing raw artefacts.
- The pack runs against demo/staging only; the CI identity must not hold live-environment credentials, consistent with `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` environment separation.

## Accessibility notes
The recipe document is the durable deliverable: most future defects will be prevented by an engineer reading one page at the moment they create a screen, not by anyone re-reading the full standard. It must be short, concrete, worked-example-driven, and link to the standard rather than paraphrase it.

## Performance notes
The pack is tiered so per-PR cost stays inside the envelope from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` while expensive full-inventory and motion work runs nightly and per RC. The measured dry-run duration is what makes the tiering defensible rather than arbitrary.

## Observability
- The consolidated report is published per RC and retained with the release record; the `E47-Q04` dashboard gains a "last full pack" tile showing date, verdict and duration.
- Guardrail failures are counted (`a11y_guardrail_failures{kind}`) so a rising trend reveals a process gap rather than individual carelessness.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Regression pack defined, wired as a single CI target, with per-PR / nightly / RC tiering documented.
- [ ] All four guardrails implemented and validated by injection.
- [ ] New-screen onboarding recipe merged and linked from the contribution guide and design-system docs.
- [ ] Ownership and cadence recorded in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.
- [ ] Dry run executed against the RC build with duration recorded in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`.
- [ ] Handover note to `E49` describing how the pack is maintained.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q03`, `E47-Q04`, `E47-Q06` - the pack composes their suites.

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-regression-pack`.

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 8.3 (ownership), 9 (gates), 11 (design-system requirements incl. 11.6).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (suite ownership, cadence).
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (RC window, PRR gates).
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` (`a11y` label conditions).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (screen inventory source).
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 (E47 -> E49 dependency).
