title: Focus order, focus visibility, target size and drag alternatives
body:
## Context
The WCAG 2.2-specific criteria are the ones most likely to be outstanding, because they postdate most teams' habits and because CandleViewer's multi-pane density makes them genuinely hard: **2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured** (floating toolbars and docked panels over a focused control), **2.5.7 Dragging Movements** (order-line reprice, drawing handles, node moves, panel resize), **2.5.8 Target Size** (24 px minimum in a UI whose compact density exists specifically to fit more), **3.2.6 Consistent Help**, **3.3.7 Redundant Entry**, **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication**.

`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.4 specifies the answers — landmark regions with `Ctrl+\` cycling, roving tabindex, focus never stolen, dialog focus trap and return, skip links, a ≥2 px ≥3:1 focus ring that is a design token and never removed, the 24 px rule with its documented essential exception, a non-drag alternative for every drag, consistent help placement, and redundant-entry/auth rules. This Story closes the E47-T01 findings across all of them, app-wide.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Landmarks and skip links**: every major panel (Chart, DOM/Heatmap, Order Ticket, Positions & Orders, Watchlist, Rule Builder) is a labelled region; `Ctrl+\` cycles regions; skip links appear on the app shell (**SCR-010**) and are visible on focus.
- **Focus visibility and obstruction**: the focus-ring token audited across dark, light and high-contrast themes for ≥2 px and ≥3:1; any `outline: none` without an equivalent replacement removed; sticky toolbars, docked panels and floating windows (**SCR-021**, **SCR-027**) audited so a focused control is never fully obscured, with scroll-into-view padding where needed.
- **Focus order and return**: tab order matches visual order per screen; every dialog (**SCR-029**, **SCR-064**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-074**, **SCR-076**, **SCR-085**, **SCR-129**, **SCR-149**) traps focus, is `Esc`-dismissible, and returns focus to its trigger; no live update moves focus.
- **Target size**: a 24 px audit across all interactive controls at both densities, with each essential exception explicitly registered plus its alternative.
- **Drag alternatives**: order-line reprice, drawing handle move, node move, panel resize and column resize each gain (or are verified to have) a discrete keyboard or menu equivalent.
- **Consistent help, redundant entry, accessible auth**: the `?` cheatsheet and help entry point occupy the same relative position on every screen; order tickets pre-fill safely per US-SET-003's defaults; **SCR-001…SCR-006** and **SCR-149** verified to require no cognitive-function test, with TOTP/WebAuthn treated as the permitted alternative.

## Out of scope
- Canvas-internal focus models — **E47-S01**, **E47-S02**, **E47-S03**.
- Visual redesign to create space for larger targets — findings needing layout change are routed to **E49** with the a11y rationale attached.
- Changing authentication factors — **E43**/**E09**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Regions are reachable and named
  Given the workspace is open with chart, ladder, ticket and positions panels
  When Ctrl+backslash is pressed repeatedly
  Then focus moves between named regions and each region's name is announced
  And the same regions appear in the screen reader's landmark list

Scenario: A focused control is never hidden
  Given a control near a sticky toolbar receives focus by keyboard
  Then it is scrolled into view such that it is not fully obscured

Scenario: Every drag has a discrete equivalent
  Given an order line, a drawing handle, a graph node, a panel edge and a table column
  Then each can be repositioned or resized using keyboard or a menu with discrete values
  And no capability exists that requires dragging

Scenario: Dialogs trap and return focus
  Given any confirmation dialog is opened from a keyboard-focused trigger
  Then focus is trapped inside it, Esc cancels safely, and focus returns to the trigger on close

Scenario: Targets meet the minimum or are registered exceptions
  Given compact density is active
  Then every interactive control is at least 24 by 24 CSS px or has 24 px spacing
  And any exception is present in the register with a named alternative

Scenario: Authentication needs no puzzle
  Given the login and step-up flows
  Then no cognitive-function test is required and credentials may be pasted from a password manager

Scenario: Help is where it always was
  Given any screen in the app
  Then the help entry point and the cheatsheet shortcut are in the same relative location and order
```

## Technical notes / design
The focus ring is fixed once in the token layer rather than per component, which converts a long tail of findings into one change plus a lint that forbids removing outlines. Focus-not-obscured is handled by a shared scroll-into-view helper that accounts for registered sticky-chrome insets, so future chrome does not reintroduce the defect. Drag alternatives reuse the existing nudge/menu patterns from E14 drawings rather than inventing new interaction vocabulary.

## Test plan
Automated: accessibility-tree snapshots for landmark and heading structure per screen; a focus-order test per top-level screen; a target-size scan against computed styles at both densities; a lint forbidding un-replaced `outline: none`. E2E keyboard-only: region cycling, skip links, dialog trap/return, each drag alternative. Manual: NVDA landmark navigation spot-check.

## Security notes
Dialog focus-trap fixes must not weaken destructive-action confirms; `Esc` always means cancel, never confirm. Skip links must not bypass an authentication or step-up gate. Accessible-authentication work must not reduce 2FA strength — the exemption covers object-recognition factors, not removing the factor.

## Accessibility notes
Direct implementation of §3.4.1–§3.4.10. WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8, 4.1.2.

## Performance notes
The scroll-into-view helper runs on focus change only and must not force synchronous layout in a frame that also renders the canvas. Landmark structure is static markup with no runtime cost.

## Observability
CI-published counts of focus-order snapshot diffs and target-size violations per screen; client metric `a11y_focus_steal_count` (expected zero) shared with E47-S01.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests or recorded manual steps.
- [ ] E47-T01 findings in the focus, target-size and drag patterns closed or registered as exceptions with alternatives.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages.
- [ ] axe, keyboard-E2E and a11y-tree-snapshot gates green across all top-level screens.
- [ ] Focus-ring token verified in all three themes; outline lint enabled.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` focus contracts and `16-design-system-brief.md` focus token reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T01**. Feeds **E47-T04**, **E47-T05**; layout-change findings hand off to **E49**.

## Branch
`feat/e47-focus-target-drag`

## References
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.4; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010, SCR-021, SCR-027, SCR-029, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-074, SCR-076, SCR-085, SCR-129, SCR-149; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-001, US-SET-003.

title: High-contrast and CVD-safe themes across every order-flow encoding
body:
## Context
**US-SET-004 Themes and density (Must)** requires that a theme switch update "every surface including WebGL canvases immediately without reload, keeping contrast ratios compliant", and that compact density keeps targets ≥24 px. **US-SET-005 Colour conventions and CVD-safe palettes (Must)** requires that changing the convention or selecting a CVD-safe palette updates "every chart, DOM, heatmap, footprint, bubble and profile surface consistently", that side and direction remain distinguishable without colour "through glyphs, signs or patterns everywhere", and — as an NFR — "an automated check asserts no view depends on hue alone".

**E47-T03** has by now produced the evidence: which token pairs and which gradient stops fail, in which theme and density, and which colour pairs collapse under CVD simulation. This Story fixes them and makes the no-hue-alone rule enforceable rather than aspirational.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Remediate every failing pair and gradient stop from the T03 matrix across dark, light and high-contrast themes at both densities — adjusting tokens and gradient ramps, not adding per-component overrides.
- Ship/complete the **high-contrast theme** (`Ctrl+Shift+H`, §5.6) as a full token-set swap reaching the ≥7:1 body-text bar, covering chrome *and* data-ink, with the WebGL surfaces re-uploading their palettes on switch without a reload.
- Ship/complete the **CVD-safe palettes** as tested design tokens (US-SET-005 NFR) selectable on **SCR-116**, applied consistently to chart, DOM, heatmap, footprint, bubbles and profiles.
- Implement the **no-hue-alone automated check**: an enumerated inventory of semantic encodings (buy/sell, bid/ask, order status, P&L, connection health, demo/live, imbalance, delta sign, risk severity) each asserted to carry at least one non-colour channel (glyph, sign, text, pattern or position) on every surface that renders it; a surface that renders an encoding without a registered non-colour channel fails the build.
- Legend obligations: every affected view states its convention in a legend (US-SET-005 scenario 1) and the LIVE/DEMO badge remains text-plus-colour on every screen (§4.1).
- Density verification: compact density keeps ≥24 px targets and re-evaluates the large-text contrast threshold (paired with E47-S05).

## Out of scope
- Generating the contrast/CVD evidence — **E47-T03**.
- The accessibility preference UI — **E47-S07**; theme selection lives on SCR-116.
- Re-designing order-flow visual language beyond what conformance requires — **E49**/design.
- Print/export colour.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Theme switch reaches the canvas immediately
  Given the chart, heatmap and footprint are rendering
  When the theme is switched to high contrast
  Then every DOM and WebGL surface repaints in the new palette without a reload
  And the contrast matrix for that theme reports no failing pair

Scenario: A CVD-safe palette applies everywhere at once
  When a colour-blind-safe palette is selected
  Then chart, DOM, heatmap, footprint, bubble and profile surfaces all adopt it
  And no surface is left on the previous palette

Scenario: No view depends on hue alone
  Given the encoding inventory covers buy/sell, bid/ask, order status, P&L, health, demo/live, imbalance and delta sign
  When the automated check runs
  Then every surface rendering an encoding declares a non-colour channel
  And a surface that declares none fails the build naming the surface and encoding

Scenario: Inverting the convention is consistent
  Given the user inverts the buy/sell convention
  Then every affected surface and every legend reflects the inversion
  And no surface retains the old convention

Scenario: High contrast holds the higher bar
  Given the high-contrast theme
  Then body text pairs meet 7:1 and non-text pairs meet 3:1 across chrome and data-ink

Scenario: Compact density does not break the rules
  Given compact density in any theme
  Then targets remain at least 24 px or spaced accordingly
  And text that drops below the large-text threshold is evaluated at 4.5:1 and passes
```

## Technical notes / design
The encoding inventory is the durable artefact: a declarative registry mapping each semantic encoding to the surfaces that render it and the non-colour channel each provides. That registry is what makes the NFR testable — without it, "no view depends on hue alone" can only be spot-checked. Palette changes propagate to the engine as a uniform/texture update rather than a scene rebuild, which is what makes the no-reload requirement achievable.

## Test plan
Unit: registry completeness (every enumerated encoding has at least one surface and one channel). Automated: contrast matrix regeneration green; CVD discriminability green; the no-hue-alone check. Visual regression: grayscale and CVD-simulated snapshots of chart, footprint, ladder, heatmap, bubbles and profiles per theme. E2E: theme and palette switch while streaming, asserting no reload and no re-subscription. Manual: designer + Accessibility role review of the simulated snapshots.

## Security notes
The demo/live distinction must never become colour-only under any theme or palette — the LIVE badge is text plus colour on every screen, and a CVD palette selection may not remove it. Theme and palette are per-user presentation settings with no authorisation effect.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §4.1–§4.4 (colour independence), §5.1–§5.7 (contrast, high-contrast theme, text resize). WCAG SCs: 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.4, 1.4.10, 1.4.11, 1.4.12.

## Performance notes
Palette switching must be a uniform/texture update, not a geometry rebuild; measure switch cost and keep it under one frame on the reference machine. The no-hue-alone check is static analysis plus registry validation with no runtime cost.

## Observability
`settings.theme_changed{theme}` and `settings.palette_changed{palette}` analytics; CI-published failing-pair count per theme, trending to zero.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests.
- [ ] T03 matrix reports zero failing pairs across all three themes and both densities.
- [ ] Encoding inventory complete and enforced by the no-hue-alone check.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages.
- [ ] SCR-116 design-qa comparison recorded; CVD-simulated snapshots reviewed and signed off.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` palettes and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-116 reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review with a live theme switch over streaming data.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T03** (evidence and the failing list). Related to **E47-S02** (surfaces that consume the palette) and **E47-S05** (density/target size); feeds **E47-T05**.

## Branch
`feat/e47-contrast-cvd-themes`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-004, US-SET-005 (§27 SET); `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §4, §5; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-031, SCR-051, SCR-116; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-031, CMP-062, CMP-063, CMP-113, CMP-136, CMP-228.

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Interfaces you must not break**

**Commands**

- `pnpm test:a11y`

- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-S06>`

- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/feature, area/design-system, priority/p1, design, design-qa, a11y, qa

**Done means**
- All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests.
- T03 matrix reports zero failing pairs across all three themes and both densities.
- Encoding inventory complete and enforced by the no-hue-alone check.
- Coverage ≥80% on touched packages.
- SCR-116 design-qa comparison recorded; CVD-simulated snapshots reviewed and signed off.
- `16-design-system-brief.md` palettes and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-116 reconciled with shipped behaviour.

**Do NOT**
- Generating the contrast/CVD evidence — **E47-T03**.
- The accessibility preference UI — **E47-S07**; theme selection lives on SCR-116.
- Re-designing order-flow visual language beyond what conformance requires — **E49**/design.
- Print/export colour.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-S06` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Settings, hotkey layer and destructive-confirm keyboard conformance
body:
## Context
Three SET Must stories carry accessibility NFRs that only a conformance pass can settle. **US-SET-001** requires the settings screen be "fully keyboard operable; every control has a persistent label, not placeholder-only text". **US-SET-002** requires one global hotkey layer with conflict detection and reserved-key refusal — which `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.3 elaborates into precedence rules, a detection algorithm, permanently reserved keys (`Esc`, `Ctrl+K`) and an OS-combo blocklist. **US-SET-003** requires each destructive action to be configurable as dialog, hold-to-confirm or immediate — and §3.1.4 forbids any mouse-hold-only or timing-only gate: hold-to-confirm must have a discrete-press keyboard fallback.

These are the SET stories where accessibility and *trading safety* are the same requirement: a hotkey a keyboard user cannot reach, or a confirm they cannot complete, is both an AA failure and a risk of an unintended order.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-110 Settings home / SCR-111 / SCR-112 / SCR-114 / SCR-115 / SCR-118 / SCR-119**: full keyboard traversal, persistent visible labels on every control, scope indicator (per user / workspace / symbol / account) exposed as text, search results announced with count and section path, and the reset-preview flow operable and announced.
- **SCR-113 Hotkey editor**: bind-time conflict detection announced, not merely coloured; conflicting action pairs named in text with the one-click swap reachable by keyboard; reserved keys (`Esc`, `Ctrl+K`) excluded from the pickable set with an explanation; OS/Electron-reserved combos filtered out rather than allowed-then-failed; trading-critical bindings refused as unmodified single letters with the reason announced.
- **SCR-013 cheatsheet** (`?`) reflects current, possibly remapped bindings, read from `GET /api/v1/me/hotkeys`, and is reachable from every screen in the same relative place (3.2.6).
- **Hold-to-confirm**: a discrete-press keyboard fallback everywhere hold is offered; the 300–2000 ms duration is configurable with a visible, non-colour-only progress indicator; progress is announced at start and completion; releasing early cancels and says so.
- **Immediate mode** acknowledgement dialog is keyboard-operable and the choice is audited; the Live-stricter-than-Demo rule holds regardless of accessibility settings.
- Remediation of E47-T01 findings on **SCR-015**, **SCR-029**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-076**, **SCR-129** confirm surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Accessibility preferences — **E47-S07**; appearance/theme — **E47-S06**.
- Adding new hotkeys or changing the default keymap in §3.2.
- Confirm-policy business rules beyond their keyboard operability — **E39**/**E44**.
- Settings persistence backend changes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Settings are fully operable from the keyboard
  Given the settings home screen
  When the user traverses with Tab and arrow keys only
  Then every control is reachable, labelled with persistent visible text, and its scope is announced
  And searching announces the number of matches and each match's section path

Scenario: A conflict is explained, not just coloured
  Given Ctrl+Shift+F is already bound to flatten
  When the user tries to bind it to another action
  Then the conflict is announced naming both actions, the save is blocked, and a keyboard-reachable swap option is offered

Scenario: Reserved and OS keys are refused with a reason
  When the user attempts to bind Esc, Ctrl+K or an OS-reserved combination
  Then the key is not offered or the attempt is refused with a spoken reason

Scenario: Hold-to-confirm has a keyboard path
  Given flatten is configured as hold-to-confirm
  When the action is invoked from the keyboard
  Then a discrete-press confirmation is available that does not require holding
  And if hold is used, progress is announced and releasing early cancels with an announcement

Scenario: Immediate mode is an informed choice
  When any destructive action is set to immediate
  Then a keyboard-operable acknowledgement states the consequence, and the choice is written to the audit log

Scenario: Live is never weakened by an accessibility path
  Given Demo has a weaker confirm policy than Live
  Then Live does not inherit it, and no accessibility setting can relax a Live confirm

Scenario: The cheatsheet tells the truth
  Given bindings have been remapped
  When the cheatsheet is opened with the question-mark key
  Then it lists the current bindings, from the same relative location on every screen
```

## Technical notes / design
Conflict detection already exists as specified in §3.3.2 (compute the new combo's active focus-context set, intersect with existing bindings); the accessibility work is making its *output* perceivable — announced text naming both actions — rather than an inline red border. Hold-to-confirm gains a paired discrete control rather than a separate code path, so the policy engine sees one confirmation result either way. The cheatsheet reads resolved bindings from the API so remaps cannot drift from documentation.

## Test plan
Unit: conflict detection across focus contexts; reserved/blocklisted key filtering; hold-progress state machine including early release. E2E keyboard-only: settings traversal and search, remap with conflict and swap, each confirm mode for flatten and cancel-all in demo. Manual SR: NVDA pass over SCR-110, SCR-113, SCR-117 and one confirm of each mode. Gates: axe, Lighthouse, keyboard-E2E on the settings band.

## Security notes
This Story touches destructive-action policy, so it is `security`-labelled: no accessibility affordance may reduce a confirmation below its configured strength, bypass the arm token for one-click entry, or weaken the Live-stricter-than-Demo invariant. Setting a policy to immediate is an audited event with actor, timestamp and prior value. Hotkey profiles are per-user and written via the authenticated `/settings/hotkeys` endpoints; a profile may not bind an action the user's role cannot perform.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §3.1.3–§3.1.6, §3.2, §3.3, §3.4.4 and §3.4.9. WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.4 (character key shortcuts — the modifier requirement on trading-critical bindings is the mitigation), 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 3.2.6, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 3.3.4, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Hotkey dispatch stays O(1) per keystroke via the resolved binding map; announcement of hold progress is throttled to start/complete rather than per animation frame so a screen reader is not flooded during a 2 s hold.

## Observability
`settings.hotkey_conflict_shown`, `settings.hotkey_swapped`, `settings.confirm_policy_changed{action,mode}` (also audited), `confirm.hold_cancelled` analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests or recorded manual steps.
- [ ] E47-T01 findings on the settings and confirm surfaces closed or registered as exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages.
- [ ] axe, Lighthouse and keyboard-E2E green across the settings band; NVDA pass recorded.
- [ ] Security review comment present (destructive-policy surface); audit entries verified for immediate-mode changes.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-013/SCR-110/SCR-113 and `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2/§3.3 reconciled with shipped bindings.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed keyboard-only at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T01**. Related to **E47-S03** (rule-editor bindings register through the same global layer); feeds **E47-T04**, **E47-T05**.

## Branch
`feat/e47-settings-hotkeys-confirm-a11y`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-001, US-SET-002, US-SET-003 (§27 SET); `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-013, SCR-015, SCR-029, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-110, SCR-113, SCR-129; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/settings/hotkeys`, `/me/hotkeys`, `/settings/arm`; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-022, CMP-049, CMP-054, CMP-064, CMP-211, CMP-212.

## Agent execution brief

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Commands**

title: SAST/DAST rules and CI guards for accessible-surface data parity
body:
## Context
`E47-X02` proves the abuse cases at a point in time. Without automation those proofs expire: the next epic adds a panel, someone writes an `aria-label` from an unmasked field, and the parity guarantee quietly dies. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep) and DAST (OWASP ZAP) as CI gates; this ticket adds the rules specific to the accessible surface so the E47 guarantees are enforced continuously.

The rules encode one idea: **anything that can be read by a person can be read by a machine, and the accessible text path must be as carefully controlled as the visual one**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Semgrep/CodeQL rules** for the web and design-system packages:
  1. A taint-style rule flagging values from fields classified as secret or masked (API key fields, TOTP, session tokens) flowing into `aria-label`, `aria-describedby` targets, live-region text, DOM-mirror node text or table-alternative cells.
  2. A rule flagging `aria-hidden="true"` applied to an interactive element, and flagging any use of `aria-hidden` as the sole mechanism gating a privileged control (the anti-pattern `E47-X02` case 3 tests).
  3. A rule flagging `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or equivalent inside mirror, live-region or accessible-name construction paths - accessible text must be text.
  4. A rule flagging `outline: none` (or equivalent focus suppression) without an adjacent compliant focus style, enforcing standard section 3.1 statically as well as at runtime.
  5. A rule flagging construction of accessible names by string concatenation with user-controlled values without the shared sanitiser, so case 9 of the abuse suite cannot recur.
  6. A rule requiring every `<canvas>` creation site in product code to register a mirror root, complementing the runtime guardrail in `E47-Q08`.
- **DAST/ZAP configuration additions**: authenticated scans as viewer, manager and owner against the screens that render accessible mirrors, with a passive rule inspecting response bodies for privileged field names appearing in accessibility attributes; plus a scan profile exercising `/api/v1/me/preferences` and `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*` with malformed and privilege-escalating payloads.
- **CI wiring**: new rules run in the existing SAST/DAST jobs as required checks; findings are triaged into the security findings register, not printed and forgotten.
- A short rule-authoring note so future teams can extend the rule set, including how to add a field to the secret/masked classification list that rule 1 reads.

## Out of scope
- Generic web SAST/DAST coverage - already established by the security program; this ticket only adds accessibility-surface-specific rules.
- Dependency scanning and container scanning - unchanged.
- Fixing the issues the new rules surface on existing code (beyond suppressions with owners and dates); those become defects.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Accessibility-surface SAST and DAST rules

  Scenario: Secret-to-accessible-text flow is detected statically
    Given code that assigns an unmasked API-key value to an aria-label
    When SAST runs
    Then the rule fires with the file, line and the classified field name
    And the check blocks merge

  Scenario: aria-hidden on an interactive element is flagged
    Given a focusable button marked aria-hidden true
    When SAST runs
    Then the rule fires and references 05-accessibility-standard.md

  Scenario: Failure case - false positives are managed, not normalised
    Given a rule that fires on a legitimate pattern
    When a suppression is added
    Then it carries a justification, an owner and an expiry date
    And an expired suppression fails the build

  Scenario: Edge case - DAST detects a privileged field name in an accessibility attribute
    Given an authenticated viewer scan of an admin-adjacent screen
    When the passive rule inspects the response
    And a privileged field name appears inside an aria attribute
    Then a finding is raised with the URL and the attribute

  Scenario: Rules are maintainable
    Given the rule-authoring note
    When an engineer adds a new masked field to the classification list
    Then rule 1 covers it without any rule code change
```

## Technical notes / design
- Rule 1 depends on a **field classification list** (which fields are secret/masked). That list must be a single committed artefact shared with the redaction post-processors in `E47-Q04` and `E47-Q05`; three copies of the list is how this rots.
- Static analysis of accessible names is inherently approximate in a React codebase; the rules are tuned for a low false-positive rate and paired with the runtime checks in `E47-Q03`/`E47-Q08`, which catch what static analysis cannot see. Neither layer is claimed sufficient alone, and the note says so.
- ZAP authenticated scans reuse the seeded role accounts from the existing security jobs; scans run against staging/demo only, never live.
- Findings flow into the same register as `E47-X01`/`E47-X02` so the epic's security posture is one list.

## Test plan
- Each rule is validated against a **positive fixture** (code that must trigger it) and a **negative fixture** (similar code that must not), both committed under the rule set - the only way to keep rules honest as the codebase changes.
- The DAST addition is validated against a deliberately vulnerable staging build exposing a privileged field name in an aria attribute; the scan must report it.
- Run the rules across the full existing codebase, record the baseline, and triage every hit before the check becomes blocking.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* security tooling. Two cautions: rule output can itself disclose sensitive values if it echoes matched content, so findings report locations and classifications rather than raw values; and scan artefacts inherit the redaction and retention rules used elsewhere in the epic.

## Accessibility notes
The rules are written so the compliant fix is always the accessible one: rule 2 pushes towards not rendering privileged controls rather than hiding them from AT; rule 4 pushes towards a compliant focus style rather than removing focus indication; rule 3 pushes towards plain text rather than markup in announcements. A rule whose easiest fix degrades accessibility is a badly written rule and must be revised.

## Performance notes
The added SAST rules must not materially extend CI time; measure before and after and keep the delta within the envelope agreed in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. Authenticated DAST scans are slower and run on merge to `main` and nightly rather than per PR, with the split documented.

## Observability
- Metrics: `sec_a11y_rule_findings{rule,severity}`, `sec_a11y_suppressions_active`, `sec_dast_a11y_findings`.
- New findings notify the Security engineer; a rule firing for the first time in months is worth a human look rather than an auto-suppression.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Six SAST rules merged with positive and negative fixtures each.
- [ ] DAST profile additions merged and validated against a vulnerable staging build.
- [ ] Shared field-classification list extracted and consumed by the rules and both redaction post-processors.
- [ ] Baseline triaged; checks required on `main`; suppression policy with expiry enforced.
- [ ] Rule-authoring note merged and linked from the security program docs.
- [ ] CI duration delta measured and within the agreed envelope.

## Dependencies
- `E47-X01` - the threat model determines which rules are worth writing.
- `E47-X02` - confirmed issues become the rules' positive fixtures.

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-security-rules`.

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (SAST/DAST tooling, gate placement, findings register, suppression policy).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3.1 (focus visibility), 6.1-6.3 (mirror, live regions, tables).
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks).
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (CI time envelope).
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/me/preferences`, `/settings/hotkeys*` (DAST targets).

title: ADR and operator docs for the accessible-surface parity and evidence model
body:
## Context
E47 establishes two decisions that outlive the epic and are currently implicit in ticket bodies rather than recorded where an architect would look for them.

First, the **accessible-surface parity rule**: the DOM mirror, live regions and table alternatives are a first-class representation of the product, derived from the same authorisation-filtered data as the renderer, subject to the same RBAC, masking and confirmation controls, and never gated by `aria-hidden`. This constrains every future feature that draws to a canvas.

Second, the **evidence model**: conformance is asserted from a queryable result store populated by scripted, automated, manual and exploratory sources, with a single screen inventory driving scans, snapshots and guardrails. Future teams need to know that adding a screen means adding inventory entries, not just writing JSX.

`docs/plan/27-adrs/` is where such decisions live, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` plus the contribution guide are where engineers actually look.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A new ADR in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (next free number), "Accessible-surface parity and the accessibility evidence model", covering: context, the parity rule and its non-negotiable clauses, the three-layer canvas strategy as an architectural constraint on the chart engine, the single-inventory principle, the evidence model and where conformance claims come from, consequences (including the cost imposed on every new canvas surface), and alternatives considered (canvas semantics only; a screen-reader-specific alternate app; no mirror) with reasons for rejection.
- Updates to `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`: the regression pack tiering, its owner and cadence after E47 closes (cross-referenced, not duplicated, from `E47-Q08`).
- Updates to the contribution guide and design-system docs: link the new-screen onboarding recipe from `E47-Q08` and the component a11y documentation requirement from standard section 11.6.
- An **operator/owner-facing note** in the help content behind SCR-119 (Help & about): what accessibility features exist, how to reach the accessibility settings (SCR-117), the high-contrast and reduced-motion shortcuts, and where the accessibility statement lives - written for the owner and managers, not for engineers.
- A cross-reference sweep: the tracking notes in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 12 (which flag that `14-screens-catalogue.md` and `16-design-system-brief.md` did not exist when the standard was written) are resolved and the standard updated to confirm those cross-references now resolve.

## Out of scope
- Writing the accessibility statement and conformance report content - `E47-D02` designs them and `E47-T06` produces them.
- Changing the accessibility standard's requirements; this ticket records decisions and fixes stale cross-references, it does not relax anything.
- Any product code.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: E47 architectural decision and operator documentation

  Scenario: The ADR records the parity rule in binding terms
    Given the new ADR
    When an engineer designing a new canvas panel reads it
    Then they can tell that a mirror root and an aria-label are mandatory
    And that hiding a privileged control from assistive technology is not authorisation

  Scenario: Alternatives are recorded with reasons
    When the ADR is reviewed
    Then at least three rejected alternatives are described with the reason each was rejected

  Scenario: Failure case - stale cross-references are fixed, not carried forward
    Given the tracking notes in 05-accessibility-standard.md section 12
    When the sweep is performed
    Then each note is resolved and marked as verified against the now-existing document
    And any genuine gap found is filed as a ticket rather than silently closed

  Scenario: Edge case - the operator note is usable by a non-engineer
    Given the owner reading the Help and about content
    When they want to enable high contrast
    Then the note tells them the shortcut and the settings location without jargon

  Scenario: Docs are discoverable
    When an engineer starts a new screen
    Then the contribution guide points them at the onboarding recipe within one hop
```

## Technical notes / design
- The ADR follows the existing template and numbering in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`; it supersedes nothing but explicitly references the chart-engine design document, because the three-layer strategy is already a binding constraint there and the ADR makes its rationale citable.
- Keep the ADR short and decisive. Detail belongs in `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the ADR's job is to record the decision and its consequences so future debates start from the right place.
- The help content is product copy: it goes through the normal content review and is drawn from the SCR-119 design, not written ad hoc by an engineer.

## Test plan
- Documentation review by the Architect, the Accessibility role and one engineer who did not work on E47; the last of these is the real test - if they cannot follow the onboarding recipe from the contribution guide to a working screen entry, the docs fail.
- Link check across all touched documents so no cross-reference is broken.

## Security notes
- The ADR states the parity rule in its security-relevant form (same RBAC, same masking, same confirmations) so a future reader cannot mistake accessibility work for a licence to expose data.
- The operator note must not enumerate internal endpoints or architecture; it is user-facing content for an internal product and stays at the level of features and shortcuts.

## Accessibility notes
Documentation is part of conformance: the help content behind SCR-119 is itself tested against the standard, and the ADR and guides are plain markdown with proper heading structure and no colour-dependent meaning.

## Performance notes
The ADR records the measured cost of the accessibility layers from `E47-Q05` as a consequence, so future feature teams can plan for it rather than discovering it. Numbers are cited by reference to the benchmark results, not copied, to avoid becoming stale.

## Observability
No runtime observability. One process signal: the cross-reference sweep is repeated at each major docs revision, and the ADR lists the documents that must be re-checked when the accessibility standard changes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` with context, decision, consequences and at least three rejected alternatives.
- [ ] `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` updated with pack ownership and cadence by cross-reference.
- [ ] Contribution guide and design-system docs link the onboarding recipe and the component a11y documentation requirement.
- [ ] SCR-119 help content updated and reviewed as product copy.
- [ ] Section 12 tracking notes in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` resolved; any genuine gap filed as a ticket.
- [ ] Link check clean; reviewed by the Architect, the Accessibility role and an engineer new to E47.

## Dependencies
- `E47-X01` - the parity rule's security framing comes from the threat model.
- `E47-Q08` - the onboarding recipe and pack ownership must exist to be linked.

## Branch
`chore/e47-adr-and-docs` (docs-only).

title: E47 QA sign-off: conformance evidence rollup and R5 GA a11y gate input
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 9.3 makes accessibility an explicit R5 exit criterion and section 9.4 lists "A11y" as a quality gate; `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` requires a production-readiness review before release. Someone has to stand behind a single statement: *CandleViewer meets WCAG 2.2 AA, here is the evidence, and here are the known gaps*.

By this sprint the evidence exists but is scattered: scripted plan results (`E47-Q01`), manual AT passes (`E47-Q02`), automated gate history (`E47-Q03`, `E47-Q04`), motion and overhead measurements (`E47-Q05`), chaos results (`E47-Q06`), exploratory findings (`E47-Q07`), the regression pack dry run (`E47-Q08`), and the design-QA ledger (`E47-D03`). This ticket consolidates them into the QA verdict that the conformance report (`E47-T06`) publishes and that the PRR consumes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **sign-off record** (`qa/signoff/e47-accessibility-signoff.md`) containing:
  1. Coverage statement: every screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` and every WCAG 2.2 AA success criterion, each marked conformant / partially conformant / not conformant / not applicable, with the evidence artefact cited for each.
  2. Defect position: open a11y defects by severity and screen, with the burn-down trend from `E47-Q04`; zero open P0 is a hard precondition for unconditional sign-off.
  3. Known gaps and owner-approved exceptions: each with its compensating control, reason, approving owner and the ticket tracking its removal - the essential-exception target-size cases from standard section 3.4.7 in particular.
  4. AT matrix result: NVDA / JAWS / VoiceOver verdicts with the pinned versions actually used and any drift from standard section 8.1.
  5. Measured results: flash rates, accommodation frame overhead, table-alternative scroll cost, announcement throttling at each load level.
  6. Regression posture: what runs per PR, nightly and per RC after E47 closes, who owns it, and the measured RC duration.
- A **PRR input package** in the form required by `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`, with a clear go / go-with-conditions / no-go recommendation from the SDET and the Accessibility role.
- A **residual-risk register entry** for `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` covering anything shipping non-conformant, with severity, affected users and mitigation.
- A short handover to `E49` naming the top three accessibility risks for polish work.

## Out of scope
- Writing the public conformance report / VPAT - `E47-T06` consumes this record and publishes it.
- Fixing defects; sign-off may be refused, which is the correct output if defects remain.
- Sign-off for epics other than E47, though the coverage statement necessarily spans screens those epics built.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: E47 QA sign-off

  Scenario: Every claim is backed by a cited artefact
    Given the sign-off record
    When any conformance claim is inspected
    Then it cites a specific test result, transcript, scan report or ledger row
    And a claim with no citation blocks the sign-off

  Scenario: Zero open P0 accessibility defects
    Given the defect list at sign-off time
    When any P0 remains open
    Then the recommendation is no-go or go-with-conditions naming that defect
    And sign-off is not recorded as unconditional

  Scenario: Failure case - an untestable screen is not silently claimed conformant
    Given a screen that could not be reached in the test harness
    When the coverage statement is produced
    Then that screen is marked not assessed with the reason
    And it is never reported as conformant by omission

  Scenario: Edge case - AT version drift is disclosed
    Given the manual passes ran on a newer NVDA than the pinned version
    When the AT matrix result is written
    Then the actual versions are recorded and the drift is disclosed
    And the standard's version-pinning changelog is updated

  Scenario: PRR receives a decision, not a data dump
    When the PRR convenes
    Then the package contains an explicit recommendation with conditions
    And the residual-risk register entry exists for every non-conformant item
```

## Technical notes / design
- The coverage statement is generated from the QA result store by query (tags `epic:E47`, `criterion:*`, `screen:*`) rather than compiled by hand; hand-compiled matrices are stale by the time they are reviewed. The generation script is committed with the record.
- "Partially conformant" must state precisely which part fails and for whom - a vague partial claim is the failure mode that makes VPAT-shaped documents worthless.
- Sign-off is a joint signature: SDET (evidence quality) and the Accessibility role (judgement), per standard section 8.3. Neither signs alone.
- The record is versioned: if a condition is later cleared, a dated amendment is appended rather than the original edited, so the release history remains auditable.

## Test plan
- Verification is an evidence audit: a reviewer independent of E47 picks five random conformance claims and follows each citation to the underlying artefact. Any claim that cannot be traced within five minutes is rejected and the record corrected before sign-off.
- Re-run the generation script twice to confirm the coverage statement is reproducible from the store.

## Security notes
- The package aggregates evidence that may include DOM snippets, transcripts and screenshots; it cites artefacts by reference rather than embedding raw captures, and any embedded sample is the redacted version.
- It is stored with the release record under existing access controls; it is an internal document for an internal, Tailscale-only product and is not published externally without the owner's decision.
- Known-gap disclosure must not double as an attack map: gaps are described in user-impact terms, not as exploitable implementation details.

## Accessibility notes
The record is written to the same standard it certifies: heading structure, tables with headers, verdicts as words rather than colours, and plain-language descriptions of each gap so a non-specialist reviewer at the PRR understands the user impact without decoding criterion numbers.

## Performance notes
The measured accommodation overhead from `E47-Q05` is reported as a first-class result, not a footnote: if using the product with a screen reader costs materially more frame time, that number belongs in the sign-off so the decision to ship is made with it in view.

## Observability
- The sign-off verdict is recorded as a release artefact and as a dashboard tile (date, verdict, conditions, open P0 count).
- Conditions attached to a go-with-conditions verdict are tracked as tickets with due dates; an overdue condition alerts the Accessibility role and the owner.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Sign-off record merged with all six sections, generated coverage statement and committed generation script.
- [ ] Evidence audit of five random claims passed by an independent reviewer.
- [ ] Zero open P0 a11y defects, or an explicit go-with-conditions/no-go recommendation naming them.
- [ ] Residual-risk entries added to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- [ ] PRR package delivered per `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`; verdict recorded.
- [ ] Handover to `E49` naming the top three residual accessibility risks.
- [ ] Signed jointly by the SDET and the Accessibility role.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q02`, `E47-Q04`, `E47-Q05`, `E47-Q06`, `E47-Q07`, `E47-Q08` - all evidence streams.
- `E47-D03` - the design-QA ledger is one of the cited artefacts.

`chore/e47-a11y-signoff` (docs and script only).

title: Screen-reader scripts and pinned-matrix sign-off passes (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver)
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 names "screen-reader scripts for the chart data cursor, footprint inspection, DOM ladder and both rule editors" as an E47 deliverable, and §9.3 exit criterion 2 requires a "manual screen-reader pass signed off" per screen. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1 pins the matrix: NVDA on Electron/Windows is P0 and a release blocker; JAWS is P1 and must fully pass before R4 with smoke checks thereafter; VoiceOver on macOS is P1 with a **full pass required before R5 GA**. §8.1 also requires pinned versions with a dated changelog rather than floating "latest".

Remediation (S01–S03, S05–S08) has landed by now; this Task is the evidence-producing pass that GA is judged on, plus the durable scripts that make it repeatable after GA — which matters because the standard's §8 cadence continues past this release, and R10 key-person risk means the procedure must not live only in one person's head.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Author the **task scripts** as durable, versioned documents: chart data cursor (traverse bars, read OHLCV/delta, open and read SCR-045), footprint inspection (navigate cells, read bid/ask/delta/imbalance), DOM ladder (navigate rows, read depth, place and cancel a demo order), rule form editor (author, validate, save) and rule node editor (author, connect, arm/disarm), plus the §8.2 cross-cutting script (login and 2FA, switch symbol, toggle table view, trigger reduced-motion override, read a fill notification).
- Each script states: preconditions and fixture, ordered steps, the expected *announcement content* at each step (not merely "it announces something"), and a pass/fail line per step.
- Execute the full pass on the pinned matrix: NVDA (P0, full), JAWS (P1, full), VoiceOver (P1, full before GA), each against the production Electron build; record results per screen band with evidence per the K01-decided capture procedure.
- Record the pinned versions with a dated changelog entry per §8.1 and file the quarterly re-pin as a recurring Chore.
- Any failure found becomes a register finding routed to the owning remediation Story if fixable in R5, or to the exception register with Owner acceptance if not.
- Sign-off: Accessibility role signs the full passes; QA/SDET co-signs the RC checklist.

## Out of scope
- Remediating what the passes find — routed back to S01–S08 or to E49; this Task owns detection and evidence.
- Mobile/Android screen readers and Safari (excluded by §8.1).
- Automated SR emulation — these are human passes by design.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Scripts are executable by someone who did not write them
  Given a QA engineer who has not used the app with a screen reader
  When they follow a script
  Then every step is unambiguous and the expected announcement content is stated
  And they can produce a pass or fail per step without asking the author

Scenario: The pinned matrix is fully executed before GA
  When the GA gate is evaluated
  Then NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver full passes are recorded against the production Electron build
  And each is signed off by the Accessibility role with a date and the pinned tool versions

Scenario: A failure is not absorbed silently
  Given a script step fails on JAWS only
  Then a register finding is created naming the screen reader, step and expected announcement
  And it is either fixed in R5 or accepted as an expiring exception with a compensating control

Scenario: Versions are pinned and dated
  Then the matrix records exact screen-reader and shell versions with a dated changelog entry
  And a recurring re-pin Chore exists for the next quarter

Scenario: A trading task is completable non-visually
  Given the DOM ladder script on the demo environment
  Then a demo order is placed and cancelled using keyboard and screen reader alone
  And the confirmation read-back states side, price, quantity and account before commit
```

## Technical notes / design
The scripts specify expected *content*, which is what turns a subjective pass into a reproducible one — "announces the focused bar's time, open, high, low, close, volume and delta in one utterance" is checkable; "is accessible" is not. Scripts live in the repo beside the standard so they version with the product, and they are the same scripts the post-GA cadence in §8.1 re-runs.

## Test plan
This Task *is* a test plan; its own quality control is that each script is dry-run by a second person before the formal pass, and that the formal pass is executed on a clean production build rather than a dev server.

## Security notes
Passes run in the demo environment with synthetic accounts; the DOM ladder script places demo orders only and must never be executed against Live. Captured speech recordings and screenshots are reviewed for account identifiers and key material before being stored as evidence.

## Accessibility notes
This is the human half of conformance that automation cannot replace: announcement usefulness, focus intent, and whether the mirror actually corresponds to what is drawn. Deferred SR spot-checks from earlier Stories are discharged here and their deferral notes closed.

## Performance notes
During the passes, note any perceptible lag between a keyboard action and its announcement; anything above roughly 200 ms is logged as an E46 candidate rather than tolerated.

## Observability
Results recorded in the findings register and the conformance matrix; pass/fail counts per screen reader published with the RC report.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five surface scripts plus the cross-cutting script authored, dry-run and merged.
- [ ] NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver full passes executed on the production Electron build and signed off.
- [ ] Pinned versions recorded with a dated changelog; re-pin Chore filed.
- [ ] All failures routed to remediation or to registered exceptions.
- [ ] Earlier Stories' deferred SR spot-checks closed.
- [ ] `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8 updated with the executed cadence and results location.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-K01** (harness and capture procedure), **E47-S01**, **E47-S02**, **E47-S03** (the surfaces must be remediated before a sign-off pass is meaningful). Blocks **E47-T05**.

title: Publish the VPAT-shaped conformance report and the exception register
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 closes E47's scope with "a published accessibility conformance report (VPAT-shaped)", and §9.3 exit criterion 2 requires that "any non-conformance is a documented, Owner-accepted exception with a remediation ticket". §9.3 criterion 4 adds the discipline that every accepted risk must have "a current owner, an expiry date, and a review record; expired acceptances are re-decided, not silently extended".

This Task produces the artefact the GA gate reads. It is deliberately *generated* from the findings register and the T03 matrix rather than written by hand, so it can be regenerated after any post-GA change without a re-transcription that quietly drifts from reality.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The **conformance report**, VPAT-shaped: one row per WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA success criterion, with a conformance level (Supports / Partially Supports / Does Not Support / Not Applicable) and remarks naming the surfaces involved — generated from the register, the contrast/CVD matrix and the SR pass results.
- A **per-screen conformance matrix** appendix covering SCR-001…SCR-159 with the four evidence columns (axe, keyboard, screen reader, sign-off).
- The **exception register**: every non-conformance with WCAG SC, level, affected surfaces, compensating control, named Owner acceptance, expiry date and linked remediation ticket. Level A entries are prohibited — a Level A entry fails the build that generates the report.
- The **in-app accessibility statement**, linked from **SCR-117** and **SCR-119**, in plain language: what is supported, what is known-limited, the keyboard and table alternatives, and how to report a problem.
- Documented regeneration: a single command, run in CI on the release candidate, that fails if the checked-in report is stale relative to the register.
- Handover: the remaining open findings and their owners handed to **E49** for burn-down, and the post-GA §8.1 cadence recorded in the ops documentation for **E48**.

## Out of scope
- Any remediation — everything fixable in R5 is already in S01–S08.
- A third-party audit or a legally-filed VPAT (this is an internal tool; §1 of the standard states there is no external AA mandate).
- Marketing or external publication of the report.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The report is generated, not transcribed
  When the generation command runs against the findings register and the contrast matrix
  Then the report and the per-screen appendix are produced without manual editing
  And CI fails if the checked-in report differs from the generated one

Scenario: Every A and AA criterion is addressed
  Then each WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA success criterion has a conformance level and a remark
  And no criterion is left blank or marked "unknown"

Scenario: A Level A gap blocks GA
  Given a Level A finding remains open
  When the report is generated
  Then generation fails naming the finding, and the GA gate cannot be satisfied

Scenario: An AA exception is complete or it is not an exception
  Given an entry in the exception register
  Then it has a success criterion, affected surfaces, a compensating control, a named Owner acceptance, an expiry date and a remediation ticket
  And an entry missing any field fails generation

Scenario: Users can find the statement
  Given a user on SCR-117 or SCR-119
  Then the accessibility statement is reachable in one action and states the supported keyboard and table alternatives and how to report a problem

Scenario: Expiry is enforced, not aspirational
  Given an exception's expiry date passes
  Then the next generation flags it for re-decision rather than carrying it forward
```

## Technical notes / design
Generation-not-transcription is the whole design point. The register (schema from K01), the T03 matrix and the T04 pass results are three machine-readable inputs; the report is their join. The staleness check is what keeps the artefact honest after GA, when nobody is watching the register daily. Expiry enforcement is a date comparison at generation time, which converts §9.3 criterion 4 from a policy into a mechanism.

## Test plan
Unit: generator joins and the four failure modes (Level A open, incomplete exception, stale checked-in report, expired acceptance). Fixture: a synthetic register producing a known report. Review: Accessibility role, QA lead and Owner read the generated report before GA; a non-specialist reads the in-app statement for plain-language clarity.

## Security notes
The report and statement must contain no hostnames, account identifiers, API-key material or screenshots with live data — an automated content check runs before publication. The exception register describes *accessibility* gaps only; it must not become a place where security findings are recorded (those belong to the E43 process).

## Accessibility notes
The report and the in-app statement must themselves conform: semantic headings, real tables with headers, no colour-only conformance indicators ("Supports" as a word, not a green dot), and readable at 200% zoom. Publishing an inaccessible accessibility report would be the most avoidable defect in the Epic.

## Performance notes
Generation runs in under 30 s so the staleness check is affordable on every release-candidate build.

## Observability
Published metrics alongside the report: open findings by level, exception count and nearest expiry date, per-screen evidence completeness — the same numbers the PRR reads.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report, per-screen appendix and exception register generated, reviewed and merged.
- [ ] Generation command documented and the staleness check wired into the RC build.
- [ ] Zero open Level A findings; every AA exception complete with Owner acceptance and expiry.
- [ ] In-app accessibility statement linked from SCR-117 and SCR-119 and verified conformant itself.
- [ ] Remaining findings handed to **E49**; post-GA SR cadence documented for **E48**.
- [ ] Owner acceptance recorded; report attached to the GA PRR.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T04** (SR evidence), **E47-S04**, **E47-S05**, **E47-S06**, **E47-S08** (remediation complete). Consumes **E47-T01** and **E47-T03** outputs. Feeds **E48** (documentation) and **E49** (burn-down), and satisfies `30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 exit criterion 2.

## Branch
`docs/e47-conformance-report`

## References
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2, §9.3, §9.4; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §1, §8, §9, §10; `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-117, SCR-119; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Agent execution brief

1. docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md (PRR/runbook procedures)
2. docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md (R5 exit criteria)
3. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md (DoR/DoD)

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint  # docs-site link/markdown checks`
- `make gen && git diff --exit-code  # if generated reference docs touched`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `docs/e47-conformance-report`
- PR title: "E47-T05: Publish the VPAT-shaped conformance report and the exception register"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-T05>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/docs/plan/` (@CandleViewer/architecture); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/docs, area/design-system, priority/p1, a11y, qa

- Report, per-screen appendix and exception register generated, reviewed and merged.
- Generation command documented and the staleness check wired into the RC build.
- Zero open Level A findings; every AA exception complete with Owner acceptance and expiry.
- In-app accessibility statement linked from SCR-117 and SCR-119 and verified conformant itself.
- Remaining findings handed to **E49**; post-GA SR cadence documented for **E48**.
- Owner acceptance recorded; report attached to the GA PRR.

**Do NOT**
- Any remediation — everything fixable in R5 is already in S01–S08.
- A third-party audit or a legally-filed VPAT (this is an internal tool; §1 of the standard states there is no external AA mandate).
- Marketing or external publication of the report.

title: Security review and sign-off for the E47 accessibility surface
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a security review and explicit sign-off per epic before its work is considered complete, and `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` makes that sign-off a PRR input. For E47 the review question is narrow and answerable: **did making the product accessible weaken any control, and did any accessibility mitigation get implemented in a way that harms accessibility?**

This is also the point at which the epic's published artefacts get a security read: the accessibility statement and conformance report (`E47-D02`, `E47-T06`) describe system behaviour in detail and, for an internal Tailscale-only product, need a decision about what is disclosed and to whom.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **white-box security review** of the E47 implementation diff: the DOM mirror layer, live-region infrastructure, table alternatives, theme/token switching, preference and hotkey persistence, keyboard-only mode, and the statement/report pages. Review checklist supplied by `E47-X01`.
- Verification that every `E47-X01` finding has been mitigated or formally accepted, and that every `E47-X02` confirmed issue is closed with a regression assertion in place.
- Verification of the two standing rules from `E47-X01`: the accessible surface is subject to the same RBAC and data scoping as the visual surface; and no accommodation removes a confirmation, arming step or Demo/Live signal.
- **Audit-coverage check**: preference changes that weaken a safety control, hotkey-profile activation, and keyboard-only mode changes emit audit events with the specified fields and appear on SCR-135/SCR-136.
- **Disclosure review** of the accessibility statement and conformance report: no internal hostnames, no architecture detail beyond what is needed, no screenshots with real account data, no known-gap description that reads as an exploitation recipe. Produce a publish/do-not-publish recommendation for the owner.
- A **sign-off record** (`docs/security/signoff/e47.md`): scope reviewed, method, findings and dispositions, residual risks with owners, and an explicit go / go-with-conditions / no-go for the accessibility surface, signed by the Security engineer.
- Residual-risk entries appended to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` and handed to `E47-Q09` for the QA rollup.

## Out of scope
- Re-running the abuse cases in full (`E47-X02` owns execution; this review verifies closure and spot-checks).
- Penetration testing - the pre-R4 pen test covers the product broadly; this review is E47-specific.
- Security review of features other than the accessibility surface those features expose.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: E47 security review and sign-off

  Scenario: Every prior finding is accounted for
    Given the findings from E47-X01 and E47-X02
    When the review is conducted
    Then each finding is verified as mitigated, or formally accepted with a named approver and rationale
    And no finding is left in an ambiguous state

  Scenario: Parity rules are verified, not assumed
    Given the accessible surface of an aggregating screen
    When the reviewer spot-checks with a restricted-role session
    Then data scoping matches the visual surface exactly
    And a mismatch blocks sign-off

  Scenario: Failure case - a mitigation degraded accessibility
    Given a fix that added aria-hidden to a control the user is allowed to operate
    When the review examines it
    Then the fix is rejected
    And a corrected approach is required before sign-off

  Scenario: Edge case - audit coverage gap
    Given a preference change that weakens a destructive-action confirmation
    When the audit log is inspected on SCR-135
    And no event is recorded
    Then sign-off is go-with-conditions at best, naming the gap

  Scenario: Disclosure decision is explicit
    When the statement and conformance report are reviewed
    Then a publish or do-not-publish recommendation is recorded with reasons
    And any required redaction is listed for E47-T06 to apply
```

## Technical notes / design
- The review is white-box: reviewers read the diff, not only the running app. The mirror-construction and live-region code paths are the priority because they are where authorisation-filtered data is re-expressed.
- Spot-checks are performed with real restricted-role sessions rather than by reasoning about the code, because role behaviour in a dynamic UI is easy to get wrong in review and easy to see in practice.
- Acceptance of a residual risk requires the owner's approval where it affects trading safety; the Security engineer cannot unilaterally accept a weakened safety control, consistent with the security program's escalation rules.
- The disclosure review applies the principle that the statement describes *user-facing behaviour and known gaps in user-impact terms*, not implementation internals.

## Test plan
- Method is documented and reproducible: the checklist, the diff range reviewed, the role sessions used and the spot-checks performed are recorded so a later reviewer can repeat the work.
- Two spot-checks are re-performed independently by a second reviewer to confirm the review is not rubber-stamping; disagreements are resolved before sign-off.

## Security notes
This ticket is the epic's security gate. The strongest failure mode to guard against is optimism: accessibility work is visibly virtuous and reviewers are inclined to wave it through. The review explicitly requires evidence for each parity claim rather than assurances from the implementing team, mirroring the evidence-audit approach `E47-Q09` uses on the QA side.

## Accessibility notes
The review has a dual mandate: no control weakened, and no accessibility degraded by a security fix. Both are recorded; a sign-off that achieved security by removing accessible access to a legitimate control is a failed review and must be reported as such to the Accessibility role and the CDO.

## Performance notes
The review confirms that the DoS mitigations identified in `E47-X01` (announcement coalescing, mirror windowing, table range caps) are actually implemented and configured with limits the measurements in `E47-Q05` support, rather than with arbitrary numbers.

## Observability
- Sign-off verdict and conditions recorded in the security findings register and surfaced on the release dashboard.
- Conditions become tickets with due dates; overdue conditions alert the Security engineer and the owner.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] White-box review completed over the E47 diff with the method and diff range recorded.
- [ ] Every `E47-X01` and `E47-X02` finding verified closed or formally accepted with an approver.
- [ ] Parity rules and audit coverage verified with restricted-role sessions; two spot-checks independently repeated.
- [ ] Disclosure recommendation recorded for the statement and conformance report, with any redactions listed for `E47-T06`.
- [ ] Sign-off record merged with an explicit verdict; residual risks added to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- [ ] Result handed to `E47-Q09` and the R5 PRR.

## Dependencies
- `E47-X02`, `E47-X03` - findings and automated guards must exist to be verified.
- `E47-S04` - the final remediation slice must be merged or the review is reviewing a moving target.

## Branch
`chore/e47-security-signoff` (docs-only).

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (review and sign-off requirement, escalation, findings register).
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (PRR inputs).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 6.1-6.3, 8.3, 11.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-117, SCR-119, SCR-135, SCR-136, SCR-149.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` (residual-risk entries).
- `docs/plan/33-raci.md` (who signs what).

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e47-security-signoff`
- PR title: "E47-X04: Security review and sign-off for the E47 accessibility surface"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-X04>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/security, area/design-system, priority/p1, security, a11y

**Done means**
- White-box review completed over the E47 diff with the method and diff range recorded.
- Every `E47-X01` and `E47-X02` finding verified closed or formally accepted with an approver.
- Parity rules and audit coverage verified with restricted-role sessions; two spot-checks independently repeated.
- Disclosure recommendation recorded for the statement and conformance report, with any redactions listed for `E47-T06`.
- Sign-off record merged with an explicit verdict; residual risks added to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- Result handed to `E47-Q09` and the R5 PRR.

**Do NOT**
- Re-running the abuse cases in full (`E47-X02` owns execution; this review verifies closure and spot-checks).
- Penetration testing - the pre-R4 pen test covers the product broadly; this review is E47-specific.
- Security review of features other than the accessibility surface those features expose.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-X04` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.
